decisionReuse.intro: The ContextGraphDecision (KRD §119.2) is the deterministic reuse gate: it decides whether a PAST decision may be REUSED for a new request, by checking EXACTLY four declared dimensions — time / scope / authority / conditions — and emitting {may_reuse, reason, checked, required_human_review}. The verdict is FALSE-DOMINANT: any failing check blocks reuse. "The LLM does not live in the ContextGraph" — the graph permits or blocks, agents propose, the Execution Layer acts.
decisionReuse.tutorialHeading: How to read and drive this screen
decisionReuse.tutorialBody: Each row is a reuse candidate (a past decision + the request judging it). Click DECIDE: the pure gate runs with a fixed `now` (never the browser clock) and renders an ALLOW (green) or BLOCK (red) badge, the four dimension chips (each ✓ passed or ✗ blocking), the human-readable reason, and a "human review required" flag when the authority no longer holds. An EXPIRED candidate ⇒ BLOCK with the time chip lit; an OUT-OF-SCOPE candidate ⇒ BLOCK with the scope chip lit.
decisionReuse.exampleBody: An EU decision expired on 2026-01-01, judged on 2026-05-30 ⇒ BLOCK (time dimension). The same EU decision judged for a US request ⇒ BLOCK (scope dimension, no_reuse_outside_scope: a decision reused outside its scope is a structural hallucination). Whereas an EU decision still valid, judged for an EU request whose domain is governed by the same authority ⇒ ALLOW.
decisionReuse.footer: Read-only against truth. The context schema is above the waterline (the agent reads SELECT-only); a decision is recorded by the aidos role via a ChangeSet (S20), never this screen and never an LLM — the LLM does not live in the ContextGraph.
decisionReuse.verdictPending: Click DECIDE to run the reuse gate.

contextPack.title: ContextPack
contextPack.subtitle: the minimal context compiled from the red-set
contextPack.intro: The ContextRouter (KRD §144) is an ALGORITHM, not a prompt and not a RAG. It compiles, from a goal's red-set (S22, never recomputed), the MINIMAL ContextPack (KRD §143) — only the load-bearing kernel, the red mirrors that define the stop condition, the contracts that CROSS a bounded-context boundary, and the scoped memory (confidence ≥ repeated). "Too much context destroys context" (§141): overload makes the agent invent. The pack is branch-aware and content-addressed (same goal + branch + graph ⇒ identical pack).
contextPack.tutorialHeading: How to read & drive this screen
contextPack.tutorialBody: Pick the branch then click COMPILE: the pure router runs (never an LLM) and renders the compiled ContextPack. The INCLUDED panel shows the affected layers (exactly the red-set), the active kernel (red mirrors + crossed contracts), the scoped memory (lessons + recent incidents), skills/tools, the stop condition and the pack hash. The EXCLUDED panel shows every dropped node with its WHY (cross-BC, stale, out-of-scope, cosmetic-below-threshold). The BOUNDARIES strip shows the allowed paths and the forbidden /kernel/** /mirror/** (the wall). Switch branches: a node from another branch never leaks.
contextPack.exampleBody: The checkout-apply-promo goal on main: the pack INCLUDES the checkout subgraph (view:cart, control:promo-field, operation:applyPromo), its red mirrors (promo-field.fixture, applyPromo.workflow) and the crossed PUBLIC contract PaymentGateway@hash. It EXCLUDES billing:invoice-internals (cross-BC), the internal contract billing-internal@hash (cross-BC), the stale old-promo-rule (stale) and refund-window (out-of-scope: billing). A checkout goal does NOT receive billing internals; stale memory is excluded.
contextPack.footer: Read-only against truth. The router READS the ContextGraph view; the pack it emits ALWAYS forbids /kernel/** and /mirror/** (the wall); a truth write goes via propose → ChangeSet → approval, never this screen and never an LLM — the ContextRouter is an algorithm.
contextPack.pending: Click COMPILE to run the ContextRouter.

emittedTarget.heading: Target of the EMITTED app — Hono + functional TypeScript
emittedTarget.intro: EL00 (ADR 0040) engraves the target of the app AIDOS EMITS: Hono front+back, pure-functional TypeScript, its own MCP + Skills, a Postgres-dialect datastore via a TS client, and the Operation-DSL run by a callback to a Go interpreter service. The constructrice≠construite frontier is trenched: AIDOS stays governable Go — never rewritten in TS, never emits Go for the user app. EL00 is ADR-only: it writes no truth. The “Verify parity” button replays the pure verdict — the declared target ≡ the arch-fitness config FN04/S84 enforces.
emittedTarget.wall: The wall (CLAUDE.md §2): EL00 is ADR-only, above the line — this screen reads a decision and computes a deterministic verdict; it writes NO truth. Promotion to truth stays the mirror write via /goal.
emittedTarget.parityOk: Parity green — declared target ≡ enforced config

emitters.heading: Emitters — one deterministic projection per kind × target
emitters.intro: An AIDOS emitter is a DETERMINISTIC generator, one per kind × target (kind = entity; target ∈ {go-sqlc, pg-ddl, ts-types}). It READS an entity AST from the kernel (a prior truth, S02) and EMITS a projection: Go structs (via sqlc), Postgres DDL, TS types — ONE source, N projections, never double-typed. The contract is determinism: the SAME source gives BYTE-IDENTICAL output. Each artifact carries its source content-hash and a protected header “CODE GENERATED BY AIDOS — DO NOT EDIT”; gen/ is never hand-edited. Staleness is COMPUTED (source_hash ≠ the entity's current head): it feeds the red wave (S22), it is never hunted. Read-only (the wall): the emitter reads the AST, it never writes it.
emitters.tutorialHeading: Tutorial — how to read this panel
emitters.tutorialStep1: 1. Pick an entity (Order or Thin): that is the source AST, read from the kernel.
emitters.tutorialStep2: 2. Read the three projection cards (go-sqlc · pg-ddl · ts-types): each carries its source_hash, its output_hash and the protected-header preview.
emitters.tutorialStep3: 3. Click RE-EMIT: the emitter recomputes the bytes; the output_hash is IDENTICAL (byte-identical — the “done” criterion made visible).
emitters.tutorialStep4: 4. Move the entity head (REMOVE discount): the prior artifact stays listed (append-only ledger) but flips to STALE — its source_hash no longer matches the new head.
emitters.exampleBody: Order (id, total, discount) emits three projections: a Go struct (Discount/Id/Total), a Postgres table (discount/id/total), and a TS interface (discount/id/total) — the three agree on the SAME field set (no inter-target drift). Thin (id only) emits ONLY the pinned field: no invented column.
emitters.wallNote: Read-only (the wall): the emitter READS the entity AST (SELECT-only on kernel) and WRITES only projections below the line (back/gen/, front/web/gen/). No truth is written here. The runtime.generated_artifacts ledger is written by the aidos role, never the agent.
emitters.archFitnessOk: Compliant: no mutable global, no init(), acyclic call graph
emitters.callGraphNodes: Nodes (function → callees) — the Understand-Anything index supplied to the agent as context
emitters.callGraphAffectedLabel: Sub-graph affected by a change to the first function (consumed by the ContextRouter S33)
emitters.callGraphEmpty: Empty index: out of scope or unparseable emitted code (fail-closed)
emitters.graphVizHeading: Functional graph of the emitted app (FN06)
emitters.graphVizIntro: The EMITTED code (the user's app, not AIDOS's own Go) in functional style: each function is a node, each call an edge (the Understand-Anything view). The layout is a PURE function of the index (same graph → same drawing, never an LLM judgement). Click to visualise, then to highlight the sub-graph affected by a change to the first function — exactly what the ContextRouter (S33) would reload.
emitters.graphVizEmpty: Empty graph: out of scope or unparseable emitted code (fail-closed)

entityMap.title: Entity source — one source, three projections
entityMap.intro: An ENTITY (KRD §23) is a SOURCE layer, human, above the waterline: the data model, living as an AST in Postgres (kernel, content-addressed, append-only). From that SINGLE source flow three deterministic PROJECTIONS — a Go struct (sqlc), a TypeScript type, the Postgres DDL — never double-typed. Attribute order is preserved; identifier → PRIMARY KEY; required → NOT NULL / non-optional; a non-required attribute → NULLABLE / optional. Read-only (the wall): the agent READS the entity (SELECT-only), it never writes it; gen/ is never hand-edited.
entityMap.tutorialTitle: Tutorial — how to read this panel
entityMap.tutorialStep1: On the left: the Order source — its ordered attributes, each with its type, its required/optional badge, and the identifier badge (the primary key).
entityMap.tutorialStep2: On the right: the three derived projections (Go struct · TS type · DDL). Each carries its source_hash, its output_hash and the protected-header preview “CODE GENERATED BY AIDOS — DO NOT EDIT”.
entityMap.tutorialStep3: Click RE-EMIT: the emitter recomputes the bytes; the output_hash is IDENTICAL (byte-identical — the “done” criterion made visible).
entityMap.tutorialStep4: Click MOVE THE HEAD (remove discount): the entity head advances (append-only); artifacts emitted from the old head flip to STALE — their source_hash no longer matches the new head (the staleness inequality feeds the red wave, S22).

apiProjection.title: API projection — a REST/JSON handler projected from an operation + entity
apiProjection.intro: An API HANDLER (KRD §23) is a PROJECTION, below the line, derived, disposable: it EXPOSES a kernel OPERATION (the N2 workflow, S10) over HTTP, and its request/response body REUSES the field shapes of the ENTITY it touches (the N3 source, S35) — never re-typed. The handler is a THIN transport adapter: JSON in → the operation interpreter (S10) → JSON out; it never re-implements the business rule. Its method + route come FROM the operation (createOrder → POST /orders), never invented. The request/response shape is frozen as a PACT CONTRACT (the “Pact between cells” slot) and VERIFIED by the pact-verifier MCP (provider verification, N5). Read-only (the wall): back/gen/api is never hand-edited; a contract is written via propose → ChangeSet → approval.
apiProjection.tutorialTitle: Tutorial — how to read this panel
apiProjection.tutorialStep1: Left: the createOrder operation (its input, verbs, emitted events) and the Order entity it mutates — the two SOURCES the handler is projected from.
apiProjection.tutorialStep2: Center: the emitted Go handler (read-only, with the protected header “CODE GENERATED BY AIDOS — DO NOT EDIT” + its source_hash), its method + route (POST /orders), and the request/response JSON shapes (the Order shape reused, never re-typed).
apiProjection.tutorialStep3: Right: the Pact contract (the consumer expectation) and the PASS/FAIL badge from the last pact-verifier run — “the createOrder route passes its contract test” made visible.
apiProjection.tutorialStep4: Click RE-EMIT (the output_hash is byte-identical — determinism made visible) then VERIFY CONTRACT (the provider is stood up in-process, the POST /orders request replayed, status + field set asserted against the contract → PASS).
apiProjection.passBadge: PASS — the createOrder route passes its contract test
apiProjection.failBadge: FAIL — the provider does not honour the contract

dbProjection.title: DB projection — the expand-contract migration projected from the entity + DataTruthScope
dbProjection.intro: The DB MIGRATION (KRD line 532) is a PROJECTION of the ENTITY, below the line, derived, disposable: emitted from the entity AST (S35, never hand-edited), it brings the schema to the new head in an EXPAND-CONTRACT / forward-only shape. A column add is an additive EXPAND step (ADD COLUMN, never an in-place rewrite); a narrowing change (drop / narrow) is split EXPAND → BACKFILL → CONTRACT, never a single silent destructive step. DataTruthScope (§44.3) explicitly declares what the new truth does to HISTORICAL DATA: "changing the truth of the code does not automatically change the truth of data already produced". A change touching existing/historical records REQUIRES a declared migration (required:true, a strategy in the closed set, preserve_old_truth:true); a new-records-only change does not. Read-only (the wall): back/gen/db is never hand-edited; a DataTruthScope is written via propose → ChangeSet → approval.
dbProjection.tutorialTitle: Tutorial — how to read this panel
dbProjection.tutorialStep1: On the left: the Atlas migration EMITTED from the Order entity (read-only, protected header "CODE GENERATED BY AIDOS — DO NOT EDIT" + its source_hash), marked "derived projection". The badge shows the shape: EXPAND (additive) or EXPAND→CONTRACT (narrowing).
dbProjection.tutorialStep2: Toggle between the ADDITIVE scenario (+ coupon → ADD COLUMN, an expand step) and the NARROWING scenario (drop discount → split EXPAND → BACKFILL → CONTRACT, forward-only).
dbProjection.tutorialStep3: Click RE-EMIT (the migration is byte-identical — determinism made visible) then DRY-RUN (the migration applies on the ephemeral Testcontainers engine — proven green on the Go side → DRY-RUN VALID).
dbProjection.tutorialStep4: On the right: pick a change descriptor and read the §44.3 verdict — REQUIRES MIGRATION (historical impact with no declared scope, with the HISTORICAL_IMPACT_REQUIRES_MIGRATION reason), ALLOWED (migration declared), or "no migration needed" (new-records-only).
dbProjection.exampleTitle: Worked example — the Order entity migration
dbProjection.dryRunValid: DRY-RUN VALID — the migration applies on Postgres (Testcontainers) without data loss
dbProjection.requiresBadge: REQUIRES MIGRATION — historical impact with no declared migration (§44.3)
dbProjection.noMigrationBadge: no migration needed — new records only

webPreview.title: Web projection — a Next.js component projected from a control-spec + action-spec
webPreview.intro: The WEB PROJECTION (S38, KRD BOOK V) is a deterministic emitter, a new target (ts-next) for kind=control inside the S34 emitter set. It READS a control-spec (the button-as-a-source, S11) + the action it binds, and EMITS a Next.js component whose visible/enabled are EvalState(control, given) (S11) embedded as the control's Expr ASTs — the button is a PROJECTION of the truth, never hand-authored UI. The click DECLARES the bound operation (Plan(action, click).invoke) via data-aidos-invoke, without executing it. Same source gives a byte-identical .tsx. Read-only (the wall).
webPreview.tutorialStep1: Left: the two S11 sources (control-spec + action-spec) and the state fixture (per given: expected visible/enabled).
webPreview.tutorialStep2: Pick a fixture row: the EMITTED component (imported from _generated/, never hand-authored) renders against that given.
webPreview.tutorialStep3: The respects-fixture badge compares the live DOM to the fixture; the stale badge compares source_hash to the materialized head (feeds the red wave, S22).
webPreview.tutorialStep4: RE-EMIT proves determinism (byte-for-byte); clicking the enabled button declares the bound invoke (createOrder) — without executing the operation.
webPreview.invokeNone: no invoke declared (click the enabled button)

meta.title: Meta-meta — the harness self-test
meta.intro: At every session start, a deterministic fault injection proves the three inviolable LEVEL 3 guarantees: every sensor still fires, the wall still refuses the agent's kernel/mirrors/fitness writes, and the fitness (the definition of "passed") was not modified. The meta loop may ADD a guardrail, never REMOVE one (KRD §70). There is no level 4: the floor is deterministic fault injection, not another judge.
meta.tutorialStep1: Pick a harness scenario — the panel re-runs the self-test (a pure twin of the Go Run function) live.
meta.tutorialStep2: The three guarantees show green/red: sensors fired N/N (with the per-sensor injected fault), wall refused on kernel · mirrors · fitness, fitness unchanged (baseline vs current hash).
meta.tutorialStep3: A mutated scenario (muted sensor, breached wall, mutated fitness) turns red and surfaces the BlockReason (MUTED_SENSOR / WALL_BREACHED / FITNESS_MUTATED) with its fix path.
meta.tutorialStep4: The graven fitness baseline is rendered READ-ONLY — owned by human + reality, no loop edits it.
meta.exampleTitle: Example — re-run the self-test on a scenario
meta.baselineOwner: Owned by human + reality — no loop edits its own fitness (KRD §70).
meta.scenarioBreachedWall: Breached wall — the agent could write truth
meta.scenarioMutatedFitness: Mutated fitness — a loop edited its own fitness

mutationScore.title: Mutation score — the kernel densimeter
mutationScore.intro: Mutation testing is the densimeter of kernel tightness (KRD §19/§43/§59.8): gremlins (Go) and StrykerJS (front) mutate the code post-integration and count how many mutants the mirrors kill. The score is compared to the DECLARED threshold, read READ-ONLY from fitness (above the line). 40% blocks, 80% passes against the 0.80 bar. A surviving mutant = a hole to plug. The agent never authors the bar it is graded against (§8).
mutationScore.tutorialStep1: Pick a scenario — the panel re-runs the gate (a pure twin of the Go Gate function) live over the mutation report.
mutationScore.tutorialStep2: The gauge shows the score against the declared threshold bar (labelled "declared above the line · read-only"). Verdict is pass if score ≥ threshold, else block.
mutationScore.tutorialStep3: Below the bar, the gate blocks the stable phase and lists the surviving mutants (file · line · operator · the hole to plug).
mutationScore.tutorialStep4: With no declared threshold the gate invents no bar: it blocks with MISSING_THRESHOLD. An empty/unparsable report also blocks (UNPARSABLE_REPORT), never a silent 1.0.
mutationScore.exampleTitle: Example — re-run the gate on a scenario
mutationScore.survivingEmpty: No surviving mutant — the kernel is dense enough over the covered surface.
mutationScore.scenarioBelow: Score 40% — below the bar (blocks the phase)
mutationScore.scenarioWeakened: Weakened mirror — a mutant survives, score 75% (fault injection)
mutationScore.scenarioMissingThreshold: No declared threshold — the gate invents no bar

kernelDebt.title: Kernel debt — the rot in the truth-store
kernelDebt.intro: KernelDebt (S41) is the READ-ONLY diagnostic that names the rot accumulating in the truth-store, in exactly THREE declared kinds: orphan mirror (a mirror reflecting no live truth — a monster by the completeness law, S12), stale fixture (a fixture pinned to a version the live head has left), and surviving mutant (a mutation left alive by the S40 run, against a truth a living mirror claims to cover). /trim PROPOSES a plan: every action opens an idea, never a deletion, and requires the door idea → mirror → /goal → human approval. It detects and suggests; it deletes nothing.
kernelDebt.tutorialStep1: Pick a scenario — the panel re-runs the scan (a pure twin of the Go Scan + SuggestTrim) live over the read-only snapshot.
kernelDebt.tutorialStep2: The debt ledger groups items under ORPHAN MIRRORS, STALE FIXTURES and SURVIVING MUTANTS, each with its target, reason and severity.
kernelDebt.tutorialStep3: The trim plan shows each suggestion as a PROPOSAL: an open_idea_* action (never a deletion) and the required door idea → mirror → /goal → human approval.
kernelDebt.tutorialStep4: No 'delete' or 'apply' button: /trim suggests, it deletes nothing. Acting on a suggestion is a later goal. A clean kernel shows the 'no debt' state.
kernelDebt.exampleTitle: Example — re-run the scan on a scenario
kernelDebt.emptyDebt: No debt detected — the kernel is clean over the scanned surface.
kernelDebt.planEmpty: Empty trim plan — nothing to propose.
kernelDebt.noDeleteNote: /trim suggests, it deletes nothing: no action removes a mirror, a fixture or a truth. Acting on a proposal goes through idea → mirror → /goal → human approval.
kernelDebt.scenarioAllThree: All three kinds at once (orphan + stale + survivor)
kernelDebt.scenarioSurvivor: Surviving mutant only (consumed from the S40 run)
kernelDebt.scenarioClean: Clean kernel — no debt, empty plan

evolutionSandbox.title: Evolution Sandbox — the evolution explores, it does not govern
evolutionSandbox.intro: EvolutionSandbox (S42, KRD §66.1) is the QUARANTINE in which every /evolve run (the medium self-play + QD loop, §62 ②) executes. It may write ONLY /branches/evolution, /reports, /ideas/proposed (candidates, branches, scores, hypotheses, suggestions) and NEVER /kernel, /mirrors/above, /authority, /fitness (truths, approvals, exceptions, rights). A variant is promoted into a niche only with mirror_green ∧ out_of_sample_green ∧ authority_approval — a BINARY gate (the deterministic mirror), never a score the loop grades itself; out-of-sample, never in-sample (§87). The evolution explores, it does not govern: a promotion is a PROPOSAL the human /goal freezes.
evolutionSandbox.tutorialStep1: Open/close the /evolve run with the button — while active (ON), the sandbox confines every write; the panel re-runs the pure Confine() twin live.
evolutionSandbox.tutorialStep2: The quarantine ledger shows each write: /branches/evolution, /reports, /ideas/proposed in blue (allowed); /kernel, /fitness, /authority, /mirrors/above in RED with their SANDBOX_WRITE_ESCAPES_ZONE BlockReason and how_to_fix.
evolutionSandbox.tutorialStep3: The MAP-Elites niche grid shows one élite per niche; each candidate carries three pills — mirror_green / out_of_sample_green / authority_approval.
evolutionSandbox.tutorialStep4: A candidate is promotable only when all three pills are lit; a RED-mirror candidate is NOT promotable, whatever its score. Each promotion is a PROPOSAL: promotion to truth goes through /goal.
evolutionSandbox.proposalLabel: PROPOSAL — promotion to truth needs /goal (the sandbox proposes, it does not govern)
evolutionSandbox.notPromotableNote: A promotion is a PROPOSAL: even all three conditions freeze nothing. The freeze goes through the human /goal (mirror_green ∧ out_of_sample_green ∧ authority_approval). A red-mirror candidate is never promoted, whatever its score — the Judge is the mirror, never the score.

incidentsToIdeas.title: RealityMirror
incidentsToIdeas.subtitle: Incidents → ideas
incidentsToIdeas.intro: Reality is a sensor: a prod incident / telemetry signal becomes a DRAFT idea (provenance incident:#NNNN), handed to the idea-intake door (S27). An incident is REALITY, never a truth — no version-freeze, no mirror: it PROPOSES a mirror, it is not one. The direct Incident → Kernel edge is ALWAYS refused. "The system learned from the WORLD, not from itself."
incidentsToIdeas.tutorialHeading: How to read and drive this screen
incidentsToIdeas.tutorialBody: Each card is an observed incident: its signal (failing operation, error/budget, recurrence), its cause_sketch (a HYPOTHESIS, never a truth), its provenance incident:#NNNN and its incident_derived taint. Click "/learn": the incident becomes a DRAFT idea (the incident:#NNNN → draft idea arrow), provenance carried verbatim, the idea shown with no mirror. Click "→ Kernel": the direct edge is refused in RED (REALITY_CANNOT_DECLARE_TRUTH), no kernel write, the kernel unchanged. When the signal does not pin a layer, an OpenQuestion marker shows — never a guessed layer.
incidentsToIdeas.shortcutLabel: there is no Incident → Kernel door: judging reality is a truth decision (above the line)
incidentsToIdeas.notTruthMarker: reality, not a truth — no mirror, no freeze
incidentsToIdeas.exampleBody: createOrder fails 30% of the time: an item goes out-of-stock between add-to-cart and pay — no fixture covered this case (the kernel was false by omission). /learn turns the incident into a DRAFT idea carrying incident:#1043 verbatim, proposes=operation (the signal pins the operation), with no mirror and no freeze; the incident is traced back via idea_id. The Incident → Kernel edge stays blocked (REALITY_CANNOT_DECLARE_TRUTH). Incident #2099 (latency budget) pins no layer → OpenQuestion, never a guessed layer. Freezing into truth is still the human's mirror + /goal + approval.
incidentsToIdeas.footer: RealityMirror (S43) — reality injects IDEAS, never truths. The only outward edge is → idea-intake (S27); the freeze into /kernel is the human's mirror + /goal + approval, never this screen (the wall).

brain.title: /brain cockpit
brain.intro: Read-only projection of the brain (MemoryItem — episodic/semantic/procedural, pgvector, S30/S31) and the context graph (reuse-allowed/-denied decisions, S32/S33). It renders the memory-firewall's verdicts; it never writes memory.
brain.tutorialBody: On the left, memory items with their firewall taint; below, the context-graph reuse decisions — allowed if inside the goal's subgraph, denied otherwise (context is compiled, not accumulated).
brain.footer: Read-only. Memory lives in Postgres (pgvector); the cockpit renders verdicts, it never writes.

check.title: aidos check — law coverage
check.intro: The keystone rule of KRD §82.1: no KRD concept exists unless `aidos check` can verify it. This panel runs the law-coverage harness — every KRD law (the ten §82.1 laws plus the §29 completeness law) carries exactly one red fixture (a graph that violates it) and one green fixture (a graph that satisfies it). It mirrors `back/cmd/aidos/lawcoverage` byte-for-byte (lib/law-coverage.ts).
check.runDemoAria: Run the law-coverage check on the demo project
check.verdictGreen: GREEN — no KRD law is violated. The red set is green (§82.1).
check.footer: Read-only. The verdict is computed by the same harness the binary runs; correcting a law goes through a /goal — never a direct write (the wall).

tutorial.heading: Understanding aidos check
tutorial.lead: Before the jargon: what the compiler verifies, and why one red plus one green per law.

t1.title: A compiler of truth, not of code
t1.body: aidos check reads the truth graph (ideas, kernel, mirrors, context) and reports the objective state of the system — which KRD laws hold, which are breached.

t2.title: One law = one red + one green
t2.body: Each KRD law carries a red fixture (a graph that violates it → check reports a breach) and a green fixture (a graph that satisfies it → check passes). That pair proves the law is actually detectable.

t3.title: The five verbs cover every law
t3.body: check owns most laws; stable owns the phase law, diff the SemanticDiff, explain the BlockReason. No concept exists if no verb verifies it.

example.heading: Authority absent → MISSING_AUTHORITY
example.body: Run the red fixture of authority_absent: a truth requiring Product approval, with nobody granted. aidos check reports a MISSING_AUTHORITY breach with its fix path. Run the green fixture — Product granted — and the breach disappears.

demoCheckout.title: Demo checkout
demoCheckout.intro: The canonical demo slice: one intention — “a customer places an order from their cart” — travels the whole KRD loop, Idea → Goal → Kernel → Mirror → Src → Stable, red to green. This panel visualizes the loop and renders the live cart: click checkout to dispatch createOrder and see the placed order. Read-only over truth; the kernel write goes through an approved ChangeSet (the wall, §2).

pipeline.heading: The KRD loop for this slice

cart.heading: Cart
cart.dispatches: The click dispatches {op} (the bound operation — Plan(action, click), S11).

tutorial.heading: Understanding the full vertical
tutorial.lead: Before the jargon: what an end-to-end slice proves, and why it invents no truth.

t1.title: A composition acceptance
t1.body: The slice creates no new capability: it composes the prior 45 teeth to carry one intention from idea to a green button. createOrder, the Order entity and the button are produced by replaying the loop, never hand-written.

t2.title: The red IS the goal
t2.body: The Idea is intaken (S27), then a /goal writes the red set for createOrder (S29). The kernel is written only by an approved ChangeSet (S20, the door) — the agent has no GRANT (§2).

t3.title: The button is a projection
t3.body: The cart and checkout button are the emitted projection (S38) of the control-spec and the action that binds it; EvalState decides visible/enabled, and the click dispatches the bound operation. Nothing is hand-coded.

example.heading: A 2-line cart → a 2-line order
example.body: The demo cart carries 2 line items (widget ×2, gadget ×1). Click checkout: createOrder is dispatched and the placed order shows exactly the 2 lines from the cart — no phantom line, no dropped line. No total is invented: price, tax and payment are not in the Idea (out of scope, an OpenQuestion).

demoCheckout.footer: Read-only. The button runs the deterministic projection (the TS twin of the Go slice); the kernel write goes through an approved ChangeSet — never a screen write (the wall).

adoption.title: Adoption + Release v0
adoption.intro: The AdoptionStage ladder names the smallest ratchet that clicks next (KRD §82.5): five declared tiers T0→T4. T1 does NOT require QualityDiversity (advanced, §82.6); T2 requires a live RealityMirror (Livre XX); T4 requires an EvolutionSandbox (§66.1). Release v0 is ASSEMBLED — a read-only, content-addressed inventory of what exists. It assembles; it installs nothing, ships nothing, writes no truth.
adoption.tutorialStep1: Pick a capability scenario: the ladder and the pack recompute (a pure, deterministic twin).
adoption.tutorialStep2: Read the T0→T4 ladder: the current tier is highlighted, the next installable ratchet is marked, each blocked tier lists its Gaps.
adoption.tutorialStep3: Spot the three load-bearing facts: T1 without QualityDiversity, T2 blocked without a RealityMirror, T4 blocked without an EvolutionSandbox.
adoption.tutorialStep4: Browse Release v0: CLI surface, routes, demo, docs, test inventory, changelog, known limits — no install / ship / publish button (assemble only).
adoption.noQdNote: T1 does NOT require QualityDiversity — QD is an advanced capability (KRD §82.6), not in the mandatory minimum.
adoption.emptyPack: Empty view → empty-but-valid pack: no lists, no fabricated content (content-addressed nonetheless).
adoption.assembleOnlyNote: It ASSEMBLES an inventory; it installs nothing, ships nothing, publishes nothing. Recording a pack goes through the aidos writer role via a ChangeSet (S20), never the agent.

firstApp.title: Your first application
firstApp.subtitle: A guided, step-by-step tutorial: from intention to a clickable button, following the KRD loop — without ever going from prompt to code.

build.heading: What you'll build
build.body: One small, canonical capability: “a customer places an order from their cart” (createOrder). You'll drive it through the whole KRD verticale, from a fuzzy idea to a green, clickable checkout button.

rule.heading: The golden rule
rule.body: You never write a line of code without a red scenario first. The human owns truth, the agent owns implementation, the wall enforces the boundary. Every truth goes through this loop:
rule.loop: Idea → Mirror (BDD) → Goal (red set) → Kernel → Green → Stable phase

funnel.title: The funnel — from account to a deployed app, for real
funnel.lead: Not a simulation: every step produces a REAL artefact through the engine. By default the template-first path instantiates a green starter (S81) then modifies it — a stranger succeeds on their first run. The blank-idea path is the advanced mode.
funnel.pathTemplateHint: Instantiate a deterministic green starter, then modify it. The acceptance gate is already green.
funnel.pathBlankHint: Start from a free-text intention, no starter. May miss the acceptance gate — hence advanced.
funnel.intentTemplateHint: On template-first, this is the modification you graft onto the starter (e.g. "add a promo code").
funnel.intentBlankHint: On blank idea, describe the app to build from scratch.
funnel.deployedTitle: 🚀 App deployed — driven by the real engine
funnel.deployedBody: Every step wrote real truth (via the deterministic twins): a content-addressed starter, a content-addressed idea, a computed red set, a non-gameable build verdict, a content-addressed deploy subdomain. No simulation.
funnel.notDeployedBody: The funnel never declares a deploy without a green build. A step is checked only if its real artefact exists (empty email → blocks at signup; fuzzy verdict → no goal; non-green build → no deploy).

guide.heading: The guided walkthrough
guide.lead: Eight steps, from idea to button. Check each one off as you go (your progress is saved), and open the matching panel to do it for real — everything happens on a screen.
guide.complete: 🎉 Congratulations — your first application went through the whole loop!
guide.completeBody: You drove an intention from idea to a green, clickable button, through the mirror, the goal, the kernel (via an approved ChangeSet) and a stable phase. This is exactly how every capability is born in AIDOS.

s1.title: 1 · Capture the idea
s1.body: It all starts from an intention, never a prompt. Drop the candidate-truth “a customer places an order from their cart” into the ideas store. An idea has no version and no mirror: it's a wish, not yet a truth.
s1.doneWhen: the idea appears in the store, in the candidate state (no freeze).

s2.title: 2 · Grill the intention
s2.body: Before nearing the kernel, sharpen the intention above the wall: is it falsifiable? is the language crisp? /grill routes it — sharp → ready, fuzzy → explore (/spike), bad → rejected (and traced).
s2.doneWhen: the intention is sharp and falsifiable (verdict “grilled”).

s3.title: 3 · Open a goal — the red set
s3.body: Promote the idea toward truth: opening the goal writes the RED mirror of createOrder. The red IS the goal. At this point no truth is written — a DRAFT ChangeSet is opened, never applied (the agent has no GRANT).
s3.doneWhen: a red set is computed; the ChangeSet is DRAFT.

s4.title: 4 · Choose the mirror form
s4.body: The nature of the truth dictates its language: a journey → Gherkin (Godog), an invariant ∀ → property test (rapid / fast-check), a workflow → state→command→events fixture. You don't prove a UX truth like a business invariant.
s4.doneWhen: the red mirror is linked to the truth (reflects) and it fails (red).

s5.title: 5 · Approve the ChangeSet — the only door
s5.body: The kernel is written only through an approved ChangeSet, admitted by the completeness gate (the spec_delta carries its mirror_delta — no monster). This is the wall: the agent never writes truth; only the aidos role applies it.
s5.doneWhen: the ChangeSet goes DRAFT → APPLIED; the mirror is alive.

s6.title: 6 · Code to green
s6.body: Now — and only now — you code. red → green → refactor, outside-in, in this goal's package only. Sensors stay green at every diff (typecheck, lint, tests, architecture).
s6.doneWhen: the red set is green ∧ prior green intact ∧ no red sensor.

s7.title: 7 · Emit the projections
s7.body: From the single source (the entity), the emitters generate — deterministically, byte-identical on re-run — the Go struct (sqlc), the Postgres DDL, the TS type and the UI. Never double-typed, never hand-edited.
s7.doneWhen: projections are up to date and byte-identical on re-run.

s8.title: 8 · Seal a stable phase
s8.body: When everything resolves and is green, seal a content-addressed stable phase on the DAG: the “kernel lockfile”, the resting point the next step consumes. Done is COMPUTED, never declared.
s8.doneWhen: a new stable phase is sealed; the button is green and clickable.

see.heading: See it green, for real
see.body: The checkout slice is already implemented and proven end to end — Godog acceptance on real Postgres, ∀ properties, a front twin and the button's e2e. Open the demo and click: the order is really placed.

panels.heading: Do it for real
panels.lead: The assistant above simulates the loop. To do it on the real Workbench panels:

globalInvariants.title: The GlobalInvariant — a cross-cell invariant, a costly exception
globalInvariants.subtitle: GlobalInvariant (KRD §49.1)
globalInvariants.intro: A GlobalInvariant is a truth that spans MORE THAN ONE cell (bounded context) — distinct from the per-truth TruthScope (S15) that scopes a single truth's reach. It declares its scope ∈ { local_cell, contract_pair, federation_policy }, its blast_radius ∈ { small, bounded, global } and approval_required ∈ { cell_owner, both_contract_owners, architecture_owner }. The rule (§49.1): "a cross-cell invariant is a costly exception, not the normal mode" — the bounded contexts stay the primary walls. Two laws: a violation reddens EVERY cell in its reach; a wider blast_radius demands a wider authority.
globalInvariants.tutorialBody: The card names the pii-forgettable-federation invariant: its scope (federation_policy), the spanned cells (checkout, profile, billing), its predicate, its blast_radius (global) and approval_required (architecture_owner). The red-wave panel shows that a violation in billing reddens ALL THREE cells, not just the violator (the §49 fan-out, weighted along composes — S19). The admission table renders, per granted approval, the computed decision: a global blast_radius approved only by the cell_owner is blocked (INSUFFICIENT_APPROVAL_FOR_BLAST_RADIUS), approved by the architecture_owner it is admitted.
globalInvariants.redWaveBody: A violation in the billing cell reddens EVERY cell in the invariant's reach (checkout, profile, billing) — not just the violator. The fan-out reuses S19's weighted propagation: a load-bearing cross-cell link crosses to the partner cell.
globalInvariants.admissionHeading: Admission table — a wider radius demands a wider authority
globalInvariants.proposeStubBody: Declaring or re-scoping a GlobalInvariant is a truth-write: it goes through propose → ChangeSet → approval (SemanticDiff change_type rescope/reweight/reauthorize, KRD §44.1), never a direct write from the screen. The ChangeSet engine (S20) and the /goal wiring are later steps; this proposal is a stub here (an OpenQuestion).
globalInvariants.footer: Source: back/kernel/globalinvariant · pure projection lib/global-invariant.ts · migration kernel.global_invariant (SELECT-only, the wall). No truth is written from this screen.

sagas.title: The SagaInvariant — a failed leg triggers compensation
sagas.subtitle: SagaInvariant + CoherenceTest (KRD §49.2)
sagas.intro: A SagaInvariant is a CROSS-CELL distributed-transaction invariant: it binds named participants (order, payment, shipping) to a property that must hold across the federation, each participant carrying its compensation. Per §49.1 a saga is transverse by definition — its scope is contract_pair or federation_policy, NEVER local_cell. The canonical property: « payment_captured implies (order_confirmed or compensation_executed) ». A leg that fails after the capture triggers the declared compensation, so compensation_executed holds and the property is satisfied VIA compensation. The forbidden monster: a captured payment with neither a confirmed order nor an executed compensation. The CoherenceTest guarantees « no consumed event is produced by an incompatible version ».
sagas.tutorialBody: The card names the checkout-payment-shipping saga: its scope (federation_policy), the cross-cell property and the cert_language (statechart). The statechart shows the commit transitions (order → payment → shipping) then the compensation transitions drawn back from a failed leg. The participant cards list the cell, the commit events and the compensation steps pinned id@version. The outcome table renders, per trace, the computed outcome: the happy path is satisfied, the failed-leg-with-compensation is satisfied (refundPayment@v3 → cancelOrder@v2 → compensation_executed visible), and the captured-payment-with-nothing is violated (SAGA_INVARIANT_VIOLATED, red). The CoherenceTest card shows incompatible / INCOMPATIBLE_CONTRACT_VERSION when payment.commands has moved past the pinned v2.
sagas.statechartBody: The saga's statechart: the forward commit transitions (order → payment → shipping) and the compensation transitions drawn back from a failed leg. A leg that fails after payment_captured triggers the declared compensation.
sagas.outcomeHeading: Outcome table — a failed leg triggers compensation
sagas.coherenceHeading: CoherenceTest — no consumed event from an incompatible version
sagas.coherenceBody: The CoherenceTest pins the consumed contracts (order.events@v3, payment.commands@v2) and checks, against the current heads, that none is pinned to a non-head producer version. It composes the S17 Resolve staleness primitive: a contract pinned off-head is incompatible.
sagas.proposeStubBody: Declaring or re-scoping a SagaInvariant is a truth-write: it goes through propose → ChangeSet → approval (SemanticDiff change_type rescope/refine/reweight, KRD §44.1), never a direct write from the screen. The ChangeSet engine (S20) is a later step; this proposal is a stub here (an OpenQuestion).
sagas.footer: Source: back/kernel/sagas · pure projection lib/saga.ts · migration kernel.saga_invariant (SELECT-only, the wall). No truth is written from this screen.

temporal.title: Temporal invariants
temporal.subtitle: TemporalInvariant
temporal.intro: A TemporalInvariant is a truth whose property is time-dependent: it MUST declare its clock (system | external | logical) and its tolerance (a duration), and its mirror is a temporal form (statechart | tla+ | uppaal). "Every temporal truth must declare its clock." A property reddens on a real violation, while the declared tolerance prevents a false red (a flake).
temporal.tutorialBody: The card shows the invariant "payment_captured implies order_confirmed within 5 minutes" with its clock, tolerance and mirror form. The green-band marker (5m ± 10s) makes the tolerance legible. The evaluation table computes each verdict via the pure evaluator: 4m58s and 5m04s are HELD (the 5m04s case is inside tolerance — NOT a flake), 5m20s is VIOLATED (over tolerance, the property reddens), and the out-of-order observation is VIOLATED. No real clock is read: the elapsed datum is passed in.
temporal.bandBody: The bound is 5m; the tolerance widens the green band to 5m + 10s (one-sided — you violate a deadline by being late, never early, ADR 0034). A confirmation at 5m04s stays inside the band: HELD, not a flake.
temporal.reEvaluateDone: Verdicts recomputed by the pure evaluator (lib/temporal) — below the line, no truth-write.
temporal.proposeStubBody: Declaring a temporal invariant or changing its tolerance is a truth-write: it goes through idea → mirror → /goal → ChangeSet → approval, never a direct write from the screen. The ChangeSet engine (S20) will wire this proposal; here it is a stub (OpenQuestion).
temporal.footer: Read-only projection of the KRD §49.3 temporal invariant. The rule (the required clock, the tolerance band) is the human truth, above the line; the pure evaluator lives in back/kernel/temporal and lib/temporal.ts.

economics.title: Harness economics
economics.subtitle: HarnessCostBudget + ValueCase
economics.intro: Each cell DECLARES its HarnessCostBudget — the most its harness may cost (CI minutes, LLM tokens per /goal, mutation-run runtime, human-review minutes) and the expected risk reduction. A truth whose MEASURED harness cost exceeds that budget without a `justified` ValueCase is flagged. "The more a constraint costs to maintain, the more it must justify its value."
economics.tutorialBody: The budget is DECLARED above the line (the read-only fitness zone) — you read it, the agent never tunes it (§8). The caps are shown beside the measured cost (red when it exceeds). The table computes, per case, the verdict with the pure evaluator: within budget, over budget flagged (with the HARNESS_COST_EXCEEDS_BUDGET BlockReason), or over budget justified (the costly truth earned its keep). Raising a cap is a /goal, never a screen edit.
economics.reEvaluateDone: Re-evaluated — the pure evaluator (lib/economics) recomputed each verdict, below the line, writing nothing.
economics.proposeStubBody: Declaring or raising a HarnessCostBudget is a truth-write above the line: it goes through propose → ChangeSet → approval, never a direct write from the screen. The ChangeSet engine (S20) will freeze the proposal; here it stays an OpenQuestion (no write without approval).
economics.footer: Read-only projection of harness economics (KRD §66.3). The HarnessCostBudget is the DECLARED bar above the line (the fitness zone); the pure evaluator lives in back/runtime/economics and lib/economics.ts. The measured cost is CONSUMED (telemetry / changesets / the S40 mutation run / the /goal's spend), never produced here.

agents.title: Agents — governed layers
agents.subtitle: CoucheAgent + AgentRun
agents.intro: Modelling an agent IS laying a LAYER: a CoucheAgent is a source above the line (versioned, content-addressed) declaring an agent's role / rights / objective / tools / skills / hooks / limits. A single execution is NOT a layer — it is an AgentRun, a runtime event below the line. An agent proposes, executes, explores — but never declares alone what is true.
agents.engraved: “In KRD an agent is never an authority — it is a governed layer; it proposes, executes, explores, but never declares alone what is true.”
agents.tutorialBody: Each card is a CoucheAgent: its taxonomy (agent | equipe_agents | orchestration), its DECLARED rights — peut_modifier_noyau and peut_modifier_fitness are ALWAYS false (locked, not a screen toggle), its read/write zones (none above the line), its skills/MCP/hooks, its AuthorityGraph (S16) and its TruthScope (S15). Below, a recent AgentRun: an agent attempting a write above the line is REFUSED (red, AGENT_WRITE_ABOVE_WATERLINE). The “Propose a scenario” button yields a `proposed` (never `admitted`) proposal routing through idea → mirror → /goal → approval; a self-approve attempt is refused (an agent is never an authority).
agents.proposeScenario: checkout charges tax on EU orders
agents.proposedBody: The agent PROPOSES — it does not declare. The proposal stays `proposed`: it must route through idea → mirror → /goal → a HUMAN authority's approval (S16) before it can be admitted. No kernel or mirror write from the screen.
agents.selfApproveRefused: Refused: an agent is never an authority. The proposal stays `proposed`; only a human authority in the graph (S16) can admit it. This is the circularity the wall forbids (CLAUDE.md §8).
agents.recordDone: AgentRun recorded below the line (runtime, append-only). A run carries no version and no mirror — it is not a layer, not a truth: just the trace of what the agent did.
agents.driveBody: Drive is the deterministic shell that claims a red item and runs a scripted session (the LLM is mocked): each turn it gates the action BEFORE execution, executes only on green, records AgentAction{Autorisee:false} on any refusal, ticks the meter, and loops until goal.IsClosed OR a budget breach. The Result is COMPUTED by goal.IsClosed — never self-reported by the mock.
agents.driveFaultLabel: Inject an above-the-line write (back/kernel) on the 1st turn
agents.driveComputedNote: The wall holds: the above-the-line write is refused BEFORE execution, its effect never lands. The Result is computed, never declared.
agents.postBody: After each action the loop applies a deterministic post-check per nature: a code-changing action → the mirror/sensor must agree; a propose → a shape-check; a read → a no-op assertion. The judge is the mirror, never the agent's claimed confidence (§8).
agents.postFaultLabel: Inject a fault: the agent CLAIMS a green flip the sensor still reads red
agents.postComputedNote: The judge is the mirror: a claimed flip the sensor disagrees with is REFUSED (AGENT_POSTCHECK_FAILED), the effect never lands, the goal stays red. The Result is invariant to the claimed confidence — EVERY action is re-checked, not only the code-changing ones.
agents.sandboxHeading: Bind the OS/Postgres sandbox (defense in depth)
agents.sandboxBody: The loop is bound to a real OS/container sandbox running under the aidos_agent Postgres role. The app tree is the ONLY writable root (the OS mirror of the PathAllowed allow-list), egress is fail-closed, exec is an allow-list, and cgroup/ulimit cap the resources. One allow-list governs THREE levels: the FS boundary (1), the hook (1', zone+path), the Postgres GRANT (3). The LLM is the single gated exception, isolated behind one GenerateAction function with a deterministic fake.
agents.sandboxFaultLabel: Inject a fault: aim OUTSIDE the sandbox (a truth zone / an undeclared host)
agents.sandboxButton: Run the sandbox on a generated action
agents.footer: Read-only projection of the agent layers (KRD §21/§13.8). The CoucheAgent is a source above the line; the pure functions live in back/kernel/agentlayer + lib/agentlayer.ts, the AgentRun in back/runtime/agentrun + lib/agentrun.ts. The wall (S04) refuses any write above the line with AGENT_WRITE_ABOVE_WATERLINE.
agents.confinementBody: The bdd-writer declares no network host and no exec — so egress and subprocess are denied by default (maximum confinement). Click to check the pure verdict.
agents.implBody: The below-the-line projection of a CoucheAgent: regenerable, content-addressed by its layer reference, it carries NO truth (no version-as-truth, no mirror field) — unrepresentable as a CoucheAgent, just as an AgentRun is never a layer. Type + invariants only (the emitter is BA03).
agents.emitterBody: Project projects the governed layer into a runnable AgentImplementation. It is deterministic: the same (layer, cfg, pack) → a byte-identical projection. The providerCfg carries ONLY the resolved endpoint/key — never a behaviour knob (temperature/seed/max-turns come uniquely from the layer). The control below runs the emitter twice (same inputs), then with a different endpoint/key.
agents.emitterUnstableTag: unstable (failure) — the emitter must be deterministic
agents.emitterCfgIgnoredTag: cfg carries no knob: endpoint/key do not change the projection
agents.emitterCfgLeakTag: knob leak (failure) — the cfg changed the projection
agents.promptBody: The system prompt is a deterministic template over the ONLY declared fields: role, objective, stop conditions, the wall boundary in prose, and the forbidden/allowed paths verbatim. Assemble twice (same inputs), then with a perturbed non-declared knob (seed/temperature/model) — the output is byte-identical: no out-of-layer field leaks, and the kernel/mirror zones always appear.
agents.promptUnstableTag: unstable (failure) — the prompt varied on equal inputs
agents.promptNoLeakTag: no leak — a non-declared knob does not change the prompt
agents.promptLeakTag: leak (failure) — an out-of-layer field changed the prompt
agents.promptNoWallTag: wall absent (failure) — a forbidden zone is missing
agents.bindingsBody: Governance can only NARROW the capability surface, never WIDEN it. Tools derive only from enabled MCP bindings; skills only from enabled skills; hooks preserve the Mandatory flag. Run the resolution from the screen: a disabled binding is excluded, a mandatory hook always survives.
agents.viewerBody: Select an agent: its governed CoucheAgent (the SOURCE, above the line) projects deterministically into an AgentImplementation (below the line, regenerable, carries NO truth). Display only — there is NO run control: nothing executes until something is applied (the wall). Re-project → same hash (determinism badge).
agents.capProbeBody: Enter an MCP tool (server, tool) and run the pure enforcer: allowed if and only if the pair is an enabled binding of the resolved implementation; otherwise the AGENT_TOOL_NOT_BOUND BlockReason renders (default-deny — set-membership, never a judgment).
agents.capProbeAllowed: Allowed — (server, tool) is an enabled binding
agents.skillProbeBody: Enter a skill and run the pure enforcer: allowed if and only if the skill is an enabled binding of the resolved implementation; otherwise the AGENT_SKILL_NOT_BOUND BlockReason renders (default-deny — set-membership, never a judgment). The 3rd of the four axes: without it, SkillBinding.Enabled is mere documentation.
agents.skillProbeAllowed: Allowed — the skill is an enabled binding
agents.pathProbeBody: Enter a target path and run the pure enforcer: allowed if and only if the path is covered by an AllowedPaths prefix AND outside ForbiddenPaths — the ALLOW-LIST, DISTINCT from the zone deny-list. Otherwise the AGENT_PATH_NOT_ALLOWED BlockReason renders (default-deny — prefix membership, never a judgment). The 4th declared axis: the writable root is the app tree, never /kernel or /mirrors.
agents.pathProbeAllowed: Allowed — path under AllowedPaths and outside ForbiddenPaths
agents.hookGateBody: Distinct from the four wall axes (zone/capacity/skill/confinement) that gate what an action may TOUCH, this gates whether a TURN may be ACCEPTED: admissible if and only if every mandatory hook (HooksObligatoires{Mandatory:true}) actually RAN and is GREEN — presence is NOT enough. The verdict comes from the hook BINARY's own deterministic exit/BlockReason (the HookVerdict record), never the agent transcript (§8 — the judge is deterministic). Inject a fault (hook-honesty §5: a hook that never fires is dead) to SEE the gate flip from accepted to AGENT_MANDATORY_HOOK_SKIPPED / AGENT_MANDATORY_HOOK_RED.
agents.hookGateFaultNone: None — every mandatory hook ran GREEN
agents.hookGateFaultSkipped: Remove a mandatory hook's verdict (never ran → SKIPPED)
agents.hookGateFaultRed: Redden a mandatory hook (ran but failed → RED)
agents.hookGateAccepted: Accepted — every mandatory hook ran GREEN
agents.budgetGateBody: A monotone RunMeter (tokens/turns/ci-minutes/wall-clock) checked against the TWO declared budgets — goal.Budgets (S29) ∧ economics.HarnessCostBudget (S51). The effective per-shared-axis cap is the min() of the two: the tightest wins (fail-closed). Cost is COST-AWARE (tokens × declared rate); a wall-clock deadline is included. The min() is the authoritative deterministic rule (§8).
agents.arbiterGateBody: Intent is classified from the action STRUCTURE (tool name + args), never from the label. Re-labelling cannot change the verdict; if a deterministic tool exists the action is never LLMGated. Ticking "LLM requested" on a deterministic structure is a determinism gap that BLOCKS.
agents.llmIsoBody: Only the provider package may import the LLM SDK. A deterministic rule (an import scan, not an agent) refuses any other import at build time — "the LLM isolated to one gated exception" becomes an ENFORCED architectural invariant, not 25 repetitions of prose.
agents.llmIsoFaultLabel: Fault injection: add an LLM-SDK import outside the provider
agents.llmIsoGreen: Green: no LLM-SDK import outside the provider — the invariant holds.
agents.llmIsoRed: Red: an LLM SDK imported outside the provider
agents.identityHeading: Identity / auth toward the MCP servers (BA18)
agents.identityBody: The loop presents the content-hash of its AgentImplementation as a capability token; each MCP server re-derives the token it expects for the CoucheAgent@version it is asked to act for and accepts the call ONLY if the token binds the calling process to exactly that identity. owner_agent is PROVEN by the token, never chain-declared.
agents.identityFaultOther: ANOTHER identity (stolen token — owner_agent not forgeable)
agents.identityVerifiedTag: Accepted: the token binds the process to that CoucheAgent@version
agents.identityRefusedTag: Refused: the token does not bind the expected identity
agents.runDriveBody: The agentloop MCP server drives the deterministic loop on a red item under the governed layer. Launching is BELOW the line: the run records an AgentRun (telemetry), it never writes truth. At the transport boundary an unbound tool is refused (AGENT_TOOL_NOT_BOUND); an action in a forbidden zone is refused in place (AGENT_WRITE_ABOVE_WATERLINE) and its effect never lands. Any truth the run proposes goes through propose → ChangeSet → approval.
agents.runUnboundLabel: Target an UNBOUND tool (refused at the transport boundary)
agents.runNoTruthTag: Wrote no truth above the waterline
agents.runComputedNote: The result is computed by goal.IsClosed over the evolving sensor world — never declared by the agent (§8).
agents.replayBody: To replay a run, the AgentRun schema gains three fields: impl (the AgentImplementation content-hash), seed (declared in BA01, else derived Hash(impl‖pack‖item)) and provider_transcript. This is a NEW @version of the record (supersede-via-version, anti-overwrite §9) — never a mutation of the existing hash. A legacy seedless run stays readable.
agents.replaySupersedeNote: A run is BELOW the line: no version field, no mirror field — unrepresentable as a layer. The schema extension goes through the legal door and is back-filled (announced), never a silent side-effect.
agents.economicsHeading: Live meter & halt-on-budget wired into the loop (BA27)
agents.economicsBody: The loop wires the RunMeter (BA11): tokens/CI-minutes/wall-clock accumulate AS IT GOES, and the budget is checked BEFORE each turn. A turn that WOULD cross the cap is refused before it starts (pre-call halt, gap G3): the meter NEVER crosses the cap. The terminated run's measured cost then feeds economics.Evaluate (§66.3) — until now no AgentRun fed the harness economy.
agents.economicsPrecallNote: Deterministic, PRE-CALL halt: the min() of the caps (BA11) is authoritative; the meter stays at/below the cap. The §66.3 verdict is read-only (the cell declares its budget above the line); raising a cap is a /goal, never an edit.
agents.ba28Body: A recorded run REPLAYS identically (Replay(run).ID == run.ID) from its inputs; the persisted transcript is REDACTED before it is shown — the ledger is not a secret store (gap H1). Click: a secret-bearing transcript is scrubbed, then the run is replayed.
agents.ba28LedgerNote: Redaction runs BEFORE persistence/display (a deterministic substitution over a CLOSED pattern set, never an LLM judgment). The replay re-injects from the confined SOURCE, not from the log. A run stays below the line — no truth write.
agents.ba29Body: Replay proves the record RE-DERIVES (hash) — but not that the REAL run matched it: an unrecorded bash side-effect never moves the hash. The ledger reconciles an INDEPENDENT effect-log, captured AT THE BOUNDARY, against the recorded actions. A run is AUDITABLE iff it re-derives (replay) AND reconciles (effects).
agents.ba29WallNote: Read-only surface: the ledger writes no truth. A fidelity breach is an OBSERVATION, surfaced via the idea-intake door (S27), never a kernel write. Reconciliation = a deterministic diff, never an LLM agent.
agents.ba30Body: A failed/abandoned/blocked run — or a GREEN run of abnormal shape (thrashing against the wall, a determinism gap) — becomes a reality.Signal carrying the incident_derived taint. The signal identity is content-addressed on the PATTERN (failure class + dominant refusal code + cause class), NEVER the run id: two distinct runs sharing a failure mode collapse into one recurring signal (Recurrence climbs). An ordinary green run produces no signal.
agents.ba30RecurrenceNote: Two distinct runs of the same pattern collapse into a single incident id: that is exactly what lets Recurrence climb (gap I2). Without identity-by-pattern, reality.Observe would re-observe a fresh identity every time and Recurrence would never exceed 1.
agents.ba30WallNote: The wall holds: the cause_sketch is a HYPOTHESIS, never a truth; the signal is reality (incident_derived taint, no version, no mirror). The far edge stays idea → mirror → /goal → human. A pure, total, deterministic classifier — never an LLM agent.
agents.ba31Heading: Learnings — the loop learns from the world (BA31)
agents.ba31Body: The on-ramp: a failed / abandoned / green-hollow run flows through reality.Observe → Learn → ToIdea to produce a DRAFT idea — PROPOSED, never applied. The only legal door stays idea → mirror → /goal → approval; no kernel write.
agents.ba31RecurrenceNote: Two distinct runs of the same failure mode collapse into ONE recurring incident (Recurrence climbs) → a single 'harden-the-harness' idea.
agents.ba31ForgedBody: The apply NEVER trusts the self-asserted Status field: it re-derives the verdict from the S16 authority graph. A forged 'admitted' with no admitting authority record is refused PROPOSAL_NOT_ADMITTED.
agents.ba31WallNote: The wall holds: the on-ramp PROPOSES a DRAFT idea, it never applies a truth; the apply re-derives admission (authority.Decide), never trusts the field. Pure, total, deterministic — never an LLM agent.
agents.economyBody: For each recent run, the tokens BEFORE and AFTER compressing the LLM input (the ContextPack + the transcript). The ContextCompressor (HR02–HR04) compresses the input BEFORE the model to extend the margin UNDER the budget cap — it never raises the cap. The gate verdict is invariant to compression: the same action structure, the same verdict.
agents.economyWallNote: The wall holds: the perRunEconomy projection is pure and deterministic (same runs ⇒ same report), read-only below the line — it writes no truth. Compression extends the margin under the cap, never the cap itself.

scheduler.heading: Scheduler — role & fencing (BA20)
scheduler.body: The scheduler is the distinct role that ALONE transitions a RedWorkItem (open→claimed), stamping owner_agent, lease_until and a monotone lease_epoch (the fencing token, gap E2). The agent role CANNOT transition (the wall: INSERT+SELECT only).
scheduler.columnsLine: Columns written (the only ones the scheduler may write): {cols}.
scheduler.agentRefusedHeading: Refused in place — the agent role never transitions
scheduler.agentRefusedBody: The agent role is INSERT+SELECT only on runtime.red_work_queue: no UPDATE, hence no transition. The Postgres GRANT makes it mechanical; the scheduler is not a 2nd privileged role (no truth write).
scheduler.matchBody: MatchRole maps the mirror-first HEAD of the queue to an agent BY DECLARED ROLE — an algorithm, never an LLM prompt (determinism-first). If no free agent of the matching role exists for N ticks, the starvation detector emits a still_red signal ("the team is mis-staffed").
scheduler.matchOk: Match: {ref} — a free agent of the required role.
scheduler.matchNone: No match: no free agent of the required role (never a wrong-role fallback — the wall holds).
scheduler.starveSignal: The head {item} demands role {role} but no free agent has supplied it for {ticks} ticks. This signal feeds the BA28 on-ramp.
scheduler.starveNone: No starvation: the head can be staffed (a free agent of the matching role exists).
scheduler.engineBody: The tick driver supplies `now`; the pure `schedule` planner reclaims expired leases (claimed→open, no human action), keeps an item with an unresolved dependency blocked, and leases the mirror-first head. Resolve the mirror then re-tick to unblock the projection.
scheduler.fenceBody: The reclaimed item's current epoch is {current}. A write carrying a stale (lower) epoch is refused — AGENT_LEASE_FENCED — to prevent a lost update from a woken-late agent.
scheduler.fenceOk: Live epoch: the write may land (lease still held).
scheduler.dispatchBody: The dispatch panel under the scheduler role: the queue in mirror-first order, status/owner/lease/epoch per item, items blocked on unresolved dependencies, free agents by role, and the starvation alert. "Dispatch next" runs scheduler.tick (the pure planner); "Reclaim expired" re-ticks to reclaim expired leases — all below the line, never truth.
scheduler.dispatchAssignments: {n} assignment(s) emitted at the last tick (fresh leases + expired markers).
scheduler.dispatchStarveBody: The mirror-first head {item} demands role {role} but no free agent supplies it: the team is mis-staffed. This signal feeds the BA28 on-ramp.
scheduler.dispatchNoTick: No tick run yet — click "Dispatch next" to schedule.
scheduler.orchBody: An orchestration layer carries a declared OrchestrationPolicy (claim arbitration, fan-out/fan-in, same-file conflict policy, MaxConcurrency + per-role caps). The policy is a SOURCE above the wall: editing it here PROPOSES a change (idea→mirror→/goal), never a live write. A run pins the @version (immutability per-run); any same-target conflict is arbitrated by rule, never by a race.
scheduler.orchPolicyValid: Policy valid — bounded by the spec MaxConcurrency knob (never a phantom cap).
scheduler.orchProposeNote: Editing the policy opens a proposal (idea→mirror→/goal) requiring the S16 authority — never a direct kernel write (the wall).
scheduler.orchPinFrozen: Run pinned to {pinned} — version frozen (immutability per-run).
scheduler.orchPinForbidden: Mid-run edit FORBIDDEN: the live version diverges from the pin {pinned} — a NEW proposal is required, never a live-edit (gap F3).
scheduler.orchConflictLoser: Loser: {agent} — it WAITS, its work is never discarded.
scheduler.orchConflictNoLost: Zero lost-update: the conflict serialises (one lease at a time) then merges via merge-semantic (a red mirror blocks). Never a race or a coin-flip.
scheduler.orchNoConflict: No conflict resolved — click "Resolve same-target conflict".
scheduler.teamBody: A team of N agents (two roles) under an OrchestrationPolicy. The scheduler (scheduleTeam, pure) serialises same-target conflicts (the loser WAITS), enforces MaxConcurrency, and drives the dependency hand-off: A (mirror) → the role-A agent; B (projection) stays BLOCKED until A resolves, then leases to the role-B agent.
scheduler.teamConcurrency: Live leases: {live} / declared cap {cap} (MaxConcurrency, never exceeded — gap F1).
scheduler.teamProposeNote: The wall holds for every member: orchestration coordinates, it never writes truth — only the scheduler role's UPDATE lands a transition.
scheduler.teamNoConflict: No same-target conflict resolved this tick — click "Tick".
scheduler.computedNote: Deterministic: every verdict is computed by the pure lib/scheduler functions (claim, matchRole, detectStarvation, schedule, fence, resolveConflict, validatePolicy, scheduleTeam), exactly as the Go core + the GRANT decide it.

proofLevels.title: The proof levels — N0 to N5
proofLevels.subtitle: Click a level to see its proof language. Six natures of truth, each with its proof form and its judge — you don't prove a UX truth like a business invariant.
proofLevels.waterline: ≈≈≈ Waterline ≈≈≈  above: the human anchors meaning · below: the agent self-certifies
proofLevels.proseNote: Beyond the ladder: a UX truth / a feeling is proven in prose (human review, a11y, A/B) — non-executable, it does not count in the completeness law.
proofLevels.docLink: The full catalogue of certification languages →

n0.name: Intention / Journey
n0.proves: That a full user journey does what the human expects, end to end.
n0.form: An approved acceptance scenario — Given / When / Then.
n0.verdict: The human — the agent never declares itself green on a journey's meaning.

n1.name: Domain / Invariants (∀)
n1.proves: A business rule true on ALL paths — an invariant, path-independent.
n1.verdict: Human-anchored — the agent may pass the existing rule, never invent one.

n2.name: Workflow / Use-case
n2.proves: That this exact path produces this exact result.
n2.form: A state → command → state + events fixture, the frozen canonical example.
n2.verdict: Human-anchored — the agent adds variants, never touches the frozen canon.

n3.name: Contract / Boundary (port)
n3.proves: That boundaries between pieces hold: versioned schemas, port contracts.
n3.form: Versioned schema + Context Map + inter-cell contracts.

n4.name: Code / Unit
n4.proves: That a function does what its signature promises.
n4.form: Unit test + local TDD, doubled by strict typing as a free sensor.

n5.name: Infra / Adapters
n5.proves: That the real adapter (real DB, real service) honors the contract — not just the fake.
n5.form: Pact provider verification + Testcontainers on real infra.

bascule.title: The proof layers — E0 to E7
bascule.subtitle: FK16, the evidence-first switch. Re-label an N0-N5 mirror corpus onto the E0-E7 ladder without any loss: each mirror gains its E derived from the test it actually runs, while keeping its old N — deprecated via lifecycle, never deleted (append-only).

e0.name: No evidence
e0.desc: nothing proves it — the floor (prose alone does not count).

e1.name: Syntax / typecheck / lint
e1.desc: the code compiles and passes strict typing + lint.

e2.name: Unit tests
e2.desc: a function does what its signature promises.

e3.name: Contract / integration
e3.desc: journey, workflow, port contract — the integration proof.

e7.name: Formal / quasi-formal proof
e7.desc: Z3 / TLA+ — the rare catastrophic, unsampleable cap.

bascule.relabelHint: Submit an N-typed mirror corpus (or leave empty for the sample). The switch derives each E and deprecates its N — losing nothing.
bascule.noLossOk: Zero loss — every N mirror now carries its E, its N preserved and deprecated.
bascule.noLossBad: Loss detected — a mirror or an N-label vanished. Switch refused.
bascule.deprecatedNote: The N-label is never deleted: its lifecycle moves to "deprecated" (kept for provenance), the typing authority moves to E. Anti-overwrite (§9): we deprecate, we do not destroy.
bascule.legacyNote: The original N0-N5 ladder, preserved for provenance. It stays inspectable; the proof authority is now E0-E7.

contextCompression.title: Context compression
contextCompression.subtitle: ContextCompressor port
contextCompression.intro: The ContextCompressor port (ADR 0035) compresses the LLM INPUT — the rendered ContextPack and the transcript — BEFORE the model, to extend the margin UNDER the budget cap. It never relieves the cap. It is a REPLACEABLE, deterministic, byte-lossless tool: Compress(prompt) returns a compacted text + a reversible handle; Retrieve(handle) returns the original. The load-bearing contract: Retrieve(Compress(x)) == the original.
contextCompression.tutorialHeading: How to read & drive the screen
contextCompression.tutorialBody: Keep or paste an LLM-input prompt, then click COMPRESS: the compacted text, the reduction ratio and the reversible dictionary (handle) appear. Click RETRIEVE: Retrieve re-expands the handle to the original, and the 'lossless' badge proves on screen that the round-trip returns the original (CCR reversibility). Everything is computed by the pure twin (deterministic, no LLM) — the same one the Go port runs.
contextCompression.losslessFail: LOSS: Retrieve differs from the original
contextCompression.footer: Determinism-first: compression is a pure function (lib/context-compressor.ts), the twin of the Go port (back/runtime/context). The wall: the port reads the prompt, writes no truth; it extends the margin under the cap, never relieves it.
contextCompression.gateInvariantOk: Invariant: same verdict before / after compression
contextCompression.replayHeading: Loop economy (HR04) — wired in front of GenerateAction
contextCompression.replaySameVerdicts: Same action verdicts with and without compression
contextCompression.replayFitsUnderCap: fits under the cap thanks to compression

compound.title: Compound — capturing the 1st goal makes the 2nd cheaper
compound.subtitle: CE01 spike · go/no-go
compound.intro: The CE01 spike MEASURES the compound-engineering claim: does capturing a finished goal's pattern reduce the effort/tokens of a SECOND, SIMILAR goal? Two goals (order-archive → invoice-archive) are decomposed into work-units; the shareable units are REPLAYED (procedural recall from a KindProcedural memory entry + behavior-macro expansion, §24.6) instead of being re-derived. The verdict is COMPUTED (never declared) against a declared floor, with a dissimilar control as a false-positive guard. Spike-confined, read-only (the wall) — it writes no truth.
compound.tutorialHeading: How to read & drive the screen
compound.tutorialBody: Click MEASURE THE DELTA to run the pure twin decide() — the same function the Go probe runs, no LLM, no clock. The badge is the verdict: green GO (the floor is cleared AND the dissimilar control stays under its ceiling AND the measurement is reproducible) or red NO-GO. The similar-pair card shows goal-2's tokens WITHOUT capture vs WITH capture, the saved tokens, the reduction %, and the reuse split (how many units came back via procedural recall vs behavior-macro expansion). The dissimilar control shows that capture does NOT manufacture a saving where no motif is shared.
compound.pending: No measurement yet — click MEASURE THE DELTA.
compound.exampleBody: Both goals add an `archive` operation to a kernel entity with the same mirror form (a fixture), the same projection (Go + TS), the same UI control and the same sensors — they differ only in the intrinsic operation (Order vs Invoice). Capturing goal-1's motif lets goal-2 replay 6 shareable units (its 1800-token write_operation stays derived in full — no fabricated reuse), cutting goal-2 from 7800 to 1940 tokens (75.1%). The unrelated migration goal shares only load_context_pack → 16.6%, under the 20% ceiling. Verdict: GO → proceed to CE02 (the capitalisation loop, via the wall).
compound.boundaryIntro: CE01 said GO. CE02 graves the DECISION: what is capitalised, through which channel, and the frontier. Click SHOW THE BOUNDARY to replay the declared table (the pure twin of back/runtime/compound) — 2 CAPITALISED motifs (procedural recall + behavior-macro), both VIA THE WALL and WITHOUT touching the fitness; 3 FORBIDDEN frontiers. The decision is pinned to an accepted ADR (0038) by a parity mirror.

boundary.heading: Capitalisation boundary (CE02 declared table)
boundary.fitnessSafeBadge: No capitalisation touches the fitness (≠ learning criteria)
boundary.pending: Boundary not shown — click SHOW THE BOUNDARY.

compound.gestureIntro: CE02 graved the decision; CE03 EXECUTES it. At a GREEN goal's close, the /compound gesture CAPITALISES the durable motif via the wall: the GESTURE motif becomes a procedural memory entry (KindProcedural, S31) and the SPEC motif becomes a candidate behavior-macro proposed via firewall.ViaIdea (draft idea → mirror → /goal). Click RUN /compound to replay the gesture (the pure twin of back/runtime/compound) — a green goal produces 1 procedural entry + 1 draft idea, NO kernel write (the wall).

gesture.heading: Capitalisation gesture (green goal → 2 events)
gesture.behaviorHeading: Event 2 — candidate behavior-macro (draft idea, via the wall)

compound.expansionIntro: A behavior attached to an entity expands (pure function, dry-run, idempotent) into attributes/relations/operations/policies/fixtures — "don't rewrite the owner-scoping boilerplate for the 50th time". The expansion writes NO truth; it is frozen later via /goal (the wall).

expansion.heading: Behavior-macro expansion (§24.6) — dry-run, pure function
expansion.pending: Pick a behavior + an entity, then click "Expand" to see the dry-run.

compound.footer: CE01 · roadmap-compound spike-gate · the spike MEASURES, it writes no truth (the wall holds) · capitalisation later flows via firewall.ViaIdea → idea → mirror → /goal, never the fitness · reproduce: cd spike/compound && go test ./... && go run ./cmd/verdict

compoundingSection.heading: Compounding — a subsequent similar goal reuses what an earlier goal capitalised
compoundingSection.intro: The capitalisation loop CLOSES here (CE05). CE03 CAPTURED a green goal's motif (a procedural recall + a candidate behavior-macro), CE04 EXPANDS it (pure dry-run), and CE05 REUSES it on the NEXT similar goal — its effort/tokens DROP. Click « Route the next goal (similar) »: the pure router (the twin of back/runtime/compound/reuse.go) routes each of the next goal's work-units against the capitalised corpus — every shared unit is REPLAYED (procedural recall below the line, or behavior expansion VIA THE WALL) instead of re-derived. The « dissimilar » control proves the anti-false-positive frontier: a goal with no shared motif reuses NOTHING. Determinism-first: routing is a NAME MATCH, never an LLM. The wall: the router READS the corpus + recalls below the line, it writes NO truth.
compoundingSection.pending: Not routed yet — click « Route the next goal ».
compoundingSection.wallNote: The router READS the capitalised corpus and RECALLS below the line — NO kernel write. Reusing a behavior recalls its shape, but FREEZING it still goes idea → mirror → /goal (the CE04 expansion is a dry-run).

governance.title: Governance — OWASP Agentic Top-10 cross-check
governance.intro: GV01: a deterministic audit of AIDOS agent governance (S52 agentlayer; BA13 GateAction + enforcers; BA29 ledger) against the 10 OWASP Agentic risks and the Microsoft agent-governance-toolkit pillars. The report is a DECLARED table — code, never an LLM judgment. The structural wall stays authoritative: the AGT AUGMENTS it, never replaces it.
governance.wallNote: The fail-closed structural wall already covers 8/10 risks. No pillar is adopted as a REPLACEMENT of the wall — only as a proven augmentation.
governance.adrHeading: ADR 0037 — AGT adoption: what we adopt / do not adopt
governance.ledgerNote: Each entry chains the prior root: altering, deleting or reordering a row changes the root → verification goes red. Append-only, deterministic, below the waterline (the AGT augments the wall, it does not replace it).
governance.complianceAllGreen: All green on the current state
governance.complianceNote: Each risk has a mirror, anchored on the real enforcer. On the current state the forbidden action is refused → green. Injecting the matching violation (degraded enforcer) lets it escape → red: proof the enforcer is load-bearing. Deterministic, below the waterline.
governance.policyEquivLabel: Equivalence — per-action verdict (reference vs tighter policy)
governance.policyNeverWidens: The tighter policy never widens the reference verdict.
governance.policyNote: The YAML policy is the declared SOURCE; it compiles to the same fail-closed enforcers (GateAction). Equivalence: for any action the policy yields exactly the same verdict/BlockReason as the Go enforcers. Tighten: a policy can only EQUAL or TIGHTEN the reference surface — any declaration that WIDENS it (a host/path/tool/skill outside the reference, a raised cap) is REJECTED at compile. The wall stays authoritative, below the waterline.
governance.sreTrustHeading: Trust chain (identity bound to the GV03 Merkle root)
governance.sreNote: The error budget and the circuit-breaker are PURE functions of the run stream (a budget IS a count, a breaker IS a threshold on an observed rate) — never an "SRE agent". Fail-closed: a failure never improves the budget nor re-closes an open breaker. Identity (the agent + impl that decided) is BOUND to the GV03 tamper-evident root — never floating. Augmentation, not replacement: the structural wall stays the garant, below the waterline (writes no truth).

ingestion.title: Document→markdown ingestion
ingestion.subtitle: DocConverter port
ingestion.intro: AIDOS's ingestion frontier: convert a document to markdown, deterministically and idempotently — same file → same markdown, byte-for-byte. The DocConverter port (ADR 0039) is REPLACEABLE: the concrete tool (microsoft/markitdown at MK03) plugs behind the same interface. The markdown becomes a candidate-truth (an idea draft), never a kernel write.
ingestion.tutorialBody: Paste an HTML document, then click CONVERT: the markdown appears with its idempotence badge. Click again (RE-CONVERT): the bytes are identical. Click PROPOSE AN IDEA: the markdown is wrapped as a candidate-truth (status=draft) — a preview of what idea-intake will capture at MK03. Nothing is frozen: the wall holds.
