ingestion.draftWallNote: The wall: ingestion proposes a candidate-truth (status=draft); it never freezes. The only door to truth stays idea → mirror → /goal → human approval.
ingestion.pending: No markdown yet. Click CONVERT to run the DocConverter port.
ingestion.footer: MK02 · DocConverter — replaceable ingestion frontier (ADR 0039), deterministic & idempotent. The port reads the document, writes no truth (the wall).

besoinNecessity.title: Necessity — must the need follow the architecture?
besoinNecessity.subtitle: EL01 spike · go/no-go
besoinNecessity.intro: The EL01 spike PROVES a free-text box (today's S64 "capture your idea") is insufficient. The SAME need — the S46 demo checkout, "a customer places an order from their cart" — is captured TWO ways: a top-down rung-by-rung BesoinGraph (product→journey→view→control→action→operation→entity) with a forcing gate, vs a flat prompt. Is the graph's emitted Idea backlog STRICTLY richer/ordered than the flat prompt? The verdict is COMPUTED (never declared), reproducible (pure function, no LLM).
besoinNecessity.tutorialHeading: How to read & drive this screen
besoinNecessity.tutorialBody: Click "Compare both captures": the panel runs the pure decide() twin (identical to the Go probe spike/besoin) and shows a GO/NO-GO badge, a side-by-side richness table (BesoinGraph vs flat prompt), the strict-dominance deltas, the computed rationale, and the HARVESTED anchor Idea as a DRAFT (no mirror, no frozen version — the wall). Nothing is written: confined spike, read-only.
besoinNecessity.goBadge: GO — the need MUST follow the architecture
besoinNecessity.pending: No comparison run yet. Click "Compare both captures" to run the pure twin.
besoinNecessity.tableHeading: Backlog richness: BesoinGraph vs free-text box
besoinNecessity.exampleHeading: The worked example — the S46 demo checkout
besoinNecessity.exampleBody: On "a customer places an order from their cart", the BesoinGraph emits 5 ordered Ideas (product→control→action→operation→entity), refs resolving @rung, each typed with the 4 metadata and carrying its anchors; journey/view are 2 NoEmit nodes seeding anchors without emitting an Idea (never a silent journey→product cast). The flat prompt yields just 1 undifferentiated, untyped candidate with no order and no edge — everything else the agent would have to guess (a prompt→code shortcut the wall forbids).
besoinNecessity.footer: EL01 spike — /spike confined, ratchet OFF, T0, throwaway. No kernel/mirrors/fitness write (the wall). The lesson is harvested as a DRAFT Idea (no mirror, no version) — promotion is /goal later. EL02+ builds the real back/runtime/besoin package.

besoinGrammar.title: BesoinLevel grammar — the 7 SOURCE rungs + transversal bands
besoinGrammar.subtitle: EL02 · runtime/besoin
besoinGrammar.intro: EL02 freezes the CLOSED BesoinLevel grammar: the 7 SOURCE rungs of the KRD §23 verticale (product→journey→view→control→action→operation→entity) in TOTAL order, plus the 2 transversal bands (invariant ∀, policy attached to operation/entity — settled in EL02: policy is a band, not a vertical rung). Each rung names its required fields and its outgoing reference. Everything is a pure function (determinism); an out-of-grammar level is a HARD refusal. Above the wall: no truth write.
besoinGrammar.tutorialHeading: How to read and drive the screen
besoinGrammar.tutorialBody: Click "List the grammar": the panel runs the pure twin (identical to the Go authority back/runtime/besoin) and renders the total order of the 7 SOURCE rungs (with NextLevel + outgoing reference + required fields), the 2 transversal bands, and the 3 layers DELIBERATELY out-of-grammar-v1 (saga/temporal/globalinvariant — a declared OpenQuestion, never aliased). Then type a level and click "Parse the level": a valid level resolves; an out-of-grammar string is refused HARD; saga/temporal/globalinvariant are refused as out-of-scope.
besoinGrammar.pending: Click "List the grammar" to compute the closed order.
besoinGrammar.oosHeading: Out-of-grammar v1 (declared OpenQuestion — refused, never aliased)
besoinGrammar.parseHeading: Parse a level (hard refusal of out-of-grammar)
besoinGrammar.parseOutOfScope: Refused — out of scope v1 (declared OpenQuestion)
besoinGrammar.footer: EL02 — CLOSED grammar, total order, pure functions (determinism §6/§8). invariant/policy are transversal bands (never vertical rungs). saga/temporal/globalinvariant out-of-grammar-v1 (declared OpenQuestion). No kernel/mirrors/fitness write (the wall); EL03+ builds the graph on top of this grammar.

besoinGraph.title: Need graph — ordered, append-only, content-addressed record
besoinGraph.subtitle: EL03 · runtime/besoin
besoinGraph.intro: EL03 freezes the BesoinGraph record: an ORDERED, append-only set of LevelNodes (one per rung) + constrains(L→L+1)/seeds(L names a deeper need) edges, content-addressed via records.Hash(Canonicalize(graph)) — NEVER a forked hash, the same S01/S02 scheme as the kernel. By construction NO Version field, NO Mirror field: that double absence IS what makes it a need above the wall, never a truth. Everything is a pure function (determinism §6/§8): same answers → same graph_hash regardless of order.
besoinGraph.tutorialHeading: How to read and drive the screen
besoinGraph.tutorialBody: Add nodes (a rung + a body + a status) with "Add node": the panel runs the pure twin (identical to the Go authority back/runtime/besoin/graph.go) and recomputes the graph_hash. Click "Compute graph_hash": a 64-char SHA-256 hex. Click "Re-sort (reverse order)": the hash DOES NOT CHANGE — the address is insertion-order-independent. Change the project and click "Compare projects": two distinct projects have DISJOINT hashes. The "Double absence" panel proves no version/mirror key ever appears in the canonical body (the wall).
besoinGraph.absenceHeading: Double absence (the wall) — no Version/Mirror field
besoinGraph.empty: No node yet. Add a rung to build the graph.
besoinGraph.pending: Add ≥1 node then compute the graph_hash.
besoinGraph.reorderSame: Identical hash after reverse re-insertion — addressing is order-independent (determinism).
besoinGraph.reorderDiff: FAIL — the hash changed with order (should never happen).
besoinGraph.compareDisjoint: DISJOINT hashes — two distinct projects never collide (isolation).
besoinGraph.compareCollide: FAIL — hash collision between distinct projects (should never happen).
besoinGraph.absenceOk: The canonical body carries NO version/mirror key — it is a need, not a truth (the wall).
besoinGraph.absenceFail: FAIL — a version/mirror key is present (wall violation).
besoinGraph.dupRefused: Refused — a node already exists for that rung (overwrite goes through a ChangeSet, §9).
besoinGraph.footer: EL03 — content-addressed record (records.Hash reused, never forked), append-only, non-destructive (§9), no Version nor Mirror (double absence = the wall). Same answers → same graph_hash; projects disjoint. Above the idea-intake door, never a kernel/mirrors/fitness write. EL15 persists it as JSONB in the besoin schema; EL19 drives it as a wizard.

besoinMetadata.title: Need metadata
besoinMetadata.subtitle: truthtyping · scope · authority
besoinMetadata.intro: EL04 attaches the four per-truth metadata to every BesoinGraph node, reusing the three distinct packages that carry them: truth_kind + verifiability (truthtyping), scope (scope), authority (authority). The canonical truth_kind is truthtyping's — a single enum source, which authority delegates to. Everything stays above the wall: these metadata qualify a need, they never freeze it into a truth.
besoinMetadata.tutorialBody: Choose the node status then its four metadata and click "Certify". A node with no truth_kind is incomplete; an "unverifiable" verifiability routes to /spike (idea_capture → idea_grill → idea_spike); an active node with no scope (nor global "*") is incomplete; a regulatory node with no legal approval is incomplete (authority's done case). "Prove the single enum source" shows truthtyping and authority share the same truth_kind enum.
besoinMetadata.complete: Complete — all four metadata present and certifiable
besoinMetadata.incomplete: Incomplete — at least one metadata is missing or not certifiable
besoinMetadata.routeKernel: Kernel zone (freezable later, via /goal below the wall)
besoinMetadata.coherenceOk: Coherent — truthtyping and authority share the enum, no fork
besoinMetadata.footer: EL04 — above the wall, read-only against truth. The metadata qualify a need (never a Version or Mirror field). Deterministic: same metadata → same verdict.

besoinProposes.title: The LevelToProposes table
besoinProposes.subtitle: level → ProposesKind | NoEmit
besoinProposes.intro: EL05 declares the honest join between the BesoinGraph grammar (9 levels) and the EXISTING closed set ideas.ProposesKinds() (control · policy · operation · action · entity · product). control/action/operation/entity/product and the policy band self-map — self-mapping is the only legal emission. journey, view and invariant are NoEmit: they have no legal Proposes target; they seed anchors instead of emitting. No silent alias (journey→product is forbidden, view→view* impossible). A closed table is a pure deterministic function, never an LLM choice, above the wall.
besoinProposes.tutorialBody: Pick a level then click “Map the level”: the table returns Emit<kind> or NoEmit. “Prove the honest join” checks that every Emit target is a member of the closed set ideas.ProposesKinds() AND that no level aliases another. “Test an out-of-grammar level” proves an out-of-grammar string (saga, temporal…) is a hard error, never an alias.
besoinProposes.joinOk: Honest — every Emit ∈ closed set, no silent alias
besoinProposes.joinFail: Failed — an alias or a target outside the closed set
besoinProposes.checkHardError: Hard error — out of grammar, no mapping (never an alias)
besoinProposes.checkValid: Valid level — carries a declared mapping
besoinProposes.footer: EL05 — above the wall, read-only against truth. The table decides only the Proposes target; it emits no Idea (EL16 does, via the idea-intake door) and writes no truth. Deterministic: same level → same mapping.

besoinThresholds.title: BesoinThresholds & OptionSpace
besoinThresholds.subtitle: declared thresholds · enumerable metric
besoinThresholds.intro: EL06 declares TWO above-the-wall capabilities, never learned (§8). (1) BesoinThresholds: ONE content-addressed record holding every gate threshold (the product's ≤5 scenarios; the per-rung required fields, sourced from the grammar, never a second copy). EL07 (CanDescend) and EL11 (the Stop hook) read the SAME record — no threshold inlined twice, no drift. (2) OptionSpace(L, L+1): the declared enumerable metric per adjacent rung pair — the CLOSED countable set of choices the lower rung admits. |OptionSpace| is an integer computed by a pure function (never an LLM judgment). A non-enumerable pair is a DECLARED OpenQuestion (size -1), never fabricated to 0.
besoinThresholds.tutorialHeading: Try the thresholds and the metric
besoinThresholds.tutorialBody: "Load thresholds" shows the declared record (max_scenarios + per-level required fields) and its content-addressed hash. "Prove the single source" checks the record's required fields == the grammar's (no second copy). "Count the OptionSpace" computes |OptionSpace(L→L+1)| for the chosen pair: a positive integer for an enumerable pair, the sentinel -1 (OpenQuestion) for a non-enumerable pair — never a fabricated 0.
besoinThresholds.sourceOk: Single source — the record's required fields == the grammar, no second copy
besoinThresholds.sourceFail: Drift detected — a second copy diverges
besoinThresholds.countEnumerable: Enumerable — a positive integer counted over the declared set
besoinThresholds.footer: EL06 — above-the-wall config, read-only against truth. Thresholds declared, never learned (§8); OptionSpace = a pure count over a closed set. EL07/EL11 read the same record; EL08 counts ShrinkOptionSpace over this set. No truth write. Deterministic: same inputs → same outputs (byte-identical hash on the Go and TS sides).

besoinCanDescend.title: CanDescend — the per-level forcing gate
besoinCanDescend.subtitle: enough is COMPUTED, never declared
besoinCanDescend.intro: EL07 is the PURE forcing function CanDescend(graph, level) → Verdict{enough, missing, openQuestions, blockReasons}. A level is descendable iff: (a) its body is statable AND non-vacant (the rung's required fields + parse rules), (b) its four metadata are present/certifiable (EL04), (c) its outgoing ref resolves @version, and (e) ANTI-VACUITY: ShrinkOptionSpace(graph, level) > 0 — a parsable level that narrows nothing is not_enough (anti-gaming). A gap toward a deeper, not-yet-existing rung is a carried OpenQuestion with enough=true (bootstrap §6), never a blocking residual. enough is COMPUTED by the code, never declared by the user or the LLM (anti-Goodhart §8).
besoinCanDescend.tutorialBody: Pick a body shape and run "Compute the verdict": a right-sized, narrowing body is enough; a parsable-but-non-constraining body is not_enough (anti-vacuity). "Count the shrink" shows |OptionSpace| pruned by the body's selects — 0 means it constrains nothing. The operation→entity case shows a forward dependency: a carried OpenQuestion, enough=true. Every verdict is computed by the deterministic twin, never an LLM.
besoinCanDescend.caseVacant: product · parses but selects nothing (anti-vacuity → not_enough)
besoinCanDescend.caseForwardDep: operation · entity not yet declared (forward dep → carried OpenQuestion)
besoinCanDescend.enoughTrue: enough = true — the level is right-sized; descent is allowed
besoinCanDescend.enoughFalse: enough = false — not_enough; the level is held until the fix path is walked
besoinCanDescend.shrinkPositive: > 0 — narrows the lower rung's OptionSpace (anti-vacuity satisfied)
besoinCanDescend.footer: EL07 — the gate reads only the BesoinGraph (the wall); it writes no truth. enough is COMPUTED from the five gates, never declared (anti-Goodhart §8). It consumes ShrinkOptionSpace (EL06/EL08) as the anti-vacuity gate condition, not as mere display. Deterministic: same (graph, level, metadata) → same verdict (lib/besoin-candescend.ts is the byte-equivalent twin of back/runtime/besoin/candescend.go).

besoinBranchTree.title: BranchTree — the deterministic per-level decision tree
besoinBranchTree.subtitle: resolved is COMPUTED ; altitude by schema-mismatch
besoinBranchTree.intro: EL12 is the deterministic, code-authoritative per-level decision tree (the missing Example-Mapping, built above the wall). BranchTree(level, body) → the CLOSED set of branches to close for resolved (one branch per EL06 required field, plus the per-rung parse rule, plus the EL07.e anti-vacuity branch), each annotated whether the body CLOSES it. IsResolved = all branches closed AND anti-vacuity satisfied — COMPUTED, never declared. Altitude classification is a deterministic SCHEMA-MISMATCH: an answer is routed to the level whose schema it satisfies; an entity attribute submitted at the product level FAILS the product schema (a declared field set), this is NOT an LLM opinion of altitude.
besoinBranchTree.tutorialBody: Pick a fixture (level + body) then "Build the tree": a complete body closes every branch (resolved); an incomplete body leaves ≥1 branch open with its how_to_fix; a parsable-but-non-constraining product leaves the anti-vacuity branch open. "Classify altitude" runs the schema-mismatch classification: an entity body submitted at the product level is OFF-altitude (fails the product schema) and is classified at entity. Each verdict is computed by the deterministic twin, never an LLM.
besoinBranchTree.caseProductComplete: product · complete body (all branches closed → resolved)
besoinBranchTree.caseProductVacant: product · parses but selects nothing (anti-vacuity branch open)
besoinBranchTree.caseEntityAtProduct: entity · attributes body submitted AT the product level (off-altitude)
besoinBranchTree.caseOperationForwardDep: operation · entity not yet declared (anti-vacuity carried)
besoinBranchTree.resolvedTrue: resolved = true — every branch is closed; the level is right-sized
besoinBranchTree.resolvedFalse: resolved = false — at least one branch is still open
besoinBranchTree.antiVacuityTrue: satisfied — the level narrows the lower rung's option space
besoinBranchTree.antiVacuityFalse: unsatisfied — the body parses but constrains nothing (anti-gaming)
besoinBranchTree.offAltitudeTrue: off-altitude — the body does NOT match the claimed level's schema (field mismatch)
besoinBranchTree.offAltitudeFalse: on-altitude — the body satisfies the claimed level's schema
besoinBranchTree.unmatched: none (the body matches no level's schema)
besoinBranchTree.footer: EL12 — the tree, the resolved verdict and the altitude classification are PURE functions; the LLM never enters. Altitude classification is a deterministic schema-mismatch (a declared field set), not a judgment. ABOVE the wall: BranchTree feeds Idea.Intent / the /grill triage, never a kernel write. Deterministic: same (level, body) → same tree (lib/besoin-branchtree.ts is the byte-equivalent twin of back/runtime/besoin/branchtree.go).

besoinCascade.title: Anchor cascade — the measured constraint inheritance
besoinCascade.subtitle: |OptionSpace| strictly smaller under a frozen anchor
besoinCascade.intro: EL08 adds the three pieces that turn the EL07 verdict into the COMPOUND. AnchorsAbove(graph, level) = the FROZEN list of `resolved` rungs strictly above (the single readable grounding the rung below reads). Descend(graph, fromLevel) opens L+1 only when CanDescend(fromLevel).enough — a premature descent is REFUSED (CANNOT_DESCEND_LEVEL_NOT_RIGHTSIZED), never an opinion. ShrinkOptionSpaceCascade(graph, level) measures |OptionSpace| BEFORE vs AFTER the frozen anchors: under a frozen anchor the count is STRICTLY smaller (the compounding); with no frozen anchor it does not narrow (Shrink 0 — the compounding failed). Re-opening a frozen anchor is NOT an edit: it is a recorded DECISION (ChangeSet); a silent rewrite is refused (BESOIN_ANCHOR_OVERWRITE, anti-overwrite §9).
besoinCascade.tutorialBody: Pick a node set, then: "List the anchors" shows the frozen grounding above; "Descend" opens the lower rung when right-sized, REFUSES otherwise; "Measure the shrink" shows Before/After/Shrink — under a frozen anchor After < Before (strictly); "Reopen the anchor" requires a ChangeSet token — without it the reopen is refused. Every verdict is computed by the deterministic twin, never an LLM.
besoinCascade.caseFrozenVacant: frozen product but selects nothing (descent refused)
besoinCascade.caseDraftingProduct: drafting product (not frozen → does not narrow)
besoinCascade.descendOk: OK — the level is right-sized; the lower rung is opened
besoinCascade.shrinkStrict: > 0 — |OptionSpace| STRICTLY smaller under the frozen anchor (the compounding)
besoinCascade.shrinkNone: 0 — not narrowed (no frozen anchor: the compounding did not happen)
besoinCascade.reopenOk: OK — reopen recorded (decision traced, frozen body preserved)
besoinCascade.footer: EL08 — the cascade reads only the BesoinGraph (the wall); it writes no truth. Descent is gated by the COMPUTED EL07 verdict; |OptionSpace| under a frozen anchor is a counted integer, never an LLM judgment; reopening an anchor requires a ChangeSet (anti-overwrite §9). Deterministic: same nodes → same cascade (lib/besoin-cascade.ts is the byte-equivalent twin of back/runtime/besoin/cascade.go).

besoinCompleteness.title: Need completeness — the completeness law applied to the NEED
besoinCompleteness.subtitle: a resolved level without its level-mirror = monster
besoinCompleteness.intro: EL09 applies the completeness law (S06) to the NEED. BesoinCompleteness(graph, mirrors) → { complete, monsters[] }: every `resolved` node must carry its right-form level-mirror (LevelMirrorForm) AND its four live metadata; no level-mirror may be an orphan. Breaking the node↔level-mirror link one way (removing the mirror) raises NEED_LEVEL_WITHOUT_MIRROR; the other way (a mirror reflecting no resolved node) raises ORPHAN_NEED_MIRROR. Detection is a PURE FUNCTION (counting + matching), never an LLM. No real mirror is written (those are written below the wall by the app-builder via /goal) — above-the-wall.
besoinCompleteness.tutorialBody: Click “Check completeness”: the intact link is complete (no monster). “Break link (remove mirror)” removes the resolved node’s mirror → NEED_LEVEL_WITHOUT_MIRROR. “Break link (orphan mirror)” adds a mirror reflecting no resolved node → ORPHAN_NEED_MIRROR. “Reset” restores the intact link. Every verdict is computed by the deterministic twin; nothing is judged by an LLM.
besoinCompleteness.footer: EL09: monster detection is a pure function (counting + matching); no real mirror is written; everything stays above the wall. The TypeScript twin (lib/besoin-completeness.ts) is byte-equivalent to the Go authority (back/runtime/besoin/completeness.go).

besoinMirrorform.eyebrow: EL10 · Mirror form per level + view/journey validators
besoinMirrorform.title: Mirror form per level — LevelMirrorForm + view/journey validators
besoinMirrorform.subtitle: the expected form per rung, for the rungs derive-mirror does not cover
besoinMirrorform.intro: EL10 builds the new table LevelMirrorForm(level) → MirrorForm: the expected mirror form for EVERY rung. For the 5 rungs the derive-mirror skill already covers (entity/policy/operation/control/action) the table DELEGATES (same form, zero fork — a property pins the agreement). For the 3 above-the-wall rungs derive-mirror does NOT know (product/journey/view) it carries the freshly-declared form. EL10 also ships the NEW deterministic validators for view (goal + named zones + named data) and journey (parseable Gherkin) — because no Go package backs view/journey (the view/action skills assist the dialogue, they do NOT provide the validator). Everything is a pure function; no mirror is written — above the wall.
besoinMirrorform.tutorialBody: The table shows the expected mirror form of each rung; the "delegated" badge marks the 5 rungs derive-mirror covers, "declared" the 3 above-the-wall rungs. Edit a view or journey body, then click "Validate": the deterministic validator returns valid/invalid. "Break zones" empties the view's zones (a screen with no zone fails); "Break Gherkin" replaces the scenario with free text (without Given/When/Then it fails). "Reset" restores a well-formed body. Each verdict is computed by the deterministic twin; nothing is judged by an LLM.
besoinMirrorform.viewHeading: View validator (new) — goal + named zones + data
besoinMirrorform.footer: EL10: the LevelMirrorForm table + the view/journey validators are pure functions; for the 5 covered rungs, the output ≡ derive-mirror (no fork); no mirror is written — above the wall. The TypeScript twin (lib/besoin-completeness.ts) is byte-equivalent to the Go authority (back/runtime/besoin/{mirrorform,validators}.go).

besoinGate.eyebrow: EL11 · Stop:besoin-gate hook — the descent gate
besoinGate.title: Stop:besoin-gate — the descent forcing gate
besoinGate.subtitle: an OR between ¬enough and monster, scoped to BesoinGraph sessions
besoinGate.intro: EL11 ships the Stop:besoin-gate hook, a Go binary DISTINCT from the existing back/hooks/stop (which reads kernel completeness over the mirrors schema). At turn close it refuses a level's DESCENT (or its promotion to an Idea) iff, for the current rung, the level is NOT right-sized (¬CanDescend.enough, EL07) OR carries a need-completeness monster (EL09). It is an OR, not an AND: the two failure modes are independent, each blocks on its own. The hook is SCOPED to sessions with an OPEN BesoinGraph — without one it is a no-op (a hook that fired on every session would be the dead/over-firing hook, §5). The verdict is COMPUTED from EL07 + EL09, never an LLM judgment; the hook REINFORCES the wall (it adds a guard, never removes one — meta-loop §5).
besoinGate.tutorialBody: The state shows the current session (BesoinGraph attached? current level, metadata complete?, level-mirror present?). Click "Evaluate the gate": the deterministic twin computes the verdict (no-op, allow, or block) and shows the two OR flags. "Break right-sizing" drops the current rung's metadata → ¬enough (disjunct 1). "Break the level-mirror" removes the resolved rung's mirror → monster (disjunct 2). "Detach the BesoinGraph" drops the session → no-op (the §5 scoping). "Reset" restores a right-sized, monster-free session. Every verdict is computed; nothing is judged by an LLM.
besoinGate.verdictNoOp: No-op — no open BesoinGraph (the hook does not fire, §5)
besoinGate.verdictAllow: Allowed — the current rung is right-sized AND monster-free
besoinGate.verdictBlock: Blocked — the descent is refused (the OR fired)
besoinGate.footer: EL11: the hook verdict is computed by the pure functions CanDescend (EL07) + BesoinCompleteness (EL09), never an LLM; an OR (not an AND) between ¬enough and monster; no-op without a BesoinGraph (anti-over-firing §5); the hook reinforces the wall — it reads the BesoinGraph above the line and writes no truth (§2). The TypeScript twin (lib/besoin-gate.ts) composes the EL07/EL09 twins and is byte-equivalent to the Go authority (back/hooks/stop/besoin-gate/gate.go).

besoinInterview.title: /compound-besoin — the level-by-level forced interview
besoinInterview.subtitle: the LLM leads, the code judges
besoinInterview.intro: EL13 is the umbrella skill /compound-besoin: the need interview, one level at a time. The LLM is the barricaded exception (§8) — it LEADS the dialogue (phrases the question, paraphrases the utterance) — but every verdict is a PURE authoritative function, the LLM defers to the code: enterableLevel computes the enterable level (the forcing: a level opens only when its parent is enough); dispatchOf is the closed gesture table (grill/view/action/generic); recordAnswer decides the routing by CODE — an off-altitude answer is rejected by SCHEMA (EL12), a fuzzy answer is routed to /spike (idea_capture → idea_grill → idea_spike, never a descent), otherwise it is recorded and the resolved verdict is COMPUTED (CanDescend.enough), never declared by the LLM.
besoinInterview.tutorialBody: Pick an answer (the fixture mimics an utterance paraphrased by the LLM) then "Record the answer": a sharp product answer closes its branches → resolved; a fuzzy (unverifiable) answer is routed to /spike via the legal three-hop gate, never a descent; an entity attributes body submitted at the product level is rejected by schema (off-altitude); a product that parses but selects nothing is recorded yet not resolved (anti-vacuity). "Enterable level" computes the rung to work + the dispatched gesture. Every verdict is computed by the deterministic twin, never an LLM.
besoinInterview.caseProductSharp: product · sharp answer (closes the branches → resolved)
besoinInterview.caseEntityAtProduct: entity · attributes body submitted AT the product level (off-altitude, schema rejection)
besoinInterview.caseProductVacant: product · parses but selects nothing (recorded, not resolved)
besoinInterview.routingHeading: The recorded turn (routing + COMPUTED resolved verdict)
besoinInterview.routingRecord: record — the answer satisfies the schema and is recorded
besoinInterview.routingOffAltitude: off_altitude — the answer fails the level schema (field-set mismatch, EL12)
besoinInterview.routingSpike: spike — the answer is fuzzy: routed to /spike, never a descent
besoinInterview.resolvedTrue: resolved = true — all branches closed (COMPUTED by CanDescend, never declared)
besoinInterview.resolvedFalse: resolved = false — at least one branch remains open (COMPUTED)
besoinInterview.enterableHeading: Enterable level + dispatched gesture (the forcing made visible)
besoinInterview.enterableLabel: Enterable level (first rung not yet enough)
besoinInterview.footer: EL13 — the LLM-led, code-judged interview: enterableLevel, dispatchOf, recordAnswer and the resolved verdict are PURE functions; the LLM never enters. An off-altitude answer is rejected by schema (EL12), a fuzzy answer routed to /spike (idea_capture → idea_grill → idea_spike). ABOVE the wall: the interview writes no truth — its output is the BesoinGraph to be appended via the EL15 MCP. The TypeScript twin (lib/besoin-interview.ts) composes the EL12/EL07 twins and is byte-equivalent to the Go authority (back/runtime/besoin/interview.go).

besoinInvariant.title: /besoin-invariant — the lateral band of invariants ∀ and policies
besoinInvariant.subtitle: constrained laterally; the human states the ∀, the code judges
besoinInvariant.intro: EL14 is the transversal band /besoin-invariant: the interview of the invariants ∀ that CROSS every level ("true on all paths") and the policies where authorization is in play. It is the lateral counterpart of the vertical interview (EL13). The human STATES the invariant; the code only records and classifies it (the circularity ban, §8 — the skill cannot author a ∀ it would then satisfy). An ∃ (a single example) is refused (INVARIANT_IS_EXAMPLE_NOT_FORALL); an invariant attached at a rung constrains that rung AND every rung above it; a policy band emits AT MOST ONE Idea{Proposes:policy} via the legal idea_capture door; a path-independent invariant emits none. Every verdict is a PURE function, the LLM defers to the code.
besoinInvariant.tutorialBody: Pick a case (the fixture mimics a human-stated invariant) then "Record the invariant": a ∀ attached at operation is recorded and constrains every rung above; an ∃ (an example) is refused by schema; a policy band emits exactly one Idea{Proposes:policy}; self-authoring is refused (circularity ban). "Crossed levels" shows the lateral constraint set. "Band completeness" flags a resolved rung that requires a crossing invariant but is crossed by none. Every verdict is computed by the deterministic twin, never an LLM.
besoinInvariant.caseInvariantForall: invariant · ∀ attached at operation (recorded, constrains every rung above)
besoinInvariant.casePolicyBand: policy · band attached at operation (one Idea{Proposes:policy})
besoinInvariant.selfAuthoredLabel: Self-authored by the skill (the circularity ban must refuse)
besoinInvariant.routingHeading: The recorded turn (routing + the lateral constraint)
besoinInvariant.routingRecord: record — the band is a ∀, attached to a valid rung, and recorded
besoinInvariant.routingOffAltitude: off_altitude — the band is an ∃ / a bad attachment / self-authored (refused)
besoinInvariant.routingSpike: spike — the band is fuzzy: routed to /spike, never recorded
besoinInvariant.crossedHeading: Crossed levels (the lateral constraint — every rung the band constrains)
besoinInvariant.policyIdeaHeading: The single Idea{Proposes:policy} (the legal idea_capture guidance)
besoinInvariant.policyIdeaNone: No idea — a path-independent invariant emits NONE (NoEmit; its mirror is a property N1).
besoinInvariant.completenessComplete: complete — every rung requiring a crossing invariant carries one
besoinInvariant.completenessMonster: monster — a resolved rung requires a crossing invariant but is crossed by none
besoinInvariant.footer: EL14 — the lateral band: parseInvariantBand, crossedLevels, recordInvariant and bandCompleteness are PURE functions; the LLM never enters as authority. An ∃ is refused (INVARIANT_IS_EXAMPLE_NOT_FORALL), a self-authored invariant is refused (circularity ban §8). A policy band emits AT MOST ONE Idea{Proposes:policy} via the legal idea_capture door; a ∀ invariant emits none (NoEmit). ABOVE the wall: the band writes no truth. The TypeScript twin (lib/besoin-invariant.ts) is byte-equivalent to the Go authority (back/runtime/besoin/invariant.go).

besoinIntake.title: besoin-intake — the MCP door above the BesoinGraph
besoinIntake.subtitle: a capability door; the code judges, the LLM never enters
besoinIntake.intro: EL15 is the besoin-intake MCP (Go MCP SDK, ADR 0009): the capability door above the BesoinGraph. A human EXPLAINS their app level by level, above the wall; each resolved level leaves as an Idea via the only legal door, idea_capture (EL05). The read/state tools (besoin_graph_state, besoin_level_schema, besoin_list), the per-rung capture tools (besoin_capture_product/_journey/_view/_control/_action/_operation/_entity/_invariant) and the validate tools (besoin_validate_level, besoin_classify) are DETERMINISTIC: no LLM enters the server. A capture on a MAPPING rung emits an Idea; a NoEmit rung (journey/view/invariant) emits NOTHING (no silent cast). ABOVE the wall: the server has NO GRANT on kernel/mirrors/fitness — a kernel write is always refused.
besoinIntake.tutorialHeading: Execute the door from the screen
besoinIntake.tutorialBody: Pick a level then "Read the level schema" (besoin_level_schema): the required fields a client renders + the EL05 mapping (emit:<kind> or no_emit). "Project the capture" shows the level's capture tool and whether it EMITS an Idea (a MAPPING rung) or not (a NoEmit rung — no silent cast). The inventory below enumerates ALL backend tools (one tool = one op, ADR 0009): every capability is reachable from a screen (ui-completeness). Every verdict is computed by the deterministic twin (lib/besoin-intake.ts), byte-identical to the Go MCP.
besoinIntake.schemaHeading: besoin_level_schema (the fields a client renders, inventing none)
besoinIntake.projectionHeading: Capture projection (the tool + does it emit an Idea?)
besoinIntake.toolsHeading: Tool inventory (one tool = one backend op, ADR 0009)
besoinIntake.noEmitNote: NoEmit rung: the capture appends the node and seeds anchors WITHOUT emitting an Idea (no silent cast).
besoinIntake.footer: EL15 — the capability door: besoin_graph_state, besoin_level_schema, the besoin_capture_* and besoin_validate_*/besoin_classify are DETERMINISTIC; no LLM enters the server (the code is the authority). A capture on a MAPPING rung emits an Idea via the legal idea_capture door; a NoEmit rung (journey/view/invariant) emits NOTHING. ABOVE the wall: the server has no GRANT on kernel/mirrors/fitness — a kernel write is always refused (WroteKernel stays false). Projects are isolated by RLS (S55). The TypeScript twin (lib/besoin-intake.ts) is byte-equivalent to the Go MCP (back/mcp/besoin-intake/main.go).

emitIdeas.title: emit-ideas — EmitIdeas(graph) → []Idea
emitIdeas.subtitle: the code judges; governed by the LevelToProposes table (EL05)
emitIdeas.intro: EL16 is the deterministic emitter EmitIdeas(graph) → []Idea, via the idea-intake door, GOVERNED by the closed table LevelToProposes (EL05). For each RESOLVED node whose rung MAPS, one draft Idea is emitted (proposes = LevelToProposes(level), intent = the verbatim utterance, human provenance); NoEmit rungs (journey/view/invariant) emit NOTHING — their constraint lives in the anchors above (no silent cast). The id reuses records.Hash → the Idea is content-addressed + idempotent. The mapping is a pure function, never an LLM choice.
emitIdeas.tutorialHeading: Run the emitter from the screen
emitIdeas.tutorialBody: Shape the already-decided graph by setting each rung's status (empty/drafting/resolved) — by default product + entity are resolved (two mapping rungs → two draft Ideas). Then "Emit the Ideas" runs emitIdeas(nodes) — the besoin_emit_ideas tool: one draft Idea per RESOLVED MAPPING rung, NoEmit rungs excluded. The count EXCLUDES NoEmit rungs and non-resolved rungs. Every verdict is computed by the deterministic twin (lib/emit-ideas.ts), byte-identical to the Go emitter.
emitIdeas.panelIntro: Set each rung's status, then emit: a RESOLVED MAPPING rung projects exactly one draft Idea; a NoEmit rung (journey/view/invariant) or a non-resolved rung emits nothing.
emitIdeas.wallNote: Above the wall: every emitted Idea is a DRAFT candidate — it carries NEITHER a version NOR a mirror (HasMirror always false). The emitter writes no kernel and no mirror.
emitIdeas.handoffNote: Hand-off S64: promotion = writing the mirror via /goal; the goals are opened in the topological backlog order (app-builder).
emitIdeas.footer: EL16 — the deterministic emitter EmitIdeas(graph) → []Idea, governed by the closed table LevelToProposes (EL05). For each RESOLVED MAPPING rung: one draft Idea (human provenance, the verbatim utterance); NoEmit rungs emit nothing (no silent cast). Re-emission is byte-identical (content-addressed, idempotent). ABOVE the wall: no kernel/mirror write, HasMirror always false; promotion = writing the mirror via /goal (hand-off S64). The TypeScript twin (lib/emit-ideas.ts) is byte-equivalent to the Go emitter (back/runtime/besoin/emit_ideas.go) + the besoin_emit_ideas MCP tool.

redBacklog.title: red-backlog — RedBacklog(graph) topo-sorted
redBacklog.subtitle: the code judges; a pure algorithm, never an LLM
redBacklog.intro: EL17 is the ordered RedBacklog for the app-builder (S53+) — "how the doc follows the architecture". RedBacklog(graph) topo-sorts the emitted Ideas (the mapping rungs, EL16) along the constrains/seeds edges → the exact promotion order, exactly the §23 verticale. Each Idea carries its anchors_above (including the NoEmit journey/view rungs that constrain it WITHOUT emitting) and its expected mirror form (LevelMirrorForm, EL10) ANNEXED — never written. An edge cycle is refused (BESOIN_CYCLE). The sort is a pure algorithm (Kahn, deterministic tie-break), never an LLM.
redBacklog.tutorialHeading: Run the topological sort from the screen
redBacklog.tutorialBody: Shape the already-decided graph by setting each rung's status (empty/drafting/resolved) — by default product + entity are resolved (two mapping rungs). Then "Sort the RedBacklog" runs redBacklog(nodes, edges) — the besoin_red_backlog tool: the topo-sorted list, each item carrying its mirror form (annexed), its anchors_above (NoEmit rungs included) and the @version resolution of its refs. "Inject a cycle" adds a back-edge → the tool REFUSES with BESOIN_CYCLE (never an arbitrary order). Every verdict is computed by the deterministic twin (lib/red-backlog.ts), byte-equivalent to the Go sort.
redBacklog.panelIntro: Set each rung's status, then sort: the RESOLVED MAPPING rungs are topo-sorted along the edges; NoEmit rungs (journey/view) appear in anchors_above but never in the list; a cycle is refused.
redBacklog.backlogHeading: The topo-sorted RedBacklog (the promotion order = the architecture)
redBacklog.cycleRefused: BESOIN_CYCLE — the emitting rungs' edges form a cycle: no total topological order. The backlog is refused (determinism would be lost).
redBacklog.wallNote: Above the wall: the mirror form is ANNEXED, never written; every Idea is a DRAFT candidate — it carries NEITHER a version NOR a mirror (HasMirror always false). The sort writes no kernel and no mirror.
redBacklog.handoffNote: Hand-off S64: the topological order IS the order the /goal are opened in (app-builder); each Idea carries its expected mirror form (LevelMirrorForm) + its anchors.
redBacklog.footer: EL17 — the ordered RedBacklog: RedBacklog(graph) topo-sorts the emitted Ideas (the mapping rungs) along the constrains/seeds edges → the exact promotion order, exactly the §23 verticale. Each Idea carries its anchors_above (including the NoEmit journey/view) and its expected mirror form (LevelMirrorForm, EL10) ANNEXED — never written. A cycle = BESOIN_CYCLE. The sort is a pure algorithm, never an LLM. ABOVE the wall: no kernel/mirror write, HasMirror always false. The TypeScript twin (lib/red-backlog.ts) is byte-equivalent to the Go sort (back/runtime/besoin/red_backlog.go) + the besoin_red_backlog MCP tool.

besoinCapitalisation.title: compound-besoin-capitalisation — capitalise the resolved need
besoinCapitalisation.subtitle: strictly via the wall (firewall.ViaIdea), never ToKernel nor fitness
besoinCapitalisation.intro: EL18 is the capitalisation of the need — /compound applied to elicitation. At a fully-resolved BesoinGraph, it captures (a) the resolved graph as a REUSABLE ANCHOR (graph_hash + canonicalised (level, normalized-intent-hash) keys) and (b) the resolution motif as procedural memory + a candidate besoin-behaviour — STRICTLY via firewall.ViaIdea (idea → mirror → /goal), NEVER ToKernel, NEVER the fitness (declared weights, §8). The capitalised idea's provenance reconstructs down to the graph_hash (carried in the memory's free text). Cross-app reuse is a name-match on canonicalised keys: a similar second need replays its units (ReplayCost), a dissimilar need fabricates NO reuse (the anti-false-positive frontier).
besoinCapitalisation.tutorialHeading: Execute the capitalisation from the screen
besoinCapitalisation.tutorialBody: Enter the verbatim intent of each SOURCE rung of a FIRST resolved need (product + entity by default), then “Capitalise the need” runs anchor() — the besoin_capitalise tool: the reusable anchor (graph_hash + canonicalised keys), the candidate besoin-behaviour (a DRAFT via the wall whose provenance reconstructs to the graph_hash), and the always-false wroteKernel proof. Edit a SECOND need's intents (casing/spacing/punctuation variants = same canonical keys) then “Measure reuse” (reuseFor) — the CE05 name-match: a similar need replays, a dissimilar need reuses nothing. Every verdict is COMPUTED by the deterministic twin (lib/besoin-capitalisation.ts), byte-equivalent to the Go code.
besoinCapitalisation.panelIntro: Enter the resolved need, capitalise it into an anchor + behaviour candidate (via the wall), then measure a second need's reuse under canonicalised keys.
besoinCapitalisation.firstHeading: The first resolved need (the mapping SOURCE rungs)
besoinCapitalisation.secondHeading: The captured anchor (reusable capital, never a truth)
besoinCapitalisation.wallNote: Above the wall: capitalisation STRICTLY via firewall.ViaIdea (idea → mirror → /goal → human approval), NEVER ToKernel, NEVER the fitness. wroteKernel always false; the idea is a DRAFT with no version and no mirror. The provenance reconstructs to the graph_hash.
besoinCapitalisation.notResolved: The need is not fully resolved (every present SOURCE rung must be resolved, ≥1 mapping rung) — it capitalises nothing (EL18's “green” gate).
besoinCapitalisation.reuseHeading: A second need (cross-app reuse under canonicalised keys)
besoinCapitalisation.dissimilarNote: Dissimilar need: NO reuse fabricated (anti-false-positive frontier — capitalisation reuses the shared motif, never the intrinsic content).
besoinCapitalisation.footer: EL18 — capitalising the need: at a fully-resolved BesoinGraph, capture the resolved graph as a reusable anchor + the resolution motif as procedural memory + a candidate besoin-behaviour, STRICTLY via firewall.ViaIdea, NEVER ToKernel nor fitness. The idea's provenance reconstructs to the graph_hash (memory free text). Cross-app reuse = name-match on canonicalised keys (level, normalized-intent-hash): a similar need replays (ReplayCost), a dissimilar need reuses nothing (anti-false-positive). REUSES back/runtime/compound (CE03/CE05) + back/kernel/behavior (CE04 Expand). The TypeScript twin (lib/besoin-capitalisation.ts) is byte-equivalent to the Go code (back/runtime/besoin/capitalisation.go) + the besoin_capitalise MCP tool.

besoinWizard.title: Compound the need — the vertical staircase
besoinWizard.subtitle: explain your app level by level
besoinWizard.intro: EL19 is the wizard tunnel: you EXPLAIN your app rung by rung, in the strict KRD §23 verticale order (product → journey → view → control → action → operation → entity). Step N+1 is LOCKED until CanDescend(N).enough — the EL07 forcing gate made visible: a level that parses but constrains nothing (anti-vacuity) does not unlock the next. The lock READS the pure canDescend verdict (the front never re-implements the gate). Above the wall: the screen PROPOSES Ideas, never writes the Kernel (HasMirror always false).
besoinWizard.tutorialBody: For each level, “Complete this level” fills its body + its 4 metadata → CanDescend recomputes enough → the next step unlocks. “Empty the scenario” (product) shows the anti-gaming: a body that parses but selects nothing stays not_enough and does NOT unlock the rest. The Compounding panel shows the ShrinkOptionSpace integer (EL08) — how much this level narrows the lower rung's option space. At the bottom: “Project to idea-intake” surfaces the real Ideas (topological order, NoEmit excluded); “Open as goals” is REFUSED until the graph is complete (EL09 gate). Every verdict is computed by the deterministic twin, never an LLM.
besoinWizard.intention: Let a customer place an order (checkout)
besoinWizard.lockedNote: Locked — the previous level is not enough yet (EL07 gate).
besoinWizard.metadataIncomplete: Incomplete — declare the four metadata to unlock.
besoinWizard.reuseOpenQuestion: Declared OpenQuestion: cross-app reuse is reliable only under the (level, normalized-intent-hash) normalisation. Until it is live, the reuse history is never shown as acquired.
besoinWizard.openGoalsRefused: Refused — the BesoinGraph is not complete (EL09 completeness gate): a resolved level without its level-mirror is a monster. Complete every rung before opening the goals.
besoinWizard.openGoalsOk: The BesoinGraph is complete — the goals can open in topological order (S64 hand-off).
besoinWizard.ideasHeading: Projected Ideas (the red backlog — PROPOSED, never written)
besoinWizard.wallNote: The wall holds: this screen PROPOSES Ideas via the legal idea-intake door (human provenance), it NEVER writes the Kernel/mirrors/fitness; each Idea carries HasMirror=false. Promotion to truth stays the mirror written via /goal (app-builder).
besoinWizard.footer: EL19 — the Workbench route /compound-besoin: the level-by-level wizard tunnel. REUSES the /first-app wizard shell, drives the deterministic TS twins (byte-equivalent to back/runtime/besoin), emits Ideas via EmitRequirementsDoc. The Idea count EXCLUDES the NoEmit rungs (journey/view). The graph_hash is stable: re-generating produces identical bytes.

EmitRequirementsDoc (lib/besoin-requirements-doc.ts) COMPOSES emitIdeas (EL16), redBacklog (EL17), levelMirrorForm (EL10), levelToProposes (EL05) — re-implements none. projectScope.title: Project scope
projectScope.intro: S54 turns the truth-store from one undivided singleton graph into a multi-tenant one: a project_id (FK) threads through every truth — kernel·mirrors·ideas·changesets·dag·brain·context — and the pre-existing graph (the Order demo) is backfilled, with zero loss (append-only), into a __system__ seed project. Every read is scoped (WHERE project_id = $1): a query for project A never returns a project B row.
projectScope.seedIntro: The content-addressed project that adopts the pre-existing singleton graph. Its id is the SHA-256 of its canonical body (the same scheme as any project, S53) — pinned byte-for-byte in both the migration and the Go code.
projectScope.tablesIntro: The closed set of truth + derived tables that gain a project_id (FK to projects.project) plus an index. The migration is expand-contract and reproducible.
projectScope.buildIntro: Runs the deterministic ScopedSelect builder: it always carries WHERE project_id = $1 (bind $1 to the active project), and refuses a table outside the closed set — never an unscoped query.
projectScope.footer: S54 · below the wall (CLAUDE.md §2): project_id is a scope column, not a write door. The agent keeps SELECT-only on kernel/mirrors; RLS keyed on the propagated identity arrives in S55.

gateway.title: MCP-over-HTTP gateway
gateway.intro: S58 exposes EVERY existing MCP tool (store · mirror-runner · changeset · dag · idea-intake · memory · context · evolve · backtester · telemetry-reader · pact-verifier · mutation-runner · project) behind one project-scoped HTTP/JSON-RPC front door. The wall is applied server-side: a below-the-line call is routed, a cross-project or forged-identity call is refused (AGENT_CROSS_PROJECT_WRITE), a direct truth-write is refused (GATEWAY_TRUTH_WRITE_NEEDS_CHANGESET). Pure routing, zero LLM.
gateway.surfaceIntro: A CLOSED registry: the 13 fronted MCP servers and their tools. The gateway never exposes an arbitrary passthrough — an unknown tool is refused.
gateway.routeHeading: Route a call through the server-side wall
gateway.routeIntro: Executes gateway.route (the same router the live HTTP server applies) over an active scope (identity + project), a tool and a target (project + an optionally-forged identity). The verdict is route, or a refusal with an actionable BlockReason.
gateway.outcomeRoute: Routed: the below-the-line call is dispatched to its server.
gateway.footer: S58 · the wall is unchanged (CLAUDE.md §2): the gateway passes below-the-line ops through and routes truth via a ChangeSet, never a direct write. The router is an algorithm, not a prompt — pure routing, zero LLM.

goalStream.title: Live goal
goalStream.intro: S60 streams the active project's open goal from the gateway (S58) via the typed SDK (S59): the red set — the still-red mirrors that ARE the goal (§56) — the RedWorkQueue (§49.4), and the REAL sensor state. When no gateway is reachable, the panel falls back to the deterministic twin (the Order/discount goal), tagged live/demo. The streamed red set EQUALS the red set the engine computed for this known goal.
goalStream.redSetIntro: The still-red mirrors. The streamed red set is, byte for byte, the red set the engine computes — no re-derivation.
goalStream.queueIntro: One row per red target: the reason and status of the work.
goalStream.sensorsIntro: The real liveness verdict of each red-set mirror.
goalStream.footer: S60 · read-only (CLAUDE.md §2): the screen PROJECTS the open goal and its red set; opening/closing a goal is a truth-write owned by the CLI writer role via propose → ChangeSet. The stream is deterministic — same input → same output.

blocks.title: Refusals (BlockReason)
blocks.intro: S60 surfaces the engine's REAL refusals: every refused write carries an actionable BlockReason (code, severity, explanation, how-to-fix) — KRD §44.5. No code, no prose is coined here: these are the same objects the wall (S55), the gateway (S58) and the goal's non-gameable stop (S29) already pin.
blocks.catalogIntro: The closed, declared codes the engine can raise, grouped by origin.
blocks.tryIntro: Runs a truth-zone tool through the gateway router (the same wall the live server applies, server-side). A direct write (kernel_write / mirror_write / fitness_write) is refused — its real BlockReason surfaces as an inline toast. No truth is written.
blocks.routedUnexpected: Routed (unexpected) — this tool is not a truth-write.
blocks.footer: S60 · the wall is unchanged (CLAUDE.md §2): truth moves only via a ChangeSet (idea → mirror → /goal → approval). The refusal is deterministic — same input → same BlockReason.

auth.title: Authentication & sessions
auth.intro: S61 adds OAuth/OIDC + sessions (Auth.js in the Workbench, JWT verified by the gateway) and the account model (accounts.users: id, email, identity_provider). The resolved identity propagates into EVERY gateway call AND descends to the Postgres RLS (S55) — never gateway-only. Auth lives outside the Kernel.
auth.sessionIntro: Pick an OAuth/OIDC provider and sign in. The gateway verifies the JWT and resolves a verified principal whose identity descends to BOTH walls (gateway scope + the RLS GUC app.identity). A blank subject is refused UNAUTHENTICATED (no anonymous door).
auth.propagationNote: This identity is the ONE value both the gateway (layer 1) AND the Postgres RLS (layer 2, SET LOCAL app.identity) use — a gateway bug cannot widen it.
auth.attemptIntro: Executes a call WITHOUT a valid session to a truth-write endpoint, through the same door the live server applies (auth → scope → zone). It is refused UNAUTHENTICATED UPSTREAM of routing — it reaches NO project data. Its real BlockReason surfaces as an inline toast.
auth.routedUnexpected: Routed (unexpected) — an unauthenticated call should never have passed.
auth.footer: S61 · authentication is never gateway-only (CLAUDE.md §2): the same identity descends to the Postgres RLS (S55). An unauthenticated call is refused UNAUTHENTICATED before any data access. Deterministic — same input → same decision.

projectWall.title: Project-aware wall
projectWall.intro: S55 makes the wall project-aware: the agent reads/writes below the line ONLY for the current project, under its propagated identity (S61). A cross-project op (a project-A scope reaching a project-B row) or a forged gateway identity is refused. Two-layer defense-in-depth: a PreToolUse hook (layer 1) AND a Postgres RLS keyed on identity (layer 2) — which redden independently.
projectWall.layersIntro: The same rule, enforced in two independent places: breaking one never opens the other.
projectWall.layerHookValue: back/runtime/projectwall: a pure, deterministic classifier (an algorithm, not a prompt) that refuses an op outside the active project.
projectWall.layerRlsValue: back/migrations/project_rls_baseline.sql: a row-level policy keyed on (app.project, app.identity); even bypassed at the hook, the agent role sees no row of another project.
projectWall.classifyIntro: Executes projectwall.Classify (the same predicate the RLS enforces) over an active scope (identity + project) and a target (project + an optionally forged identity). The verdict is allow, or deny with an actionable BlockReason.
projectWall.verdictAllow: Allowed: the op is in the current project, under the active identity.
projectWall.footer: S55 · the wall is unchanged (CLAUDE.md §2): RLS governs scope (which project), never the waterline (which zones). The agent keeps SELECT-only on kernel/mirrors. The context router is an algorithm, not a prompt.

projectDag.title: Per-project DAG
projectDag.intro: S56 gives every project its own DAG genesis and its own content-addressed namespace. Branch, checkout, rebranch and merge stay inside the project frontier: a phase cut in A is invisible from B's heads, a cross-project merge is refused (CROSS_PROJECT_MERGE), duplicate forks an isolated root, and archive masks without ever destroying (append-only).
projectDag.codesIntro: The project frontier is a pure predicate (sameProject); crossing it is refused with an actionable BlockReason.
projectDag.branchHeading: Cut a phase inside the frontier
projectDag.branchIntro: Runs branch(from) inside the project. A node from another project is refused (CROSS_PROJECT_NODE): a foreign phase is invisible here.
projectDag.mergeIntro: Runs the frontier guard: a merge between two different projects is refused (CROSS_PROJECT_MERGE) before the merge engine even runs.
projectDag.mergeAllowed: Allowed: both sides are in the same project; the semantic engine (§122) then decides clean/conflict.
projectDag.dupIntro: Runs duplicate: forks an isolated DAG root for a new project. The copy shares no node with the source.
projectDag.dupIsolated: Isolated root: the fork shares no node with the source (disjoint genesis).
projectDag.archIntro: Runs archive: masks the project's version view while keeping all its nodes (append-only). Restore brings the heads back — nothing is ever destroyed.
projectDag.footer: S56 · the Archive is unchanged (CLAUDE.md §2): this panel computes the version-space verdict via the deterministic projectDag twin (byte-identical to Go); recording a node rides the dag MCP under the privileged role, never the screen.

projectMembers.title: Project members
projectMembers.intro: The join (identity × project × role). The third layer of the wall (S55 ⇄ S61 ⇄ S62): authentication proves WHO you are, membership proves you belong to THIS project. A non-member is refused NOT_A_MEMBER; a viewer reads but cannot mutate. Invite / change role / remove — below the wall, append-only, gradient owner ⊃ editor ⊃ viewer.
projectMembers.demoTitle: Postgres unreachable — deterministic demo (oz owner, ed editor, vic viewer).
projectMembers.inviteHint: Bind an identity to the project with a role. Owner-only (the acting identity must be an owner of this project); a non-owner is refused ROLE_FORBIDDEN.

result.badRole: Invalid role — owner, editor or viewer.
result.notAMember: Refused: the acting identity is NOT a member of this project (NOT_A_MEMBER).
result.roleForbidden: Refused: only an owner may administer membership (ROLE_FORBIDDEN).

projectMembers.footer: Below the wall (CLAUDE.md §2): accounts.project_members is not kernel/mirrors/fitness. The S55 RLS keys on membership; the gradient is declared, never learned (§8).

collab.title: Collaboration & adoption
collab.intro: The project's social plane: identified provenance ("who wanted what" with real users), comments on ideas/mirrors/changesets, an activity feed, real-time presence without overwrite, and the adoption ladder (§82.5) surfaced per project. Every act passes the authority gate (S62/S110) and is stamped with the real user — never a placeholder. A member without authority cannot approve. The ladder advances only when the stage gate is reached (done is computed).
collab.approveHint: A member without administer authority (owner) cannot approve — a viewer/editor is refused ROLE_FORBIDDEN.
collab.presenceHint: Two users present on the same canvas see each other without overwrite; the edit lock is never silently stolen.
collab.stageHint: The project surfaces its current stage and the next dent. The ladder advances ONLY when the stage gate is reached.
collab.canAdvanceYes: The gate is reached — the project may advance.
collab.canAdvanceNo: The gate is not reached — no advance (done is computed).
collab.footer: Below the wall (CLAUDE.md §2): comments/shares/invites/feed/presence live in the below-the-line collab zone — never kernel/mirrors/fitness. Approving a truth stays the propose→ChangeSet path (S110/S85). Everything is pure and deterministic (§8).

authorityBinding.title: Authority binding & provenance
authorityBinding.intro: A real user — via their membership role (S62) — is bound to an authority (approver / veto / escalation) PER SCOPE (S16 AuthorityGraph). A truth-write proposal requires approval from a user holding the scope's authority, else INSUFFICIENT_AUTHORITY. Every Idea/ChangeSet records the acting human as provenance — never a placeholder. An override stays a RECORDED decision (ChangeSet + ADR + provenance).
authorityBinding.liveTitle: Deterministic decision — the judge is code (not an LLM).
authorityBinding.demoTitle: Deterministic decision — the judge is code (not an LLM).
authorityBinding.proposeHint: The acting human must hold the scope's authority. Domain checkout: approver product_owner, veto security. Bindings: an owner holds product_owner.
authorityBinding.intentPlaceholder: e.g. I want a checkout discount
authorityBinding.overrideHint: An override is not an edit, it is a RECORDED decision (CLAUDE.md §8): ChangeSet + ADR + real-actor provenance are required.
authorityBinding.footer: Code: back/runtime/authoritybinding (pure, deterministic) + its twin lib/authority-binding.ts. The judge is code, never an LLM (CLAUDE.md §8). The wall holds: the decision neither reads nor writes truth; an override goes through a ChangeSet.

behaviorCapture.eyebrow: Workbench/Build · attach a behavior at capture (S67)
behaviorCapture.title: Behavior at capture
behaviorCapture.subtitle: surface the library, attach a behavior, propose a DRAFT ChangeSet
behaviorCapture.intro: At idea-capture the reusable behaviours library (S79) is surfaced. Attaching a behavior DRY-RUN-EXPANDS it — attributes, relations, operations, policies, fixtures — as a DRAFT proposal, by calling the ONE authoritative Expand of S76 (never a second implementation: a single authoritative code, else a reproducibility hazard). "Don't rewrite the owner-scoping boilerplate for the 50th time" (§24.6). The expansion is a PURE FUNCTION, never an LLM. The screen PROPOSES — it NEVER writes the Kernel (the wall).
behaviorCapture.tutorialBody: Give the captured idea (its ref) and the target entity, pick a behavior from the surfaced library, then attach: AIDOS returns the expansion (byte-identical to S76's) and a DRAFT ChangeSet that PROPOSES freezing it — or a traced refusal (no idea, unknown behavior, missing entity). The attach writes NO truth (the dry-run and the DRAFT propose); freezing goes via the wall: idea → mirror → /goal → human approval (CLAUDE.md §2).
behaviorCapture.attachHeading: Attach a behavior (propose a DRAFT ChangeSet)
behaviorCapture.wallNote: The screen PROPOSES — it never writes the Kernel (the wall).

messages.attachOk: Behavior attached — dry-run expansion + proposed DRAFT ChangeSet (byte-identical to S76; the Kernel is not written).

behaviorCapture.footer: KRD §24.6 · attach at capture · the ONE Expand of S76 (never duplicated) · expansion = pure function, never an LLM · byte-identical to S76 · rendered as a proposed DRAFT ChangeSet · the screen PROPOSES, it NEVER writes the Kernel (the wall).

shapeEditor.title: Shape editor
shapeEditor.subtitle: derive the form, author a red mirror, merge or lock two drafts
shapeEditor.intro: You author a mirror by its FORM, and the form is DERIVED from the nature of the truth — never picked by hand: acceptance N0 → Gherkin, invariant ∀ N1 → property, workflow N2 → fixture (state→cmd→events). The source is PARSED by a pure parser (never an LLM); the mirror is born RED ("watch it fail") and project-scoped, proposed as a DRAFT ChangeSet. Two concurrent edits of the same draft MERGE (disjoint fields) or LOCK (same-field clash) — never a silent last-write-wins (distinct from the truth-write conflict of S110).
shapeEditor.tutorialBody: First derive the form from a nature (the closed table, never a guess). Then author: pick the nature and the reflected layer, type the source in its form, and propose — AIDOS parses the source (a pure function), renders the RED mirror and a DRAFT ChangeSet that PROPOSES to freeze it, or a traced refusal (unknown nature, unparseable source). Finally simulate two authors on the same draft: disjoint fields → merge; same-field clash → lock (both candidates surfaced, never last-write-wins). Nothing writes truth: freezing goes through the wall (propose → ChangeSet → approval, CLAUDE.md §2).
shapeEditor.deriveHeading: Derive the form (closed table, never a guess)
shapeEditor.deriveNote: The form is derived from the nature, never picked by hand.
shapeEditor.authorHeading: Author a red mirror (propose a DRAFT ChangeSet)
shapeEditor.wallNote: The screen PROPOSES — it never writes the mirror (the wall).
shapeEditor.concurrencyBody: Two authors edit the same draft field. Same field + different values → lock (both candidates surfaced); disjoint fields or same value → merge. Never a silent last-write-wins.

messages.deriveOk: Form derived from the nature (closed table).
messages.natureUnknown: Unknown nature — no form is guessed (the honesty of the closed set).
messages.proposeOk: Mirror authored — RED and project-scoped, proposed as a DRAFT ChangeSet (the mirror is not written).
messages.mergeMerged: Edits merged (compatible fields) — the draft version advances.
messages.mergeLocked: Lock: same-field clash — both candidates are surfaced, no write overwrites the other (never last-write-wins).

shapeEditor.footer: KRD §34/§90 · form derived from the nature (closed table, never a guess) · parsing = pure function, never an LLM · mirror born red, project-scoped · proposed DRAFT ChangeSet · draft-level concurrency (lock/CRDT), never last-write-wins · the screen PROPOSES, it NEVER writes the mirror (the wall).

mirrorWatch.title: Materialize-and-watch-it-redden
mirrorWatch.subtitle: the « watch it fail » as a product
mirrorWatch.intro: Trigger materialization of an authored mirror toward its runner (Gherkin → Godog, property → rapid, fixture → the interpreter) and watch the verdict stream live: RED against absent code, GREEN as soon as a stub exists.
mirrorWatch.tutorialBody: Pick the truth-nature, the reflected layer and type the mirror source. The runner is DERIVED from the form (never chosen). Leave « code present » unchecked to watch the mirror redden against absent code; check it to simulate a stub and watch it go green. Materialization and the verdict are PURE functions, never an LLM.
