mirrorWatch.wallNote: The wall: S69 only RUNS the authored mirror — it writes no truth.
mirrorWatch.footer: S69 · the authored mirror above the line is run, never written (propose → ChangeSet → approval, S68/S20).

messages.watchRed: RED — the mirror fails against absent code (the « watch it fail » of KRD).
messages.watchGreen: GREEN — the present stub makes the mirror pass.
messages.materializeRefused: Materialization refused — the source does not parse or the nature is unknown.

mirrorLibrary.title: Mirror library by project
mirrorLibrary.subtitle: project-scoped completeness
mirrorLibrary.intro: Your mirrors listed BY APP with their liveness, plus the completeness law SCOPED to one project: a monster (a truth without a living mirror; an orphan mirror) is hunted WITHIN that project alone. Scope changes the verdict — a cross-project mirror is an orphan within the project.
mirrorLibrary.tutorialBody: Pick a project and run the scoped completeness law. The monster detector sees only the chosen project's cut: a layer with no living mirror is a monster (no_truth_without_mirror); a mirror reflecting a layer absent from the cut (including a layer owned by ANOTHER project) is an orphan (no_orphan_mirror). The detection is a PURE function, never an LLM; project isolation is the RLS wall (S55).
mirrorLibrary.runHeading: Pick a project · run the scoped law
mirrorLibrary.wallNote: The wall: the detection READS a projection and computes a verdict — it writes no truth.
mirrorLibrary.footer: S70 · scope is not cosmetic: it changes the verdict. The detection is read-only (the wall, §2).

messages.monsterFired: MONSTER — the project-scoped detector fired for « {project} ».
messages.complete: COMPLETE — project « {project} » has no monster in its cut.

entityRelation.title: Entity AST relation node
entityRelation.subtitle: 1-1 / 1-N / N-N · fk / association / composition
entityRelation.intro: The entity type system gains a DISTINCT node — a relation — without touching the closed scalar set of S35. A relation references a DECLARED entity, with a cardinality (1-1 / 1-N / N-N) and a semantic (fk / association / composition) from the closed sets. It round-trips as a content-addressed AST; its target is resolved, never guessed.
entityRelation.tutorialBody: Pin a relation (name + target + cardinality + semantic) and resolve it against the declared entity set. A declared target yields the content address (id = Hash(body)) — the content-addressed round-trip. An unknown target is refused UNKNOWN_RELATION_TARGET (never a guessed mapping); an out-of-set cardinality/semantic is refused UNKNOWN_RELATION_KIND. Resolution and hashing are PURE functions, never an LLM; a relation is a SOURCE above the line (the wall, §2).
entityRelation.runHeading: Pin a relation · resolve + content-address it
entityRelation.wallNote: The wall: resolving and hashing writes no truth — a relation is a SOURCE above the line.
entityRelation.footer: S71 · the scalar set stays closed: a relation is its own node, never a scalar. Resolution is read-only (the wall, §2).

messages.resolved: RESOLVED — the relation to “{target}” has a content address (round-trip).
messages.refused: REFUSED — the target is not declared or a kind is outside the closed set.

entityModeler.title: Entity/relation modeler
entityModeler.subtitle: canvas · propose → ChangeSet → approval · draft-level concurrency
entityModeler.intro: Model entities (scalar attributes + identifiers) and their relations (1-1 / 1-N / N-N) on a canvas, then PROPOSE the draft as a project-scoped Kernel source via propose → ChangeSet → approval — never a direct truth-write from the screen (the wall). The modeler produces a `proposed` (DRAFT) ChangeSet. Concurrent canvas editing does not overwrite: two editors see their additions merged (CRDT), neither clobbers the other.
entityModeler.tutorialBody: The canvas pins Customer ◀──1-N── Order. Click “Propose”: the draft is validated (every relation resolves its target in the declared set, else REFUSED — never guessed; an FK requires an identifier on the target), content-addressed (hash invariant to edit order), and a DRAFT ChangeSet is produced (status `proposed`). The entity-map shows the proposed schema. The ChangeSet stays DRAFT: only the `aidos` CLI, after human approval, applies it; a reject leaves the kernel intact. Click “Two editors”: Alice adds Order, Bob adds Invoice concurrently — the merge keeps BOTH (anti-overwrite). Everything is PURE (no LLM); the wall (§2): proposing writes no truth.
entityModeler.wallNote: The wall: proposing writes no truth — the ChangeSet stays DRAFT (only `aidos`, after approval, applies it).
entityModeler.mergeBody: Alice adds Order, Bob adds Invoice — concurrently, on the same canvas. The merge keeps BOTH: neither editor overwrites the other (draft-level concurrency, distinct from S110 truth-writes).
entityModeler.footer: S75 · the modeler produces a `proposed` ChangeSet; truth-writes go through propose → ChangeSet → approval (the wall, §2). Canvas concurrency is handled at the draft level (presence/lock/CRDT).

messages.proposed: PROPOSED — a DRAFT ChangeSet carries the Customer↔Order schema (never applied: the wall).
messages.merged: MERGED — both editors' additions were kept (no overwrite).

behaviorExpander.title: Behavior-macro expander
behaviorExpander.subtitle: the ONE Expand · ownable/versioned/taggable/localizable record · expansion → DRAFT ChangeSet
behaviorExpander.intro: A behavior-macro is a reusable RECORD — ownable (owner), versioned (≥ 1), taggable, localizable (per-locale labels, FR required) — whose Expand(behavior, entity) is the ONE pure authoritative function producing attributes / relations / operations / policies / fixtures. Never an LLM, never re-implemented elsewhere (S67/S79/S80/S81 consume it). The expansion is PROPOSED as a DRAFT ChangeSet — never an applied truth (the wall).
behaviorExpander.tutorialBody: Pick a behavior (ownable / soft-deletable / auditable) and an entity, own/version/tag/localize the record, then “Propose”. The ONE Expand produces the pieces the macro implies (ownable → owner_id + an owner→User relation + the owner-scoping policy + fixtures), content-addressed (same behavior+entity → byte-identical, idempotent expansion). A DRAFT ChangeSet carries the expansion. The wall (§2): proposing writes NO truth — the ChangeSet stays DRAFT; only the `aidos` CLI, after human approval, applies it. Everything is PURE (no LLM, determinism-first §6/§8).
behaviorExpander.proposeHeading: Attach a behavior-macro · propose the expansion (→ DRAFT ChangeSet)
behaviorExpander.wallNote: The wall: proposing writes no truth — the ChangeSet stays DRAFT (only `aidos`, after approval, applies it). WroteKernel = false.
behaviorExpander.footer: S76 · the ONE authoritative Expand (single source); S67/S79/S80/S81 consume it without duplicating it. The expansion is a proposed ChangeSet, never an applied truth (the wall, §2).

dslEditor.title: Typed DSL editors
dslEditor.subtitle: Operation · Policy · Control+Action · typed form (no free code) → DRAFT ChangeSet
dslEditor.intro: The user's domain is edited through TYPED EDITORS — never free code. Operation (validate/authorize/read/mutate/return, incl. S73's async/scheduled), Policy (the ALLOW/DENY tree) and the Control+Action verticale (visible_when/enabled_when/triggers → invoke operation): each edit is a structured form that the parser — a PURE FUNCTION — turns into the existing DSL AST, validates, then PROPOSES as a DRAFT ChangeSet — never an applied truth (the wall).
dslEditor.tutorialBody: Pick a DSL (operation / policy / control / action), fill the pre-seeded typed form (a structured body, never a code string), then « Propose ». The parser — a pure function, never an LLM — decodes each verb / scope / node of the CLOSED grammar (an unknown verb or a code/script/eval field is REFUSED), validates the links (an orphan trigger / bind is a monster) and produces a DRAFT ChangeSet carrying the content-addressed canonical AST. The verticale: an AUTHORIZED control (visible ∧ enabled) triggers its action bound to its operation; enabled_when false BLOCKS the action. The wall (§2): proposing writes NO truth — the ChangeSet stays DRAFT; only the `aidos` CLI, after human approval, applies it.
dslEditor.proposeHeading: Edit a typed DSL · propose (→ DRAFT ChangeSet)
dslEditor.bodyLabel: TYPED body (structured form — no free code)
dslEditor.noFreeCodeNote: No free code: the body is the DSL's TYPED form (verbs, scopes, closed-grammar nodes) — a code/script/eval field is refused (KRD §24).
dslEditor.wallNote: The wall: proposing writes no truth — the ChangeSet stays DRAFT (only `aidos`, after approval, applies it). WroteKernel = false.
dslEditor.footer: S77 · typed editors (no free code) reusing the S09/S10/S11 interpreters. Parsing DSL is a pure function; the edit is a proposed ChangeSet, never an applied truth (the wall, §2).

relationEmitter.title: Relation-aware emitters (+ async + blob)
relationEmitter.subtitle: DDL FK/join · TS typed associations + navigation SDK · worker/outbox
relationEmitter.intro: The EmitDDL/EmitTS/EmitWorker emitters render a MULTI-ENTITY schema — entities + their relations (S71) + their async operations (S73) — to the emitted app's targets (ADR 0040, TS/Hono). An N-N emits a JOIN TABLE; the DDL's FKs reference REAL tables; an async node emits a WORKER + an OUTBOX table. Everything is DETERMINISTIC: same AST → byte-identical output, invariant to input order.
relationEmitter.tutorialBody: The demo schema pins author (1) ──< book (N) ──N-N── tag, plus a cron async op "sendReminder". Pick a target (DDL / TS / Worker) and emit: the DDL creates the tables, an FK column author_id REFERENCES "author"("id") (a real table), a join table "book_tags" for the N-N, and — async schema — an "outbox" table. The TS renders typed associations (author?: Author, tags?: Tag[]) and a navigation SDK (loadBookAuthor / loadBookTags). The worker drains the outbox. Emission is a PURE function (no LLM): re-emitting yields exactly the same bytes (the hash proves it). An undeclared relation target is refused UNKNOWN_RELATION_TARGET — never a guessed FK.
relationEmitter.runHeading: Emit a target · DDL / TS / Worker
relationEmitter.wallNote: The wall: emitting writes no truth — the emitted bytes are a PROJECTION (S78 regenerates), never a kernel write.
relationEmitter.footer: S74 · reproducible emitters: same schema → byte-identical bytes. Emission is read-only (the wall, §2).

messages.refused: REFUSED — malformed schema: a relation target is undeclared, or an FK has no identifier to reference.

truthLevel.title: The 7 truth levels
truthLevel.subtitle: Raw → Reconciled · stored, written by the sole transition · parity mirror
truthLevel.intro: Every truth carries its LEVEL (1 raw → 7 reconciled, FKE-5). It is STORED on the record (queryable, historised) but written ONLY by the deterministic transition — a pure, total function of the idea / changeset / mirror / evidence / consciousness doors — never hand-posed. A parity mirror proves stored == computed: any divergence is RED. "Done is computed" holds: the stored level is a CACHE PROVEN BY THE COMPUTATION, not a second source.
truthLevel.tutorialBody: The ladder has 7 rungs: 1 raw (what was said/pasted/observed), 2 interpreted (an idea exists), 3 proposed (a DRAFT changeset proposes it above the wall), 4 accepted (validated by a human/Governor — changeset APPLIED), 5 projected (emitted code/config/test/doc), 6 observed (tests/logs/metrics/runtime), 7 reconciled (the consciousness concludes after comparison). Pick a level in the filter and run: the panel recomputes each record's level via the transition and shows only those at the chosen rung, each with its parity badge 🟢 (stored == computed) or 🔴 (divergence). The transition is PURE (no LLM): same doors → same rung (the reproducibility mirror proves it).
truthLevel.footer: FK01 · the level is a cache proven by the computation; the transition is read-only (the wall, §2) — it never hand-writes a truth.

record.rec-proposed: DRAFT changeset proposed above the wall

facets.title: The 8 declared facets
facets.subtitle: F/I/S/B/R/V/M/X · collapsible · F always present · X soft
facets.intro: A kernel declares which LENSES it instantiates (functional F · invariants I · security S · budgets B · reliability R · evolvability V · maintainability M · experience X), COLLAPSIBLE: it carries only the facets matching its nature of truth. The FUNCTIONAL facet (F) is always present — the incompressible minimum = intent (s1) + the proof pair (s4↔s5/s6). Validation refuses a kernel with no F, an empty facet, or a declared facet missing its proof pair (a MONSTER — a security hole, a perf regression, a data-losing migration, an unproven invariant are monsters, exactly like a missing functional test). X is the soft truth (§13.6): its missing pair stays advisory (informs, never blocks).
facets.tutorialBody: Eight canonical lenses (the octuor: correct-by-example · true-everywhere · safe · viable · resilient · durable · sound · usable). A pure sort function carries F + I + M; a PII user-facing endpoint carries all eight; a declarative view-kernel carries only F + X. Pick a facet in the filter and run: the panel validates each kernel's facet-set and shows only those instantiating the chosen facet, each with its validity badge 🟢 (legal) or 🔴 (monster) and its content-addressed signature (same facets → same hash, order-independent). Validation is PURE (no LLM): same facets → same verdict (the reproducibility mirror proves it).
facets.octuorHeading: The octuor of the 8 facets (F → X)
facets.footer: FK02 · F is incompressible (intent + proof pair); validation is read-only (the wall, §2) — it writes no truth by hand.

kernel.k-nopair: MONSTER: security declared without its proof pair

grid.title: The level × facet grid
grid.subtitle: coupling verticale (product→entity) × orthogonal facet (F/I/S/B/R/V/M/X)
grid.intro: Every truth carries TWO coordinates (FKE-1.4): the LEVEL — the architectural verticale product→entity, the LATERAL axis that COUPLES (a rung rests on the rungs below it) — and the FACET — the nature of the truth (FK02), the ORTHOGONAL axis that SEPARATES (the eight lenses do not interact). The crossing resolves to a deterministic CELL the ContextRouter exposes. The verticale couples: a change LOW (entity) marks the source rungs ABOVE it (operation, action, control, view, journey, product) stale — the foundation moved, so what stands on it must be re-proven. The facets do not interact: a change on security (S) never touches budget (B).
grid.tutorialBody: Two axes. The VERTICALE descends product → journey → view → control → action → operation → entity (the 7 §23 source rungs): they COUPLE. The FACET is the octet F/I/S/B/R/V/M/X: it SEPARATES. Pick a rung + a facet and run RESOLVE & MARK: the panel resolves the deterministic cell (law 1) + its content address, marks the stale cells above with the FACET HELD CONSTANT (law 2 — the verticale couples, the mark never crosses a facet), and lists the seven OTHER facets left untouched (law 3 — orthogonality). The resolution is PURE (no LLM): same coordinate → same cell, same blast radius (the reproducibility mirror proves it).
grid.verticaleHint: product→entity: a rung rests on the rungs below; a low change marks the rungs above.
grid.facetteHint: F/I/S/B/R/V/M/X: eight independent lenses; a change on one never touches the others.
grid.staleEmpty: Nothing above: this rung is the summit of the verticale (product).
grid.staleNote: The facet is held CONSTANT: the mark walks the rung column, it never crosses a facet.
grid.untouchedNote: The other seven facets are never touched by this change — the facets do not interact.
grid.columnHeading: The chosen facet's column (demo truths, top→bottom)
grid.columnEmpty: No demo truth on this facet.
grid.footer: FK03 · a cell is a COORDINATE the ContextRouter exposes, never a truth posed by hand (the wall, §2). The resolution is read-only and pure.

facetCompleteness.title: Facet-aware completeness
facetCompleteness.subtitle: the generalised monster — a missing pair of ANY instantiated facet
facetCompleteness.intro: The completeness law (S12: "truth ↔ living mirror", over test_kind) extended to the octuor (FKE-1.3 consequence 5). For EVERY facet a layer INSTANTIATES, a LIVING proof pair must exist. A required pair MISSING or DIVERGENT (the mirror is dead / non-executable) on ANY instantiated facet is a MONSTER — a security hole (S), a perf regression (B), a data-losing migration (V), an unproven invariant (I), an unsound architecture (M) — exactly like a missing functional test (F). X (experience) is the sole SOFT exception: its missing pair is ADVISORY (informs, never blocks — §13.6). ADDITIVE: a collapsed legal kernel (F alone, its pair living) PASSES; no existing conformant kernel is invalidated.
facetCompleteness.tutorialBody: The demo cut pins two layers: op-checkout (operation) instantiating F+S+B, and view-cart (view) instantiating F+X. Each instantiated facet DEMANDS a living proof pair. Run the law: with the conformant cut the verdict is COMPLETE. Then FAULT-INJECT — pick a facet to REMOVE (its living pair is dropped) and re-run: the facet loses its pair and a MONSTER appears (op-checkout × S, for instance). The law is PURE (no LLM): same cut → same verdict (the reproducibility mirror proves it). A facet NOT instantiated demands no pair (anti over-constraint §13.4). THE WALL: the screen computes the verdict, it writes no truth — the facet-set is set at the legal FK02 door, never here.
facetCompleteness.cutHint: each facet a layer instantiates demands a living proof pair.
facetCompleteness.faultNote: Remove a pair of an INSTANTIATED facet to see the monster appear (the done-criterion).
facetCompleteness.monstersHeading: Monsters (missing/divergent pair of a hard facet)
facetCompleteness.monstersEmpty: No monster: every instantiated facet has its living pair.
facetCompleteness.monstersNote: One monster per facet: a security hole (S), a perf regression (B), a data-losing migration (V), an unproven invariant (I) — like a missing functional test (F).
facetCompleteness.advisoryHeading: Advisory (soft X — informs, does not block)
facetCompleteness.advisoryNote: X (experience) is soft (§13.6): its missing pair informs the verdict, it never flips it to red.
facetCompleteness.footer: FK04 · completeness checks the pairs of ALL instantiated facets. The screen is read-only and pure (the wall, §2) — it computes, it writes no truth.

proofType.title: The E0-E7 expand
proofType.subtitle: the N→E mapping (pure function) + additive double-labelling + E4/E6/E7
proofType.intro: The N0-N5 → E0-E7 table (KRD FKE-16) declared as a PURE, TOTAL function + ADDITIVE double-labelling (the N preserved verbatim, the E derived ALONGSIDE — "zero existing N mirror modified") + the proof types ADDED to the contract: E4 (security — gosec/gitleaks/evals-injection), E6 (runtime — observation + monitoring + rollback) and E7 (formal). This is the EXPAND step of the E0-E7 migration: compatible with the build-in-progress (E-typing is added to the N-levels, it does not replace them); the dry schema switch is FK16, last. E4 is reached ONLY via the S facet, E6 via R or V, E7 via the formal cap (the rare T2) — never by an ordinary N or facet.
proofType.tutorialBody: The mapping table is CLOSED and declared (never learned, never an LLM, §8): N0/N2/N3 (journey/workflow/contract) → E3, N1 (invariant ∀) → E5, N4 (unit) → E1+E2, N5 (infra) → E3+E4. Tag a kernel: pick its N-level, check the facets it INSTANTIATES (FK02), and — if its invariant is a catastrophic-and-unsampleable formal cap — check the cap. Run the mapping: the E-typed contract appears, the N preserved as-is beside the derived E. An S facet adds E4 (security), R or V add E6 (runtime/rollback), I/B add E5, M adds E1; the X facet (soft, §13.6) adds NO hard E. The mapping is PURE: same input → same contract (the reproducibility mirror proves it). THE WALL: the screen DERIVES the contract, it writes no truth — the N is intact, the schema switch stays with FK16.
proofType.mappingHeading: The N0-N5 → E0-E7 mapping table (closed, declared)
proofType.mappingHint: each N-level inherently requires its set of E evidence (pure function, never learned).
proofType.nLabel: The kernel's N-level (the inherited, preserved label)
proofType.facetsLabel: Instantiated facets (FK02 — each adds its E)
proofType.facetsHint: S adds E4 (security), R/V add E6 (runtime/rollback), I/B add E5, M adds E1; X (soft) adds nothing.
proofType.formalLabel: Formal cap (catastrophic ∧ unsampleable invariant — the rare T2)
proofType.tagNote: The N is PRESERVED verbatim ("zero existing N mirror modified"); the E is derived alongside (the additive double-label). The contract is PURE — no LLM.
proofType.preservedNote: the N is preserved verbatim — additive, never modified.

proofType.fromFacetsHeading: E added by the facets (E4/E6/E5/E1 — the types FK05 adds)
