proofType.requiredNote: the required contract is the UNION of the base mapping, the facet-added E and E7 (iff formal cap), sorted and deduplicated. The ADDED E (E4/E6/E7) are highlighted.
proofType.footer: FK05 · the N→E mapping is a pure, total function; the double-label is additive (zero N mirror modified). The screen is read-only and pure (the wall, §2) — it derives, it writes no truth.

honoEmitter.title: Hono/TS server scaffold + Pulumi emitter
honoEmitter.subtitle: bootable server · /healthz · sync handlers · async worker · Pulumi/TS program
honoEmitter.intro: EmitServer renders a BOOTABLE Hono/TS service (main + router + middleware + GET /healthz + one POST handler per SYNC operation, delegating to the Go interpreter callback, ADR 0040 Déc.7) wired on ALL the Kernel operations; EmitWorker renders the async worker (S73/S74, drains the outbox); EmitPulumiProgram renders the infra Pulumi/TS program (ADR 0043: one docker.Container per service on the shared Traefik network). Everything is DETERMINISTIC: same Kernel → byte-identical bytes + FN02-pure Pulumi program.
honoEmitter.tutorialBody: The demo Kernel pins two sync operations (createOrder, cancelOrder) and one async (sendReceipt, notification), and a StackManifest (server + Go interpreter sidecar + Postgres + Valkey). Emit the server: GET /healthz answers { status: "ok" }, and each sync op becomes a POST /createorder route delegating to deps.interpret (the Go interpreter) — no business rule reimplemented. Emit the worker: it drains the outbox and dispatches typed effects. Emit the Pulumi program: a shared docker.Network, one docker.Container per service, Traefik labels on the server. Emission is a PURE function (no LLM): re-emitting yields exactly the same bytes (the hash proves it). A malformed source is refused — never a guessed route/service.
honoEmitter.serverHeading: Emit the Hono/TS server · server / worker
honoEmitter.wallNote: The wall: emitting writes no truth — the emitted bytes are a PROJECTION (S78 regenerates), never a kernel write.
honoEmitter.footer: S87 · reproducible emitters: same Kernel → byte-identical bytes. Emission is read-only (the wall, §2).

appRegenerator.title: Regenerate my app
appRegenerator.subtitle: project-scoped re-emit · byte-stable · refuses a hand-edit
appRegenerator.intro: A Runtime action, bound to the user's Kernel cut, that re-emits the WHOLE project app — entities + relations + operations (sync AND async) + controls + blobs — toward its emission target in ONE deterministic pass. It classifies what changes (STALE by source-hash / FRESH / UNCHANGED) and REFUSES if any generated file was hand-edited (GEN_FILE_HAND_EDITED). Reused by preview/deploy (E10).
appRegenerator.tutorialBody: Regeneration COMPOSES the S74 deterministic emitters (never a second emitter) over the whole demo project, then (1) first checks that no emitted on-disk file diverges from its recorded output_hash — a drift is a hand-edit, refused fail-closed before any write (§9 non-destruction); (2) re-emits byte-stable; (3) classifies each file stale (the source moved) / fresh (never emitted) / unchanged. Pick « faithful tree » to see the Plan, or « one hand-edited file » to see the GEN_FILE_HAND_EDITED refusal. Regenerating writes NO truth — gen/ is a regenerable projection, never hand-edited.
appRegenerator.scenarioLabel: State of the emitted on-disk tree
appRegenerator.wallNote: The wall: regenerating writes NO truth — gen/ is a PROJECTION. The source changes only via idea → mirror → /goal.
appRegenerator.footer: S78 · reproducible regeneration: same project → byte-identical artifacts. A hand-edited generated file is refused (the wall, §2/§9).

blobAttribute.title: Blob/file type of the Entity AST
blobAttribute.subtitle: upload · signed URLs · MIME + size · project_id-scoped
blobAttribute.intro: The entity type system gains a third DISTINCT node — a blob/file (an upload: image/document/file) — without touching the closed scalar set of S35 nor the relation node of S71. A blob round-trips as a content-addressed AST and emits a DETERMINISTIC upload/download handler (signed URLs). The bytes live in PER-PROJECT object storage (project_id-scoped), never in the truth-store nor git.
blobAttribute.tutorialBody: The blob node “avatar” declares a CLOSED MIME allow-list (image/png, image/jpeg) and a size ceiling. Pin an upload (MIME + size) and validate it: a conforming upload mints the project_id-SCOPED storage key (projA/User/avatar/…), proves cross-project isolation (A reaches it, B is refused BLOB_CROSS_PROJECT) and emits the deterministic handler. An out-of-MIME upload is refused BLOB_MIME_REFUSED; over-size, BLOB_SIZE_REFUSED — never truncated nor coerced. Validation, scoping and emission are PURE, never an LLM; a blob is a SOURCE above the line (the wall, §2).
blobAttribute.declaredHeading: Declared blob node (closed MIME list + ceiling)
blobAttribute.runHeading: Pin an upload · validate + scope + emit it
blobAttribute.wallNote: The wall: validate, scope and emit writes no truth — the bytes never enter the truth-store nor git.
blobAttribute.footer: S72 · the scalar set stays closed: a blob is its own node, never a scalar. Validation is read-only (the wall, §2); the bytes live in per-project object storage (provider ADR, replaceable slot).

messages.accepted: ACCEPTED — the upload conforms: scoped key minted, cross-project isolation proven, deterministic handler emitted.

asyncOperation.title: Async / scheduled operation + outbox
asyncOperation.subtitle: cron · queue · webhook_out · notification · exactly-once relative
asyncOperation.intro: The Operation DSL (S10) gains a THIRD dimension — an async/scheduled node (cron / queue / webhook_out / notification) — without touching the six sync verbs. A scheduled operation fires at its echeance (a tick over an INJECTED clock) and emits its events; its effects flow through the transactional OUTBOX — written in the same transaction as the state change, then dispatched exactly-once relative. The scheduler is code, never an LLM.
asyncOperation.tutorialBody: The « sendReminder » operation declares a cron trigger (an RFC3339 echeance) and a notification effect. Pin an INJECTED clock instant and run: before the echeance nothing fires; at/after it the operation fires exactly once. The panel then drives the outbox crash → replay path: the effect is written PENDING, the dispatcher delivers it once (at-least-once: a write-then-crash never loses the effect), then the at-least-once redelivery re-presents the same content-addressed id → SUPPRESSED. The observable delivery count stays exactly 1 (exactly-once relative). The tick and dispatch are PURE, never an LLM; an async operation is a SOURCE above the line (the wall, §2).
asyncOperation.runHeading: Pin an injected clock · tick + dispatch the outbox
asyncOperation.wallNote: The wall: ticking, scheduling and dispatching writes no truth — the outbox is a runtime datastore table.
asyncOperation.exactlyOnceNote: Exactly-once relative: at-least-once (the effect is never lost) + idempotent dispatch (the replay is suppressed) ⇒ no observable duplicate.
asyncOperation.footer: S73 · the trigger set stays closed { cron, queue, webhook_out, notification }, never invented. The tick/dispatch is read-only (the wall, §2); the scheduler is code, never an LLM (DP16, ADR 0043: Windmill/NATS substrate).

messages.fired: FIRED — the scheduled operation runs at this echeance; the effect flows through the outbox, dispatched exactly-once relative.
messages.notFired: NOT YET — the injected clock is before the echeance; no operation fires (deterministic scheduling).

behaviors.title: Behavior library
behaviors.subtitle: project-scoped · consumes S76's Expand
behaviors.intro: The user-facing library of your reusable behaviours, scoped per project: browse, search (deterministic rg-like match, never an LLM), tag, attach, soft-delete, publish, comment. Attaching previews the expansion (its scoped policies+fixtures) by calling S76's ONE Expand, and lands it via an APPROVED ChangeSet — never a direct kernel write (the wall).
behaviors.tutorialBody: Search a behaviour (by owner, tag or label): the match is a deterministic substring search, never an LLM. Then attach owner-scoping to an entity: the screen previews the scoped policies+fixtures the expansion implies and lands them via an APPROVED (APPLIED) ChangeSet, the only legal door to truth.
behaviors.attachIntro: Attach owner-scoping (the §24.6 behaviour) to an entity: preview the scoped policies+fixtures via S76's ONE Expand, then land via an approved ChangeSet.
behaviors.wallNote: The wall: attaching writes no truth — the expansion lands as an APPLIED ChangeSet VALUE (propose → approve door), never a direct kernel write. Only the aidos CLI freezes the source via /goal.
behaviors.footer: S79 · The library consumes S76's ONE Expand — never a second expansion (single-function law, §24.6).

appAuth.title: app-auth behavior-macro
appAuth.subtitle: auth of the app YOU build · not the AIDOS users
appAuth.intro: The application you build has ITS OWN users: login, roles, runtime authorization — distinct from the auth of AIDOS' own users. Attach the app-auth behavior-macro to your app: it expands deterministically into entities (User/Role/Session), operations (login/logout) and role-based authz policies, mapping the AuthorityGraph of the EMITTED app's RUNTIME — never the AIDOS approvers.
appAuth.checkIntro: Simulate the emitted app's authorization gate: may a role invoke a protected operation? The decision is a deterministic lookup over the declared role→operation band, never an LLM. A protected operation refuses an insufficient role at runtime.
appAuth.allowed: ALLOWED — the role meets the required minimum.
appAuth.denied: DENIED — insufficient role for this protected operation.
appAuth.attachIntro: Attach the app-auth subsystem to your app: preview the auth entities+operations+policies (byte-identical, deterministic) and land it via an approved ChangeSet — the legal door (propose → approve), never a direct kernel write.

templates.title: Template catalogue
templates.subtitle: content-addressed bundles · deterministic & green instantiation
templates.intro: Don't start from a blank page. Curated templates (e-commerce, CRM, booking) are packaged as content-addressed bundles: entities + relations + behaviors (incl. app-auth) + mirrors + operations + UI sources. Instantiating a template produces a DETERMINISTIC, GREEN starting project (green Kernel, mirrors present, no monster); "fork this app" duplicates a project at a stable phase.
templates.instantiateIntro: Pick a template and a target slug: instantiation materialises the app skeleton (entities/relations/operations/mirrors/UI) and expands app-auth via the ONE S80 function. Deterministic — same (template, slug) ⇒ same content-addressed starter. No kernel write (the wall).
templates.forkHeading: Fork this app (at a stable phase)
templates.forkIntro: Fork a starter to a new slug from a content-addressed stable phase: a deterministic copy. Same phase ⇒ same starter; a different phase ⇒ a different starter. No kernel write.
templates.forkedHeading: App forked from a stable phase

workspace.title: Per-project sandbox
workspace.lede: An isolated workspace (container + git/jj repo + worktree + CPU/mem/disk/time limits) per project where the generated code lives, compiles and runs its mirrors. The ADR 0001 zones (/ideas /spike /src /kernel/spec) are realized as REAL runtime workspaces, never directories of this repo. Project A's sandbox cannot read project B's tree/build nor the truth-store (SANDBOX_ESCAPE); a runaway is killed by the resource limit (SANDBOX_RESOURCE_LIMIT).

provision.title: Provision a workspace
provision.desc: Name a project: its isolated workspace is provisioned (ADR 0001 zones, private git/jj worktree, declared caps) and a confined hello-world builds+tests green inside. No kernel write (the wall).

access.title: Cross-project isolation (SANDBOX_ESCAPE)
access.desc: May a project's workspace read/write a path? A path under ANOTHER project or under the truth-store is refused with SANDBOX_ESCAPE (default-deny).
access.allowed: Access allowed (confined to the workspace root)

resource.title: Resource limit (SANDBOX_RESOURCE_LIMIT)
resource.desc: Anti noisy-neighbor: a sampled load vs the declared caps. A runaway (CPU/mem/disk/time over a positive cap) is KILLED.

buildConsole.title: Build console
buildConsole.subtitle: live + per-turn cost meter
buildConsole.intro: The deterministic, read-only aggregation of everything a human watches while a build runs: the diff streamed per attempt, the sensor results, the HarnessCostBudget consumption (CI minutes, LLM tokens/goal), the circuit-breaker state, the AgentRun timeline and the human approval gate. The streamed state EQUALS the recorded AgentRun.
buildConsole.tutorialBody: Op 1 — project the console state from the recorded AgentRun (id, goal, result, writes), the iteration history, the loop verdict, the consumed budget and the pending approvals: AIDOS computes the streamed state and PROVES it equals the AgentRun (the console cannot fabricate a turn). Op 2 — record a per-project stable phase: a green §43 records a DAG node, an inconsistent cut is REFUSED.
buildConsole.footer: S86 — the console is a FAITHFUL PROJECTION (never an LLM judgment). Both ops are read/compute below the line — they write no truth; the DAG node is recorded by the aidos role inside a ChangeSet (the wall, §2).

project.heading: Project the build state
project.body: From the recorded AgentRun + history + decision + cost + pending approvals, compute the streamed state — and check it EQUALS the recorded AgentRun.
project.runIdHint: the recorded AgentRun id (S52) the console projects
project.writesHint: one per line: "diffHash | ok" (ok = authorised below the line)
project.diffHashesHint: one diff hash per line (the loop history)
project.pendingHint: one proposal id per line (S85 BuildInbox)
project.faithfulOk: FAITHFUL projection: the streamed state EQUALS the recorded AgentRun.
project.faithfulKo: UNFAITHFUL projection: the state drifts from the recorded AgentRun (refused).

stable.heading: Record a stable phase (per project)
stable.body: From the project's §43 cut (heads / links / sensors), compute the S23/S40 verdict and record the DAG node when STABLE; an inconsistent cut is REFUSED (no node from a red mirror).
stable.projectIdHint: the slug of the project whose DAG frontier receives the node (S56)
stable.label: Label
stable.labelHint: the human line name of the recorded phase
stable.linksHint: one link per line: "fromId@v1 -> toId@v3" (off-head ⇒ stale)
stable.sensorsHint: one sensor per line: "id | ok" (a red one makes the cut unstable)
stable.recorded: STABLE — the S23/S40 verdict passes; a DAG node is recordable (§43).
stable.refused: UNSTABLE — the cut is NOT coherent; NO node is recorded.

messages.runIdEmpty: The AgentRun id is required to project the state.
messages.projectIdEmpty: The project is required to record a stable phase.

doltgresSpike.title: Doltgres go/no-go spike
doltgresSpike.subtitle: plain-Postgres default · Doltgres opt-in
doltgresSpike.intro: The spike submits N concurrent connections to Doltgres and MEASURES stability + perf ratio. The verdict is a PURE function of the measurement against declared thresholds — a count and two comparisons, never an LLM. plain-Postgres stays the default by construction; Doltgres is opt-in iff go.
doltgresSpike.tutorialBody: Supply a measurement (driver, N connections, failed connections, perf ratio, reproducible) and click Decide. The verdict is computed against the declared thresholds; a REPRODUCIBLE failure flips to no-go, a non-reproducible blip does not. The Decision is content-addressed: same measurement → same id. Judging writes no truth (the wall).

provision.title: Per-app datastore provisioning
provision.subtitle: plain-Postgres default · Doltgres opt-in · per-project isolation
provision.intro: The provisioner PLANS the emitted app's datastore: plain-Postgres by default (+ a pgvector sidecar if needed), Doltgres opt-in iff the S88 verdict is go, the SAME Atlas emitter for the DDL, per-project isolation, and an expand-contract migration human-gated via DataTruthScope. The plan is a PURE function of the spec — a membership check + a hash + the existing emitter, never an LLM. Emitted as a Pulumi resource (DP15).
provision.tutorialBody: Pick a target (plain-Postgres default / Doltgres opt-in), toggle vector search and/or a historical-impact migration with/without a declared DataTruthScope, then click Provision. A Doltgres target with no S88 go decision is REFUSED (the gate); a historical-impact migration without a declared scope is REFUSED (human-gate). The Plan is content-addressed: same spec → same id. Planning writes no truth (the wall).
provision.fieldNeedsVector: The app needs vector search (pgvector sidecar)
provision.fieldHistorical: The change touches data already produced (historical impact)
provision.blockedBody: A Doltgres target requires an S88 go verdict; a historical-impact migration requires a declared DataTruthScope. The gate refuses, it never bypasses.

apiSurface.title: Complete emitted API surface
apiSurface.subtitle: CRUD + operation routing · per-app OpenAPI · one Pact per operation
apiSurface.intro: The emitter PROJECTS the emitted app's API surface: the CRUD + operation routing (sync), the per-app OpenAPI 3.1 (byte-stable from the Kernel), and ONE Pact contract per operation (generalising the single createOrder.pact.json), with provider-verification across ALL endpoints. The Hono/TS handlers delegate to the Operation-DSL interpreter via a CALLBACK to the Go sidecar interpreter service (ADR 0040 Dec.7); the policy is enforced (a DENY → HTTP 403). Emission is a PURE function of the spec — never an LLM.
apiSurface.tutorialBody: Toggle whether the createOrder operation AUTHORIZES (a policy) and whether a read-only listOrders endpoint joins the surface, then click "Emit + verify". The screen shows the per-app OpenAPI, the Hono/TS router (delegating to the Go sidecar), the Pact suite (one contract per operation) and the provider-verification verdict across all endpoints. A policy DENY is enforced at runtime (HTTP 403). Emitting writes no truth (the wall).
apiSurface.authorizeLabel: createOrder authorizes (a policy; a DENY → HTTP 403)

frontEmitter.title: The emitted app's front-end
frontEmitter.subtitle: pages/forms over entities+relations+blobs · control+action verticale as real buttons · Hono JSX/SSR
frontEmitter.intro: The emitter PROJECTS the built app's front-end: the navigation index, one create-form per entity (one input per scalar, an <input type=file> per blob, a <select> per relation), and the control+action verticale rendered to REAL buttons — each carrying its control-spec fixture as a SENSOR (data-aidos-fixture) and bound to its operation (data-aidos-invoke). Target: Hono JSX/SSR, server-rendered (OQ-0040-front decided: no client SPA over hc). Inherits the ccup theme (ADR 0010) + bilingual i18n (ADR 0011), wired to the emitted API (S90). Emission is a PURE function of the Kernel — never an LLM; same Kernel → byte-identical bundle.
frontEmitter.tutorialBody: Toggle whether the order entity carries its blob upload (receipt) and its relation (customer), then click "Emit the front". The screen shows the byte-identical bundle (with its digest), the emitted form source (the blob → <input type=file>, the relation → <select>), and the verticale buttons — each carrying its control-spec fixture. Below, a REAL create-form submits an operation against the datastore (blob upload included): the generated form is executable, not read-only. Emitting writes no truth (the wall); the submission writes to a below-the-line datastore.
frontEmitter.withBlobLabel: The order entity carries a blob upload (receipt — image/png, application/pdf)
frontEmitter.withRelationLabel: The order entity carries a relation (customer — foreign key)
frontEmitter.liveFormHeading: Generated form — submit a real operation

preview.title: Per-app ephemeral preview
preview.subtitle: emitted server+datastore+UI · phase-keyed URL · `pulumi up`/`pulumi destroy` · Hono Node/Bun/edge
preview.intro: For the active stable phase (content-addressed), preview computes a DETERMINISTIC preview plan: a phase-keyed URL, the `pulumi up` that boots the emitted app (a Hono Node/Bun/edge process — ADR 0040, NEVER a Go binary), the `pulumi destroy` that tears it down deterministically, and the phase's emitted-app hash. The done-criterion: the preview's served-app hash EQUALS the phase's emitted-app hash (judged by CODE, never an agent); clicking an emitted button executes the bound operation against the datastore. The plan is PURE and content-addressed: same emitted surface → byte-identical plan, same URL. ADR 0043 / DP25.
preview.tutorialBody: Give the project and the content-addressed phase hash, then click “Build the preview”. The screen shows the phase-keyed preview URL, the emitted-app hash, the `pulumi up` (boot) and `pulumi destroy` (deterministic teardown) commands, and the PROBE badge: served-app hash == emitted-app hash (the done-criterion). Toggle “re-emit the surface” to observe that a new surface → a new hash + a new URL (content-addressing is observable). Below, a REAL form served by the preview submits an operation against the datastore (blob upload included): clicking the emitted button executes the bound operation. Planning writes no truth (the wall); the submission writes to a below-the-line datastore.
preview.mutatedLabel: Re-emit the surface (a new hash → a new URL)
preview.matchOk: The served hash equals the phase's emitted hash
preview.matchFail: The served hash does NOT match — stale preview
preview.liveFormHeading: App served by the preview — submit a real operation

dataMigrate.title: Migrating the emitted app's data
dataMigrate.subtitle: deployed app + real rows · expand-contract + backfill · DataTruthScope-gated · driver-neutral
dataMigrate.intro: On a DEPLOYED app carrying REAL ROWS, a BREAKING schema change (column rename, entity split, 1-N→N-N cardinality) migrates the data via Atlas expand-contract + backfill — each step forward-only, non-destructive until contract. Distinct from the truth-store migration. The gate is the DataTruthScope (§44.3): a breaking change with NO declared backfill is REFUSED (BREAKING_MIGRATION_NO_BACKFILL), never a silent DROP. The breaking-ness is COMPUTED (structural diff × scope), never an LLM judgment. The plan is PURE and content-addressed: same change → byte-identical plan. Gates S96 (deploy migrates).
dataMigrate.tutorialBody: Pick the deployed project, the breaking-change kind (rename / split / cardinality) and fill its body. Toggle 'declared backfill' to observe the gate: with a backfill, the plan stages EXPAND → BACKFILL → CONTRACT (the backfill recopies/ventilates/fills the join table from the real rows — nothing lost); with no backfill, the plan is REFUSED with BREAKING_MIGRATION_NO_BACKFILL. The 'preserves all data' badge is COMPUTED (every contract preceded by a backfill). Planning writes no truth (the wall); the migration is driver-neutral (emitted SQL + content address).

deploy.title: Deploy this phase
deploy.subtitle: stable phase ONLY · re-projection (S78) · forward-only migration (S95) · `pulumi up` · URL provisioning
deploy.intro: The « Deploy this phase » action is permitted ONLY from a STABLE phase (« done is computed »: red→green ∧ prior green intact ∧ mutation ≥ threshold ∧ no monster). The deploy RE-EMITS the app from the phase (S78, deterministic) — never a stale sandbox artifact — then runs a FORWARD-ONLY data migration (expand → backfill → contract, S95) and provisions a URL via `pulumi up` (ADR 0043). Deploy = re-projection, never procedural (DP26). The Stop-gate is INHERITED: a non-stable phase is REFUSED with PHASE_NOT_STABLE, naming the reasons (the red mirror, the below-threshold mutation score, the present monster). The plan is PURE and content-addressed: same stable phase + surface → byte-identical plan, same URL.
deploy.tutorialBody: Give the project and the phase hash, then click « Deploy this phase ». The screen shows the per-phase deploy URL, the hash of the app RE-EMITTED from the phase, the `pulumi up` (boot) and `pulumi destroy` (teardown) commands, the PROBE badge (the served hash == the emitted hash — the re-projection, judged by CODE), and the FORWARD-ONLY migration staged as expand → backfill → contract. Toggle « non-stable phase » to observe the PHASE_NOT_STABLE refusal (deploy is keyed on stable phases ONLY). Toggle « migration » to stage the migration lifecycle. Planning WRITES NO truth (the wall); recording the deploy as a DAG decision goes through propose → ChangeSet → approval.
deploy.unstableLabel: Deploy a NON-STABLE phase (a red mirror → PHASE_NOT_STABLE refusal)
deploy.appHashLabel: App hash re-emitted from the phase
deploy.probeHeading: Probe — served hash ≟ emitted hash (re-projection, never a stale artifact)
deploy.matchOk: The served hash equals the phase's re-emitted hash
deploy.matchFail: The served hash does NOT match — stale sandbox artifact

domainBind.title: Custom domains + TLS for the deployed app
domainBind.subtitle: one domain, one project
domainBind.intro: Once the stable phase is deployed (S96), the app is served on a deterministic deploy subdomain. Here you bind a CUSTOM DOMAIN on top — like the Workbench behind Traefik, but for the emitted apps. AIDOS computes a DETERMINISTIC bind plan: the HTTPS URL, the Traefik labels (websecure router + TLS + ACME certresolver) and the DNS instruction (a CNAME to the deploy host). A domain belongs to EXACTLY ONE project (the binding is injective).
domainBind.tutorialBody: Enter the project and the custom domain, then « Bind the domain ». AIDOS emits the Traefik labels that serve the app over HTTPS (automatic ACME certificate) and the CNAME to set at your registrar. Tick « domain already bound to another project » to prove the DOMAIN_ALREADY_BOUND refusal (a domain serves only one app). THE WALL: planning writes no truth.
domainBind.conflictLabel: Domain already bound to another project (proves DOMAIN_ALREADY_BOUND)

envRollback.title: Environments + rollback by re-projection
envRollback.subtitle: preview → staging → prod
envRollback.intro: Promote a STABLE phase into an environment (preview → staging → prod), then roll back to an earlier phase: rollback DETERMINISTICALLY RE-EMITS the app from the earlier DAG phase (S78) — it NEVER restores a stale sandbox artifact (CLAUDE.md §9). The decision is provenanced (who/what/why), append-only; nothing is deleted. The wall: a rollback does not write the kernel — the screen proposes the decision as a ChangeSet.
envRollback.tutorialBody: PROMOTE binds a stable phase to an environment (a non-stable phase is refused ENV_PROMOTE_NOT_STABLE). ROLLBACK returns to an EARLIER, DISTINCT, STABLE phase (else ROLLBACK_NOT_EARLIER): the env then serves a FRESH re-emit of N-1, never the stale artifact of N. Code judges the re-projected equality, never an LLM.
envRollback.promoteRedToggle: Promote a NON-STABLE phase (proves the ENV_PROMOTE_NOT_STABLE refusal)
envRollback.rollbackSameToggle: Target the SERVED phase (proves the ROLLBACK_NOT_EARLIER refusal)
envRollback.rollbackNoAncestorToggle: Target a NON-ANCESTOR phase (proves the ROLLBACK_NOT_EARLIER refusal)
envRollback.reProjectedLabel: App re-emitted from N-1 (served after rollback)
envRollback.servesFresh: prod serves the FRESH re-emit of N-1 (judged by code)
envRollback.rejectsStale: the stale artifact of N is REJECTED (nothing restored as stale)

cellFederation.title: Cells: the large app as a federation of bounded contexts
cellFederation.subtitle: one Kernel per cell, one ratchet per cell
cellFederation.intro: A large app is NEVER one indivisible Kernel (KRD §43–§51): it is a deliberate federation of small cells (bounded contexts), each with its OWN Kernel and its OWN ratchet, linked ONLY by contracts (S17 contracts_with). The agent in cell X loads its own Kernel + ONLY the public CONTRACTS of its contracted neighbors — never a neighbor's internals (§145). Greatness lives in the NUMBER of cells, never the size of one. The wall: the Context-Map persists via ChangeSet (S101), never a direct write.
cellFederation.tutorialBody: PARTITION splits a project's Kernel into sub-Kernels by bounded_context (a node with no cell is refused). COMPILE a cell's PACK returns ONLY its own Kernel + its contracted neighbors' PUBLIC contracts — neighbor internals are excluded (done-criterion 1). CHECK a cross-cell access without a honored contract is REFUSED (CROSS_CELL_NO_CONTRACT — done-criterion 2). A cell SHIPS if it is locally stable (green ratchet), independent of the others (§43 fractal). The code judges, never an LLM.
cellFederation.openQuestion: Open question E11 (resolved here): a cell is a FIRST-RANK partition concept reusing the bounded_context already carried by every node — NOT a sixth TruthScope dimension (S15). TruthScope qualifies where/when/for-whom ONE truth holds; a cell is the partition the truth LIVES in.
cellFederation.scenarioBody: checkout ⇄ billing (honored contract). checkout ✗ catalog (no contract). billing is RED, checkout & catalog are GREEN.
cellFederation.neighborContractsLabel: Contracted neighbors' PUBLIC contracts (the only thing that crosses)
cellFederation.noNeighborInternalLabel: no neighbor internal leaked into the pack
cellFederation.accessAllowed: access allowed (own cell or contracted neighbor)

contextMap.title: Context-Map: the only true human work
contextMap.subtitle: consumer/provider contract pairs verified by Pact
contextMap.intro: The Context-Map is the ONLY true human work (KRD §46): you DESIGN which cells exist and how they talk (event storming, aggregates, ACL, contract pairs). Cells connect ONLY via versioned contracts_with links verified by Pact. A pair is HONORED iff the provider publishes a SUPERSET of the consumer's expectation (matching method/path, every required field, status). A cross-cell call that VIOLATES the contract is REFUSED (CROSS_CELL_NO_CONTRACT). Architecture is designed, never generated. The wall: the Context-Map persists as Kernel truth via a DRAFT ChangeSet (propose → ChangeSet → approval), never a direct write from the screen.
contextMap.tutorialBody: VERIFY A PAIR applies the pact-verifier semantics to one consumer/provider pair: HONORED iff the provider publishes a superset of what the consumer expects (done-criterion 1). VERIFY ALL designed pairs at once. CHECK A CALL across cells: a call that violates the contract (an unhonored or absent pair) is REFUSED CROSS_CELL_NO_CONTRACT (done-criterion 2); the refusal names the fix path. PROPOSE persists the Context-Map as a DRAFT ChangeSet — the only legal way to write Kernel truth (the wall). The code judges (field set + status assertion), never an LLM.
contextMap.scenarioBody: checkout CONSUMES billing: billing publishes POST /charges {amount, orderId, status} ⊇ the expectation → HONORED. checkout CONSUMES catalog: catalog publishes only GET /items {sku}, the price field is missing → UNHONORED, and the checkout → catalog call is REFUSED.
contextMap.callAllowed: call allowed (own cell or honored pair)
contextMap.wallNote: The wall: this is a DRAFT — the Context-Map only becomes Kernel truth after a human approves the ChangeSet. The screen never writes truth directly.

archFitness.title: Structural ratchet: hold or improve
archFitness.subtitle: arch-fitness over the inter-cell dependency graph (§47)
archFitness.intro: The SECOND ratchet (KRD §47). Where the behavioural ratchet (S05) protects behaviour (a green mirror never goes red), this one protects ARCHITECTURE: four 'lower-is-better' metrics over the inter-cell dependency graph — boundary violations, inter-cell cycles, inter-BC edges, max cell complexity — can only HOLD or IMPROVE between two cuts. A new boundary violation OR a new inter-cell cycle REDDENS the structural ratchet and BLOCKS THE CUT, INDEPENDENT of green behavioural mirrors. It prevents 'green tests, rotten system' (go-arch-lint/depguard AIDOS side, dependency-cruiser emitted side — the same structural judgment, in pure code). The wall: the structural baseline moves via a DRAFT ChangeSet (propose → ChangeSet → approval).
archFitness.tutorialBody: MEASURE computes the four arch-fitness metrics of the clean cut (each metric is a graph algorithm — Tarjan SCC for cycles, edge dedup, max — never an LLM). RATCHET compares candidate ↔ baseline, component-wise: HELD iff every metric is non-increasing. THE GATE injects a fault (a new uncontracted inter-cell dependency, or a cycle): the ratchet REDDENS (BROKEN) and blocks the cut, even if every behavioural mirror is green. PROPOSE moves the structural baseline as a DRAFT ChangeSet — the only legal way (the wall).
archFitness.scenarioBody: The CLEAN cut: checkout depends on billing across the HONORED contract — no violation, no cycle. THE GATE injects a fault: 'violation' adds an uncontracted checkout → catalog edge (catalog has no honored pair); 'cycle' adds billing → checkout, closing a cycle with checkout → billing. Each fault reddens the ratchet.
archFitness.heldBody: Every metric is non-increasing: the cut may proceed.
archFitness.wallNote: The wall: this is a DRAFT — the structural baseline only moves after a human approves the ChangeSet. The screen never writes truth directly.

secretStore.title: Per-project secret store
secretStore.subtitle: encrypted at rest · scoped to project_id · boot env injection · rotation
secretStore.intro: The store holds the emitted app's secrets — DB credentials, third-party API keys, OAuth secrets — encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM), scoped to the project_id, NEVER in the truth-store, never in git, never in the emitted source. Injection via boot-time env vars; rotation invalidates the old secret; a secret missing at boot raises an actionable, fail-closed BlockReason. The leak scan is deterministic CODE (gitleaks-style), never an LLM.
secretStore.tutorialBody: Set a secret (SET), rotate it (the prior value is invalidated), inject the boot environment from a DECLARED key list (a missing key → the fail-closed BlockReason), and scan an emission for leaked secrets (deterministic gitleaks-style scan). The screen NEVER shows a value: only the stored key names and the boot env var names (values masked). A secret is operational material, never a truth (the wall).

opsObservability.title: Ops observability
opsObservability.subtitle: OpenTelemetry · one ops panel per app · writes no truth
opsObservability.intro: Once running, the emitted app must be OPERATED day to day: see its logs, its request traces, its errors, and a latency + error-rate dashboard. OpenTelemetry (JS/TS) instrumentation; signals feed a PER-APP ops panel (one panel per project). DISTINCT from "telemetry as a Kernel sensor" (E12): ops observability writes NO truth — the RealityMirror is the only Kernel on-ramp.
opsObservability.emitTitle: Emit an OTel signal (the emitted app)
opsObservability.seeded: Demo set loaded (spans + error log + logged secret).
opsObservability.built: Ops dashboard built — no truth written.

federation.title: Composing federation invariants
federation.subtitle: §51 · global red wave
federation.intro: Wires S48 GlobalInvariant / S49 SagaInvariant / S50 TemporalInvariant onto REAL multiple cells (S100). The red wave deploys globally; each cell reconciles locally.
federation.tutorialBody: Run the saga over the two real cells order + payment (tick "break a leg" to trigger compensation). Then fire the global policy "all PII forgettable" expressed ONCE: it fans out to a RedWorkQueue per cell — order and payment redden, shipping (unaffected) stays GREEN.
federation.sagaBody: The saga payment_captured ⇒ order_confirmed ∨ compensation holds over two contracted cells. The happy path is satisfied; breaking a leg (payment captured, order never confirmed) triggers the declared compensation (refundPayment), after which the saga is satisfied VIA compensation.
federation.fanOutBody: A global policy "all PII forgettable" expressed ONCE over the federation fans out to a RedWorkQueue per cell: order and payment (which violate the policy) each get their own queue; shipping (which does not violate) stays GREEN.
federation.footer: THE WALL (§2): composing WRITES NO truth — the RedWorkQueue rows are a projection (the S22 hook does the INSERT below the waterline). Deterministic (§6/§8): same input → same output, no LLM.

federationCockpit.title: Federation cockpit: the cell graph at a glance
federationCockpit.subtitle: §50 · two ratchets · red wave
federationCockpit.intro: The only true dashboard of greatness (§50): the cell federation seen at a glance — the graph, the inter-cell contracts, the status of BOTH ratchets (S100 behavioural per cell + S102 structural over the cut), local vs global stability, and the red-wave fan-out. Executable: assemble the cockpit, fire the transverse red wave, watch one cell ship its green local cut while a neighbor is still red.
federationCockpit.tutorialBody: Assemble the cockpit over the two real cells order + payment (one honored contract). Tick « fire the red wave »: a global policy expressed ONCE reddens ONLY payment — order shows a green local cut and SHIPS while payment is still RED (the §43 fractal). Tick « break the structure »: a regressed cut (a new un-contracted inter-cell edge) flips the SECOND ratchet to BROKEN — the federation is no longer globally stable, even with green cells.
federationCockpit.assembleBody: Composes cell.Partition (per-cell behavioural ratchet) + arch-fitness (structural ratchet) + the red-wave fan-out into ONE snapshot: each cell with BOTH ratchets, the contracts, the cells that ship now, and whether the federation is globally stable.
federationCockpit.fireWaveLabel: Fire the transverse red wave (reddens payment)
federationCockpit.breakStructureLabel: Break the structure (an un-contracted inter-cell edge)
federationCockpit.cellGraphHeading: Cell graph · both ratchets per cell
federationCockpit.footer: THE WALL (§2): the cockpit COMPOSES + RENDERS — it WRITES NO truth; the structural baseline moves via a ChangeSet (S102), the per-cell INSERT is the S22 hook's job below the waterline. Deterministic (§6/§8): same input → byte-identical snapshot, no LLM.

realityIngest.title: Reality loop: production becomes a sensor
realityIngest.subtitle: E12 · divergence → RealityMirror → draft idea
realityIngest.intro: The DEPLOYED app's production emits OpenTelemetry to the telemetry-reader; a divergence from a mirror's promise (e.g. 30% of createOrder fails on out-of-stock — a case no fixture covered) becomes a project-scoped RealityMirror record (provenance=incident) → a draft idea. The idea text is a DETERMINISTIC TEMPLATE projection, never an LLM summary; only the later human grilling is judgment.
realityIngest.tutorialBody: Ingest the divergence: the out-of-stock telemetry report (createOrder fails 30% over 1000 calls) is compared (deterministically) against the mirror promise "createOrder-succeeds" (0 errors tolerated). The divergence becomes a project-scoped RealityMirror (provenance=incident) and a draft idea whose text is TEMPLATE-rendered — it names the mirror, the operation, observed vs expected, the traffic. Toggle "healthy report": a within-promise report → NO divergence, NO idea (reality never invents a truth). THE WALL: reality NEVER writes truth directly.
realityIngest.ingestBody: Compares the production telemetry report against the mirror's promise (deterministic comparison, never an LLM); a divergence becomes a project-scoped RealityMirror (provenance=incident) → a draft idea whose text is a deterministic template projection. WroteKernel=false; the direct Reality→Kernel edge is always refused.
realityIngest.healthyLabel: Healthy report (within the mirror's promise → no idea)
realityIngest.noIdea: Production is within the mirror's promise: no divergence, no idea invented. Reality never declares a truth from a healthy app.
realityIngest.ideaHeading: The draft idea · deterministic template text
realityIngest.ideaTemplateNote: The text is a TEMPLATE projection over the divergence record (same record → byte-identical text), never an LLM summary.
realityIngest.nextStep: Next step: the human grills this idea (S107/S65), then /goal decides — idea → mirror → /goal → approval.
realityIngest.footer: THE WALL (§2): reality WRITES NO truth — the draft is a value (wroteKernel=false; the direct Reality→Kernel edge is always refused, REALITY_CANNOT_DECLARE_TRUTH). Deterministic (§6/§8): detection AND rédaction = code, same input → same output, no LLM.

projectEvolve.title: Medium loop: /evolve + QD from a fixed mirror
projectEvolve.subtitle: E12 · variants → cull → Pareto niches → gated promotion
projectEvolve.intro: From a FIXED user mirror, the EvolutionSandbox searches for a BETTER IMPLEMENTATION of an already-frozen truth — never a new truth. The deterministic mirror + property test KILL the variants that break the truth; the Pareto élites (fast/cheap/simple) survive in project-scoped QD niches; promotion requires authority (∧ out-of-sample green). The Judge is the mirror, never an LLM. Evolution explores, it does not govern.
projectEvolve.breakMirrorLabel: Break variant v-broken's mirror (mirror=red) → it is killed, never an élite, whatever its score (anti-Goodhart).
projectEvolve.grantAuthorityLabel: Grant authority approval (else a green élite is not promotable).
projectEvolve.nichesHeading: The QD niches (the surviving Pareto élites)
projectEvolve.killedNote: The deterministic mirror kills any variant that breaks the fixed truth — whatever its backtest score. The score never overrides the mirror.

truthApproval.title: Truth approval: propose → ChangeSet → gated approval, no last-write-wins
truthApproval.subtitle: E3 · AuthorityGraph (S63) + ChangeSet (S20) + content-addressed optimistic lock
truthApproval.intro: Every truth-write through the cockpit goes propose → ChangeSet → approval, gated by the bound AuthorityGraph (approver / veto / escalation, S63) at the right TruthScope. A veto dominates; missing approval blocks; partial approval escalates; all approvers admit. Concurrency is governed by a CONTENT-ADDRESSED optimistic lock on the head: two concurrent applies → the SECOND is refused (STALE_HEAD), NEVER last-write-wins (anti-overwrite §9). An override is a RECORDED decision (provenance + ADR, §8), never a silent bypass. Everything is deterministic: the judge is the gate + the content-addressed head, never an LLM; the cockpit writes NO truth.
truthApproval.gateHeading: 1. The authority gate (S63) — veto, approval, recorded override
truthApproval.gateBody: A member proposes a truth-write ({domain}/{kind}). The gate decides: a veto (legal) blocks regardless of approvers; no approval blocks; partial approval escalates. An override of a block requires full provenance (actor + reason + ADR) — otherwise refused (no silent bypass). THE WALL: the cockpit writes NO truth; it decides admission and returns the envelope the CLI would apply.
truthApproval.outcomeApplied: APPLIED — the tooth landed, the head moved
truthApproval.concurrencyBody: Two members propose concurrently onto the SAME head. The FIRST admitted+fresh apply moves the head (the new tooth); the SECOND references the OLD head → refused STALE_HEAD, never last-write-wins. The stale member re-runs their mirrors against the new head (merge-semantic decides, S25) and re-applies. Exactly ONE write lands.
truthApproval.relandHeading: 3. The conflict resolved by re-running the mirrors (S25)
truthApproval.reland: Re-run & re-apply against the new head
truthApproval.noTruthWrite: the cockpit writes no truth (propose → ChangeSet → approval)

costMeter.title: Harness economics: a per-cell budget wired to real AgentRun counters
costMeter.subtitle: E13 · HarnessCostBudget (S51) + AgentRun (S52) → circuit-breaker (S83)
costMeter.intro: Each cell DECLARES its HarnessCostBudget (max_ci_minutes / max_llm_tokens_per_goal / max_mutation_runtime / max_human_review_minutes / expected_risk_reduction) above the line (read-only fitness zone). The meter AGGREGATES the consumption of the cell's REAL recorded AgentRuns — a COUNT, never an estimate — and compares it to the cap. A costly constraint WITHOUT a justified ValueCase is FLAGGED (advisory), never silently blocked: « the more a constraint costs, the more it must justify its value ». The over-budget signal feeds the circuit-breaker (S83). Everything is deterministic: the judge is economics.Evaluate, never an LLM; the cockpit WRITES NO truth.
costMeter.budgetHeading: The declared budget (read-only, above the line)
costMeter.runsHeading: 1. The cell's real AgentRuns (S52) — the counted metering
costMeter.runsBody: Each recorded AgentRun carries its real consumption (tokens, CI minutes). The meter SUMS those counters — exactly, never an estimate. Add the heavy run to push the sum over the declared cap.
costMeter.includeHeavy: Include the heavy run (Order.heavy: +40000 tokens → exceeds the cap)
costMeter.verdictHeading: 2. The §66.3 verdict — advisory, never a silent block
costMeter.valueCaseLabel: Attach a justified ValueCase (the costly cell earned its keep)
costMeter.disjoncteurHeading: 3. The circuit-breaker (S83) — the cost cut-off signal
costMeter.disjoncteurBody: The metered verdict projects onto the circuit-breaker signal: it TRIPS if and only if the cell is over budget WITHOUT a justified ValueCase. A within-budget — or justified — cell never trips the breaker. This is the named S111→S83 wire: the build-loop composes it (OR no-progress).
costMeter.noTruthWrite: the cockpit writes no truth (the budget is DECLARED, read-only)

kernelGarden.title: Garden the kernel debt: surface the five rots, propose without deleting anything
kernelGarden.subtitle: §82.4 · composes KernelDebt (S41) + §66.3 economy (S51) + cost meter (S111)
kernelGarden.intro: Per-project KernelDebt gardening. It surfaces the FIVE rots of a project's slice — orphan mirror, stale fixture, surviving mutant (consumed from S41), DEAD LIVENESS (a mirror declared dead still pinning a live truth) and LOW-VALUE CONSTRAINT (a cell over its HarnessCostBudget without a justified ValueCase, consumed from S51). /trim PROPOSES reductions — it DELETES NOTHING: accepting a proposal OPENS an idea → mirror → /goal → human approval (the only door). The scan is project-scoped: project A never sees project B's debt. Everything is deterministic: the judge is code, never an LLM; the cockpit writes NO truth.
kernelGarden.tendHeading: 1. Garden a project — the debt ledger, project-scoped (§82.4)
kernelGarden.tendBody: Pick a project and garden its slice of the truth-store. The scan is PROJECT-SCOPED: it surfaces ONLY that project's debt (project A never sees project B's). The ledger lists the five rots, ranked by severity.
kernelGarden.cleanGarden: Clean garden: no debt in this project (no false positive).
kernelGarden.suggestOnly: /trim PROPOSES only — it deletes nothing. Accepting a proposal OPENS an idea → mirror → /goal → human approval (the only door, never a direct removal).
kernelGarden.acceptHeading: Proposal accepted → an idea opens (never a deletion)

realityEvolution.title: Reality & evolution cockpit: incident → learned mirror → red wave
realityEvolution.subtitle: E12 · composes S106 ingest + S107 /learn + S108 QD
realityEvolution.intro: The per-project COCKPIT that composes the three already-built engines into ONE screen: telemetry→RealityMirror→draft-idea ingestion (S106), the /learn approval gate that closes the external loop (S107), and the per-project QD elites archive (S108). The canonical journey, executable from the screen: INGEST an incident → APPROVE the learned mirror → SEE the red wave APPEAR. Everything is deterministic: the judge is the mirror, never an LLM; the cockpit writes NO truth.
realityEvolution.loopHeading: 1. The external loop: ingest → approve → red wave
realityEvolution.loopBody: The canonical §S109 journey, one click: ingest the out-of-stock divergence (createOrder fails 30%, S106); the human approved at /goal the NEW mirror 'out-of-stock-during-checkout' (S107), the cockpit attaches it → the createOrder hash BUMPS → a TARGETED red wave (mirror-first) APPEARS — the worklist. Tick 'healthy report': prod within promise → NO divergence, nothing learned. THE WALL: the cockpit writes NO truth.
realityEvolution.healthyLabel: Healthy report (within promise → no divergence, nothing learned)
realityEvolution.closeLoop: Ingest the incident & close the loop
realityEvolution.noIdea: Prod is within the mirror's promise: no divergence, no idea invented, nothing learned. Reality never declares a truth from a healthy app.
realityEvolution.step1Heading: Step 1 · the ingested incident (S106) — RealityMirror + draft idea (template)
realityEvolution.step2Heading: Step 2 · the approved mirror bumps the hash (S107)
realityEvolution.notMoved: the hash did not move (cosmetic re-reflection)
realityEvolution.step3Heading: Step 3 · the RED WAVE APPEARED (the §S109 done-criterion)
realityEvolution.waveNote: The bump triggers a targeted red wave (mirror-first): the mechanical worklist. 'facts change' resolved.
realityEvolution.waveAppeared: red wave appeared — {n} target(s) in the worklist
realityEvolution.waveEmpty: no red wave (a cosmetic re-reflection is not a new tooth)
realityEvolution.elitesBody: The project-scoped QD niches: one GREEN élite per niche (fast/cheap/simple) of an ALREADY-frozen truth. The mirror-breaker is NEVER an élite, whatever its score (anti-Goodhart). Grant authority then promote: a PROPOSAL (writesTruth=false) with authority, refused without. The AI proposes, the human freezes at /goal.

learn.title: /learn: the incident becomes a new mirror and a new tooth
learn.subtitle: E12 · approved mirror → hash bump → red wave
learn.intro: A RealityMirror (draft idea, provenance=incident, S106) re-enters idea→grill→goal; on HUMAN APPROVAL a NEW mirror (e.g. out-of-stock-during-checkout) is attached to the operation/policy, its content address (the hash) CHANGES mechanically, and a TARGETED red wave (mirror-first) becomes the worklist — 'facts change' resolved mechanically. The loop does NOT author the mirror: the human does at /goal — nothing learns its own fitness.
learn.tutorialBody: Close the loop: on the createOrder out-of-stock incident, attach the approved mirror 'out-of-stock-during-checkout'. The createOrder operation's hash BUMPS (before ≠ after), and a targeted red wave (mirror-first) becomes the worklist. Check 're-reflect': re-attaching an ALREADY-reflected mirror → NO bump, an EMPTY wave (a cosmetic re-reflection is not a new tooth). THE WALL: the loop writes NO truth, and the direct Reality→Kernel edge is always refused.
learn.closeBody: Attaches the human-approved mirror to its operation/policy; the content hash changes (PURE records.Hash, never an LLM) and a targeted red wave (mirror-first) becomes the worklist. WroteKernel=false; the human authors the mirror at /goal — nothing learns its own fitness.
learn.reReflectLabel: Re-reflect (mirror already attached → no bump, empty wave)
learn.close: Close the loop (attach mirror → red wave)
learn.bumpHeading: The hash bump (the operation/policy address changed)
learn.bumpNote: Attaching a new mirror re-canonicalises and re-hashes the target's body (records.Hash/Canonicalize, REUSED) — same target + same mirror → byte-identical (before, after) pair; after ≠ before IFF the reflection actually changes the body.
learn.waveHeading: The targeted red wave · the worklist
learn.waveNote: The bump seeds exactly the target's red wave (redwave.Impact, REUSED), ordered mirror-first (§42/§98): the mirror reddens first, then the projections.
learn.waveEmpty: No bump → no tooth → empty wave (no work).
learn.nextStep: The worklist (the red wave) is what the build loop drains next, tooth by tooth — each item turns red→green.
learn.footer: THE WALL (§2): the loop writes NO truth — the outcome is a value (wroteKernel=false; the direct Reality→Kernel edge always refused, REALITY_CANNOT_DECLARE_TRUTH). Deterministic (§6/§8): the hash bump AND the red wave = pure functions, same input → same output, no LLM; the world teaches, never the agent itself.

strangler.title: Strangler-fig: freeze the legacy, refactor safely
strangler.subtitle: §50 · characterization tests
strangler.intro: Carve a cell around the legacy, FREEZE it with auto-generated characterization mirrors over its current behaviour (input→output, bug-for-bug), publish its contract, then let the build-loop refactor INSIDE the frozen cell — nothing the legacy did is silently lost.
strangler.tutorialBody: Start a strangler cell: the "billing" cell is carved around the legacy and its three observed traces are FROZEN into characterization mirrors. Then run a refactor inside the frozen cell: a refactor that preserves behaviour and honors the contract is ACCEPTED; tick "break behaviour" to see a drift REFUSED (STRANGLER_CHARACTERIZATION_DRIFT) or "break contract" to see a broken contract REFUSED.
strangler.carveBody: A cell is carved around the "billing" legacy and its current behaviour is FROZEN: one characterization mirror per observed trace (input→output), tagged "characterization" so it is never confused with an intent mirror. This is the green net a refactor must keep green.
strangler.refactorBody: The build-loop refactors inside the frozen cell. A refactor that preserves behaviour (same output for each frozen input) and honors the published contract is ACCEPTED. Tick "break behaviour" to change an observable output (drift) or "break contract" to break the published contract — both are REFUSED with their BlockReason.
strangler.footer: THE WALL (§2): carve/freeze/refactor WRITE NO truth — the strangler cell and its characterization mirrors are a value (the ChangeSet proposes them above the line). Deterministic (§6/§8): mirror generation is code, never an LLM; same input → same output.

accountRelease.title: Account Release v0 — the honest inventory
accountRelease.intro: The per-ACCOUNT release pack enumerates HONESTLY what EXISTS in your live truth-store: your projects (with their demo-vs-real status), the completed CLI surface (goal/grill/spike/harvest/trim/init on top of the core verbs), Workbench routes, the docs index, the test inventory, the changelog, and the honest known-limits (Doltgres beta, async best-effort, plan quotas) — then advises the next adoption tier. Content-addressed, read-only: it assembles and advises; it installs nothing, ships nothing, writes no truth.
accountRelease.tutorialStep1: Pick a demo account, then click “Assemble the pack”.
accountRelease.tutorialStep2: Each project carries its HONEST status: real (a working app) or demo (a runnable slice).
accountRelease.tutorialStep3: The CLI surface lists the 5 core verbs + the 6 gateway verbs (S117), each routed over the passerelle.
accountRelease.tutorialStep4: The next adoption tier is COMPUTED (the smallest ratchet that clicks) — advised, never installed.
accountRelease.allGreenBadge: Every tier is satisfied — nothing more to install.
accountRelease.assembleOnlyNote: Assemble-only: this pack installs nothing, ships nothing, writes no truth (the wall, §2). Turning on a capability goes through idea → mirror → /goal → human approval.
accountRelease.scenarioKernel: Kernel+mirror account (blocked at T2: RealityMirror missing)

deriveDoc.title: The deterministic derivation of s9
deriveDoc.subtitle: DeriveDoc(kernel) → s9
deriveDoc.intro: The pure emitter DeriveDoc(kernel) → s9 derives the LOWER half of the doc-mirror from the kernel ASTs (operations, controls, routes/bindings, test names, errors). s9 is structured — lexicon concepts, behaviors, errors — for the structural comparison FK07 runs against s2 (the human-authored upper half). Same kernel → byte-identical s9: the doc is a COMPUTATION, never an LLM. The wall: the screen derives the doc, it writes no truth.
deriveDoc.tutorialBody: Pick a kernel and click DERIVE S9. The emitter projects its ASTs into three sorted sections — the lexicon concepts (operation:/control:/action:/entity:/event:/policy:), the behaviors (one per operation, one per control→action→operation binding, one per emitted event) and the error surface. The canonical bytes shown are identical on every run (the badge proves it). This is the lower half FK07 will compare, set by set, to the human-written doc.
deriveDoc.footer: FK06 — FKE-1.3 decision (a). s9 is a deterministic projection: regenerable, never a truth (the wall, CLAUDE.md §2).

docMirror.title: The doc-mirror: structural comparison s2↔s9
docMirror.subtitle: Compare(s2, s9)
docMirror.intro: The STRUCTURAL set-comparison of the human-authored doc (s2, the upper half) against the code-derived doc (s9, the lower half, FK06): concepts, behaviors and errors present or absent. A STRUCTURAL divergence is BLOCKING (red); PROSE is ADVISORY (the LLM signals, never arbitrates — §8 “the judge is a computation”). Same pair → same verdict. The wall: the screen compares, it writes no truth.
docMirror.tutorialBody: Pick a scenario and click COMPARE. The engine takes the concepts/behaviors/errors sets of both sides and computes the symmetric difference. “aligned”: s2 describes the code exactly → GREEN. “behavior removed from code”: the code no longer emits the event but s2 still documents it → RED (code_missing). “prose only edited”: a behavior's text is rewritten without touching its structure → GREEN, with an advisory. Prose NEVER blocks — only the structural plane judges.
docMirror.structuralEmpty: No structural divergence — both halves align.
docMirror.footer: FK07 — FKE-1.3 decision (a). The judge is a computation (§8): structural blocks, prose informs. The report is a projection, never a truth (the wall, CLAUDE.md §2).

facetWire.title: Wire the S/R/V/M/X facets
facetWire.subtitle: WireSkeleton
facetWire.intro: The five non-functional facets — Security (S), Reliability (R), Evolvability (V), Maintainability (M), Experience (X) — wired as PARALLEL COLUMNS of the same six-pair skeleton (FKE-1.3), each reusing an existing sensor. The judge is the same STRUCTURAL set-comparison as the doc-mirror (§8): a declared-not-proven pair reddens its column. The facets are ORTHOGONAL — breaking a pair reddens ITS column and no other. X is SOFT (§13.6): its divergences inform, they never click the ratchet hard. The wall: the screen wires, it writes no truth.
facetWire.tutorialBody: Pick a scenario and click WIRE. Each non-functional facet carries its 6 pairs (spec → behaviour → scenarios → model → contract → evidence) and a reused sensor. 'all aligned': every declared pair is proven → GREEN. 'break S/R': a pair of a hard column is no longer proven → that column REDDENS, the others stay green (orthogonality), the overall verdict turns red. 'break X': the same break on Experience stays GREEN with an advisory — X informs, never blocks. The judge is a computation.
facetWire.footer: FK08 — FKE-1.3 (the six facet tables). Each facet reuses an existing sensor; X stays advisory (§13.6). The report is a projection, never a truth (the wall, CLAUDE.md §2).

conscience.title: Consciousness
conscience.subtitle: Reconcile
conscience.intro: Consciousness is a DETERMINISTIC AGGREGATOR (FKE-6.3): a pure function composing the verdicts of the EXISTING judges — the mirror runner, completeness/monster, the S/R/V/M/X facets, SemanticDiff, the RealityMirror, the sensors, the ledger — into one report per kernel + the §FKE-31 decision cards. NO new judge: an active evaluator-organ would be 'the second agent that validates', which the Tome refuses as proof (§8). It READS sourced verdicts and ROUTES them; every line carries the judge that produced it. The overall verdict turns to DRIFT as soon as a HARD pair is red; the soft facet X never flips it (§13.6). The wall: the screen reconciles, it writes no truth.
conscience.tutorialBody: Pick a scenario and click RECONCILE. The consciousness composes the sourced verdicts into reconciled pairs (each carries its judge, facet, verdict) and produces one decision card per divergence. 'all aligned': no card. 'runner drift': the s2↔s9 pair diverges → its decision card (options · recommendation · blast radius). 'break S': the Security column reddens → a block card, the kernel drifts. 'break X': the same break on Experience stays ALIGNED with an advisory card — X informs, never blocks. The judge is a computation; same input → same report.
conscience.noCards: No divergence — no decision card (kernel aligned).
conscience.footer: FK09 — FKE-6.3. Consciousness is a deterministic aggregator; no new judge. The report contains only sourced verdicts; acting on a card goes idea → mirror → /goal → human decision (the wall, CLAUDE.md §2).

autonomy.title: Autonomy A0-A8
autonomy.subtitle: autonomy_level
autonomy.intro: Autonomy is the 6th axis of the agent layer (FKE-11/34): a CLOSED level autonomy_level ∈ A0..A8 DECLARED by the CoucheAgent. Enforcement is FAIL-CLOSED: an action whose required level exceeds the declared level is refused with the AGENT_AUTONOMY_EXCEEDED BlockReason. A8 is NEVER allowed on a critical action (a merge, a deploy, an irreversible truth write). A one-rung PROMOTION is COMPUTED from the AgentRun history (N green E4+ runs without incident), never declared by the agent. The wall: the screen enforces and computes, it writes no truth.
autonomy.tutorialBody: Two controls, two pure functions. ENFORCE: pick an action and its required level; the screen compares required ≤ declared. An A1 agent attempting a merge (which requires A6) is REFUSED — the AGENT_AUTONOMY_EXCEEDED BlockReason names the door out (earn the promotion from history, freeze the level via /goal). A8 on a critical action is always refused. COMPUTE PROMOTION: pick a run history. Three green E4+ runs without incident promote A1→A2; a single incident, a below-E4 run, or a non-green run in the window WITHHOLDS the promotion. The level is COMPUTED from the record, never declared; same history → same level.
autonomy.promoteHeading: Compute promotion (pure function of the history)
autonomy.promoted: promotion earned (current+1) — proposed, to be frozen via /goal
autonomy.withheld: promotion withheld — the history does not earn it
autonomy.footer: FK10 — FKE-11/34. Autonomy is a declared, closed axis; enforcement is fail-closed and promotion is a pure function of the history, never declared. A8 never on a critical action. The wall (§2): the screen enforces and computes, it writes no truth — freezing a promotion goes idea → mirror → /goal → approval.

aiLab.title: AI Lab
aiLab.subtitle: the spec generator (chat → 6×6 → machines)
aiLab.intro: The AI Lab is a two-pane spec generator. On the LEFT, a natural-language chat: what you write generates the specs above the wall, across the 6 mirror-pairs of the chosen facet (a column of the 6×6 grid). On the RIGHT, the 6×6 grid (6 pairs × facets): each cell shows the generated spec (above the wall) and its machine — the executable mirror/test (below) — with the conscience voyant 🟢/🔴/🟡. “The machines it changes” = exactly these mirrors. The wall holds: the chat proposes; promotion to truth goes through /goal.
aiLab.tutorialBody: Pick a facet (the column), write in natural language, then “Generate specs”. Specs appear above the wall in that column (the amber strip at the top of each cell); below, the machine (the mirror) takes its voyant: 🟢 aligned, 🔴 diverges, 🟡 declared but not yet proven. A direct truth-write request (“write the kernel”) is refused at the wall.
aiLab.leftHelp: Describe a need in natural language. The left brain (Claude) fans it out and places the specs where they belong — it decides the level(s), facet(s) and pair(s). It proposes; promotion to truth goes through /goal.
aiLab.chatPlaceholder: “when the cart expires after 30 min, notify the user and release the stock…”
aiLab.proposedSlot: Proposed slot (a candidate, not a truth)
aiLab.wallRefused: Refused at the wall (§2) — the chat never writes truth
aiLab.wallNote: The wall runs through the middle of each cell: above, the spec the chat generated (proposed); below, the machine (mirror/test), read-only. The only promotion to truth is a decision → /goal.
aiLab.noCards: No decision card — everything is aligned.
aiLab.openedGoal: Above-the-wall option → a /goal is opened (idea → mirror → /goal). No truth written from the cockpit.
aiLab.replyGreeting: Hi 👋 Describe in natural language what you want — I generate the specs above the wall, across the 6 mirror-pairs of the chosen facet, and you watch the machines (on the right) react. The chat proposes; promotion to truth goes through a /goal.
aiLab.replyRefused: I can’t write truth from the chat — that’s the wall (§2). I propose, I don’t decide: promotion goes idea → mirror → /goal. Rephrase as intent and I’ll generate the specs.
aiLab.replyGenerated: I posted {n} spec(s) above the wall for the {facet} facet (the 6 mirror-pairs). {divergent, plural, =0 {Their machines turn green 🟢.} one {# machine still diverges 🔴 — the conscience computed it; refine its pair to realign it.} other {# machines still diverge 🔴 — the conscience computed it; refine their pairs to realign them.}}
aiLab.placementsHeading: What the intelligence generates and impacts
aiLab.replyFallback: (deterministic mode — Claude unavailable) I placed {placed} specs at the operation level, Functional facet. Wire Claude for the real multi-level fan-out.

aiLab.selectCellHint: Click a cell of the table above to open its anatomy (the 6 pairs) and validate the descent.

aiLab.reqHint: Each requirement = a feature, with its niveau × facette grid. Click one: its sum (Σ per level/facet) + its links + its specs.
